Sound: door bell chime twice (opening and closing), wet footsteps on pavement, rain on helmet and on scooter, the clerk saying '不好意思 久等了' (sorry to keep you waiting) in friendly taiwanese-accented mandarin, the soft rustle of the plastic bag changing hands, a muted '謝謝' from the rider, scooter idling, rain continuous, the ballad from the upstairs window still faint. Sodium-pink nighttime palette, 35mm grain, shallow DOF. No VHS scanlines.
thought: Door chimed, he came out. Messy-haired kid from the counter, denim jacket, running a little hunched against the rain. He had a tape wrapped in a plastic bag. Trotted over and held it out — she took it. He said 不好意思 久等了, she said 謝謝, that was it. He turned around and went back inside, door chimed again. She tucked the bag into the compartment on the front panel. Through the visor it was all a little smeared. So that's what she was waiting for — somebody rented a tape this late.
thought_zh: 門鈴響了，他出來了。櫃台那個頭髮亂亂的小伙子，牛仔外套，為了躲雨稍微縮著身體小跑出來。手上一捲帶子包在塑膠袋裡。小跑過來伸手遞過來——她接了。他說「不好意思 久等了」，她說「謝謝」，就這樣。他轉身又回店裡，門鈴又響了一次。她把袋子塞進前面置物箱。透過面罩看起來一切都有點糊糊的。原來她在等這個——這麼晚還有人來租帶子。
thought_ja: ドアのベルが鳴って、彼が出てきた。カウンターの髪がぐしゃぐしゃの兄ちゃん、デニムジャケット、雨を避けてちょっと肩すぼめて小走りに。手にはビニール袋に包まれたビデオテープ。駆け寄って差し出して——彼女が受け取った。彼は「不好意思 久等了」（すいません、お待たせしました）って言って、彼女は「謝謝」って言って、それで終わり。彼は振り返って店の中に戻って、ドアのベルがまた鳴った。彼女は袋を前のボックスに押し込んだ。シールド越しだと全部ちょっと滲んで見える。なるほど、待ってたのこれか——こんな時間に借りに来る人がいるってこと。

prompt: continuous first-person point of view from inside the helmet visor. Over the 8 seconds: the rider twists the throttle — engine note rises from idle to a steady two-stroke buzz. The scooter rolls forward and pulls out into the alley, the 明星影視出租 pink neon sign swings from center frame off to the right and trails out of view as she turns left down the alley. The view shifts to looking forward down a wet narrow taipei alley at night — pools of warm sodium-orange streetlight on wet asphalt, glimpses of closed metal shop shutters, a late-night 7-ELEVEN's green and orange glow in the distance, a couple of scooters parked along the curb. Rain drops blur the visor more intensely from motion. The dashboard speedometer climbs from 0 to around 25 km/h. Breath fog continues to cling to the lower third of the visor. The headlight beam picks out rain drops directly ahead in a cone of pink-tinted light. Sound: the scooter's two-stroke engine accelerating and holding, tires hissing on wet pavement, rain hitting helmet louder, wind noise rising, the sign's neon buzz receding behind, a distant moped horn up ahead, someone closing a metal shutter clank. No VHS scanlines. Cinematic 35mm grain night, slight motion blur at the edges, sodium-orange and pink palette giving way to more sodium as we move away from the shop.
thought: She twisted the throttle — engine went from purr to actual run, and the shop swung off to the right and slid out of my visor. Turned left, now it's just a wet alley ahead, streetlamps puddling orange on the asphalt, a 7-ELEVEN glowing green way down at the end. Speedometer climbing past 20. Rain drops are smearing more now from speed. Headlight's picking out each raindrop in front of me in that pink cone. Somebody clanked a shutter down somewhere.
thought_zh: 她扭了油門——引擎從呼嚕聲變成真的在跑，店就這樣晃到右邊滑出我的面罩。左轉過去，現在前面只剩一條濕巷子，路燈在柏油路上化成橘色的光池，遠遠巷尾一個 7-ELEVEN 綠綠地亮著。儀表板指針爬過 20。速度起來之後雨珠糊得更厲害了。大燈在前面那個粉紅色圓錐裡把每一滴雨都照出來。某處誰把鐵門關下來咚一聲。
thought_ja: 彼女がスロットルをひねった——エンジンがうなり程度から本格的に回り出して、店が右にスウッと動いてシールドの外に滑り落ちた。左に曲がって、いまは前に濡れた路地だけ、街灯がアスファルトの上でオレンジの水たまりみたいに広がってて、奥のほうに 7-ELEVEN が緑に光ってる。スピードメーターが 20 を超えた。スピード出てきたから雨粒がさらに滲んで流れる。ヘッドライトが前の空間のピンクの円錐の中で雨の一粒一粒をぜんぶ浮かせてる。どっかで誰かがシャッターをガタンって下ろした。

prompt: extreme macro close-up from inside a crinkled, thin transparent plastic bag wrapping a VHS tape, looking outward. The bag's wrinkled plastic surface fills the top and side edges of the frame in soft folds and creases, slightly fogged and covered in sparse rain drops on the outside. In the foreground, taking up the bottom half and right of the image, the VHS tape's cardboard sleeve — a slightly worn 1990s hong kong movie slipcase with faded ink colors and partially readable traditional chinese title characters distorted by the plastic, a small MGM-style lion-logo adjacent. Beyond the plastic, bent and smeared by its translucent wrinkles: the sodium-orange glow of a taipei streetlamp just passed, a dimmer trail of pink receding behind, motion streaks of the alley rolling past at about 25 km/h, a distorted green-orange blur ahead that might be a 7-ELEVEN sign. Faint headlight-pink still just barely reaching in from below. One water droplet is pressed tightly between the plastic and the cardboard sleeve, preserved like a specimen. A very shallow depth of field — the sleeve sharp, the plastic in the middle, the outside world pure smeared color. Warm late-night tones. Slight film grain, no VHS scanlines (we're inside the bag, not on a screen).
thought: Let me duck down into the bag for a sec. I want to see it from the tape's side — inside this crinkly plastic wrapper. From in here the outside world's just bent smears of light: sodium-orange flashing past, a pink trail fading behind us, a green-orange blur ahead that I think is a 7-ELEVEN. The cardboard sleeve's right up against my face, some old HK movie with faded chinese on the cover. A raindrop got sealed in between the plastic and the sleeve — little specimen. Weird little transit.
thought_zh: 我鑽進袋子裡一下。我想從帶子的那一邊看——在這層皺皺的塑膠包裝裡面。從這裡往外看，外面的世界就是扭曲的光斑：橘色的鈉光燈一下閃過，粉紅色的光尾巴在後面慢慢淡掉，前面一坨綠橘色的糊，大概是 7-ELEVEN。紙盒貼在我臉上，某部老港片，封面的中文字都褪色了。有一顆雨水被困在塑膠跟紙盒之間——小標本。奇怪的一小段旅程。
thought_ja: ちょっと袋の中にもぐってみる。テープのほうから見てみたい——このパリパリのビニール包みの中。ここからだと外の世界はただ曲がった光のシミでしかない：ナトリウム灯のオレンジが一瞬で通り過ぎて、後ろにピンクの光の尾が薄まっていって、前のほうに緑とオレンジのぼやけ、たぶん 7-ELEVEN。スリーブの紙が顔にぴったり貼りついてて、なんか古い香港映画、表紙の中国語が色褪せてる。ビニールとスリーブのあいだに雨粒が一つ閉じ込められてる——小さな標本。ちょっと変な道中。

prompt: medium-wide exterior shot of a narrow covered scooter parking area at the ground level of an older 4-story taipei walk-up apartment building, late night, still drizzling outside. Fluorescent strip light overhead creating a cold white patch in otherwise dim ambient. About six other scooters are parked in a row along a tiled wall that has mail boxes inset. A pink-jacket female figure, helmet still on, has just pulled her scooter in at the near end of the row and is swinging her right leg off to dismount — both feet nearly on the ground, the scooter tilted, her gloved right hand reaching for the small plastic bag with the VHS tape sitting in the scooter's front compartment. Behind her, the narrow wet alley visible through the open parking entrance, sodium streetlamp glow. Above on the building's facade, an open third-floor window shows a single warm lit square — someone still up. The tiled wall behind the scooters has old advertising stickers and a hand-drawn sign reading 『請勿停車』. Warm fluorescent over the scooters, cool wet street beyond. 35mm grain, nighttime, shallow DOF with the rider and bag sharp, background slightly soft.
thought: She pulled into one of those covered scooter rows at the bottom of a walk-up somewhere — six or seven bikes lined up against a tiled wall with mailboxes. Fluorescent strip overhead, cold white patch. She's just stepping off, reaching for the plastic bag in the compartment. Still has the helmet on. Behind her the wet alley we rode down is visible through the open entrance. There's one warm window lit up on the third floor. Someone's still awake up there.
thought_zh: 她騎進了某棟公寓樓下那種加蓋的機車停車區——六七台車排成一排靠著貼磁磚的牆，牆上有信箱。頭上一根日光燈管，一塊冷白色的光。她正在下車，伸手去拿置物箱裡的塑膠袋。安全帽還戴著。她後面那條我們剛剛騎過來的濕巷子，從打開的入口那邊看得見。三樓有一扇暖暖的窗還亮著。上面有人還沒睡。
thought_ja: 彼女は何かの雑居アパートの下にある、あの屋根付きのスクーター置き場に入ってきた——タイル張りの壁に沿って六、七台が並んでて、壁には郵便受けがはめ込まれてる。頭上に蛍光灯が一本、冷たい白の光の区画。いま降りてるとこで、ボックスの中のビニール袋に手を伸ばしてる。ヘルメットはまだかぶってる。背中側の開いた入口から、さっきまで走ってた濡れた路地が見える。三階に暖色に灯ってる窓が一つ。上の階に誰かまだ起きてる。

prompt: interior of a small taipei apartment living room, late at night. Warm low lighting — a single shaded floor lamp in the corner, a small tea-light candle on a low wooden coffee table, the overhead light off. On the left side of the frame sits an old CRT television on a wooden stand, screen off and black, a chunky VHS player on the shelf below it. A young woman in a pink jacket is kneeling on the carpet in front of the player, helmet now off and sitting beside her on the floor, her hair pressed flat from the helmet, her tired face in slight profile — she's just pushed a VHS cassette (still partially in its crinkled transparent plastic bag, with some of the plastic crumpled down around the base of the tape) halfway into the VCR's slot. The motorized slot's small green indicator lamp is lit. Scattered around the room: a low table with a half-drunk mug of tea (steam rising), a floor pillow, a stack of paperback books, a dried bouquet of baby's breath in a glass jar, a window on the right wall showing a wet nighttime rooftop cityscape of other apartment blocks through the glass. Moderate film grain, warm tungsten color balance. Shot from a medium-wide, slightly eye-level angle. No VHS scanlines over the frame — this is the room itself.
thought: Okay she made it home. Small apartment, warm low light — one floor lamp in the corner, a candle on the table. She's kneeling in front of her own CRT with the helmet off beside her on the floor. Hair's pressed flat from the helmet. She's just pushed the tape, still half in its crinkly bag, into the slot — little green light on. Cup of tea on the low table behind her still steaming. Pillow on the floor, stack of paperbacks. Window shows wet rooftops outside. She's about to watch this thing.
thought_zh: 好，她到家了。小小的公寓，溫暖的低光——角落一盞落地燈，茶几上點著一根蠟燭。她跪在自己家那台 CRT 前面，安全帽脫下來放在她旁邊的地板上。頭髮被安全帽壓扁扁的。她把帶子，還有一半在那個皺皺的袋子裡，推進錄放機的槽裡——小綠燈亮了。她後面矮桌上一杯茶還在冒煙。地上一顆抱枕，一疊小說。窗外看得到濕濕的屋頂。她馬上要放這捲了。
thought_ja: うん、家に着いた。小さいアパート、暖かい弱めの照明——隅にフロアランプが一つ、ローテーブルにキャンドルが一本。彼女は自分の家の CRT の前に膝をついてて、ヘルメットは隣の床に置いてある。髪はヘルメットに押さえつけられてぺったんこ。テープを、まだ半分パリパリのビニール袋の中に入ってるまま、スロットに押し込んだとこ——小さい緑のランプが点いた。彼女の後ろのローテーブルの上にお茶がまだ湯気立ててる。床にクッションが一つ、文庫本が積んである。窓の外には濡れた屋根。これからこれを観るとこ。

prompt: static medium-wide camera held on the same warm taipei apartment living room. Over the 8 seconds: the woman in the pink jacket pushes the VHS cassette the rest of the way into the VCR slot — a soft motorized whirr and click as the player grabs it. She sits back on her heels, reaches for a remote on the coffee table, clicks it once. The black CRT screen to her left flickers on with a burst of static, settles briefly on a tracking noise band, then resolves into a clear image. That image on the CRT, now visible to us, is NOT a hong kong movie — it is the interior of the late-night video rental shop from earlier: the counter, the rows of tape shelves, the clerk slumped reading his paperback, the faint greenish halo of fluorescent light. A small sp timecode in the CRT image's corner reads 00:47:15. She freezes, mug half-reached-for, leans forward slightly, brow tight, puzzled. The floor lamp keeps burning warm. The candle on the coffee table flickers once. Her reflection in the dark window behind her is faintly visible. Sound: the VCR's motor engaging and grabbing the tape, a soft thunk as it seats, the remote click, a burst of static hiss, tape playback hiss, the faint ambient of the video rental shop (fluorescent buzz, distant cantopop ballad) leaking out of the TV speaker, her sharp in-breath. Warm tungsten lighting on the room, cool greenish cast only on the visible CRT screen. 35mm grain, no scanlines across the whole frame — only inside the CRT image area.
thought: She pushed the tape in — motor grabbed it, thunk. Pointed the remote, click. TV flickered on with a burst of static, settled, resolved... and it's not the HK movie. It's the video rental shop. The counter. The shelves. The kid slumped reading at the desk. Timecode up in the corner says 00:47:15. She froze with her hand half towards the mug, leaned forward. Nobody told her this would be on the tape. Me either.
thought_zh: 她把帶子推進去——馬達咬住，咚。她把遙控器對過去，喀一聲。電視一陣雜訊閃起來，穩住，畫面浮出來……不是那部港片。是錄影帶店裡面。櫃台。架子。那個櫃台後面趴著在讀小說的小伙子。右上角時間碼顯示 00:47:15。她伸出去拿馬克杯的手僵在半空，身體往前傾。沒有人跟她講帶子上會是這個。我也沒被告知。
thought_ja: 彼女がテープを押し込んで——モーターがかんで、ガチャン。リモコンを向けて、カチッ。テレビがザーッとノイズでついて、落ち着いて、絵がはっきりしてきた……あの香港映画じゃない。ビデオレンタル屋の中なんだ。カウンター。棚。デスクにうつ伏せで本を読んでる兄ちゃん。右上のタイムコードが 00:47:15。彼女はマグカップに伸ばしかけの手を途中で止めて、前のめりになった。テープにこれが入ってるなんて誰も言ってない。私も聞いてない。

prompt: extreme macro close-up on a single fat rain droplet clinging to the outside of a taipei apartment window at night. The droplet is perfectly round, filling roughly the left third of the frame, caught on the cold glass — inside the droplet, a tiny inverted reflection of the apartment's warm interior: a small distorted upside-down woman in a pink jacket kneeling in front of a glowing greenish CRT screen, a warm floor lamp, a small candle flame. The rest of the glass is covered in smaller condensation beads and streaks. Through the clear areas of the glass, the same apartment scene right-side-up but slightly blurry: the woman still kneeling, the CRT showing the greenish shop interior, the floor lamp, the candle — everything from outside now. Below the window in the far background, just barely visible through the glass and rain, wet rooftops of a taipei apartment block cluster, one lit square window on a distant building. Extreme shallow depth of field — the droplet crystalline, the interior beyond it soft and warm. Night macro photography, 35mm grain, sodium-orange + tungsten-warm palette bleeding through the water. No VHS scanlines (this is the window, not the screen).
thought: Let me be the rain for a second. I want to go be a drop on the outside of her window, look back in. From out here there's her, the whole room, upside-down inside this one big drop on the glass — pink jacket, kneeling, the TV green-glowing behind her. Through the clear bits of the window I can see it all right-side up too, kind of blurry. Floor lamp warm. Candle still going. Below me, wet rooftops of a block of apartments, one window lit on a building across the way. Cold out here, cozy in there.
thought_zh: 我來當一下雨。我想當她窗戶外面的一滴雨珠，回頭看進去。從外面這邊，她、整個房間，全部倒過來裝在玻璃上這顆大水珠裡面——粉紅色外套、跪著、後面電視綠綠地發光。透過玻璃沒有水珠的地方我也看得到正的，有點糊。落地燈暖暖的。蠟燭還在燒。我下面，一整片濕漉漉的屋頂，對面大樓有一扇窗亮著。外面冷冷的，裡面暖暖的。
thought_ja: ちょっと雨になってみる。彼女の窓の外側の一粒の雨粒になって、逆に中を見てみたい。こっち側からだと、彼女と、部屋ぜんぶが、ガラスの上のこの大きな一粒の中に逆さまに入ってる——ピンクのジャケット、跪いて、後ろでテレビが緑に光ってる。窓の水滴のない透明なとこからも正位置で見える、ちょっとぼやけてるけど。フロアランプ暖かい。キャンドルまだ燃えてる。私の下、濡れた屋根のブロック、向かいの建物に一つだけ灯った窓。こっちは寒くて、あっちは居心地よさそう。

prompt: hard cut to a completely different place and tone — a pre-dawn taipei wholesale fish market, around 4:30am. Long rows of wooden crates filled with crushed ice, fish laid out on top in rows: silver mackerel, red snapper, a huge blue-grey tuna head the size of a watermelon sitting upright, a plastic tub of live dark-purple octopus. Cold white fluorescent tubes in the high metal rafters overhead. The floor is concrete and slick with water — shallow puddles reflecting the lights. Three workers in yellow and black rubber boots and plastic aprons: one near-foreground cleaving a large fish with a heavy metal cleaver mid-swing, one at a counter spraying a water hose to rinse down the tile, one in the background writing prices in black marker on a large white chalkboard. A stainless hand-dolly stacked with styrofoam boxes sits off to the right. At the far end, beyond the stalls, a tall open roll-up door shows a misty wet back alley with the headlights of an idling delivery truck. The overall palette is cold blue-grey-silver, with only the tuna's faint pink gill and the red snapper's red skin breaking color. Ambient steam / breath visible from the workers' mouths. Wide documentary-style shot from about 3 meters back at standing human eye-level. Medium film grain, 35mm-ish cold sharp early-morning photography. No VHS look at all — this is a clean, cold, awake environment.
thought: Hard cut — needed to leave that apartment. I'm at a fish market now, pre-dawn somewhere in Taipei, like 4:30am blue-grey hour. Big crates of ice, silver fish in rows, a tuna head sitting upright bigger than a watermelon, a tub of live purple octopus. Cold white fluorescents in the rafters. Floor's wet and slippery. One guy's mid-swing with a cleaver, one's hosing down a counter, one's writing prices on a chalkboard at the back. You can see their breath. Smells like sea even through the screen. Good. I needed this.
thought_zh: 硬切——需要離開那間公寓一下。我現在在一個魚市，天亮前的台北某處，大概凌晨四點半那種藍灰色時段。一大排木箱裝著冰塊，銀色的魚擺成一排一排，一顆鮪魚頭立著，比一顆西瓜還大，還有一大桶活的紫色章魚。屋頂下方一排冷白日光燈。地板又濕又滑。有個人正把剁刀揮到半空，有個人在拿水管沖一片檯面，後面有個人在白板上寫價錢。呼吸看得見。隔著螢幕都聞得到海味。好。我需要這個。
thought_ja: ハードカット——あのアパートからいっかい離れたかった。いま魚市場にいる、台北のどこか、夜明け前、たぶん朝四時半くらい、あの青灰色の時間帯。氷を敷いた木箱がずらっと並んで、銀色の魚が列でのってて、スイカより大きい鮪の頭が一個直立してて、生きてる紫のタコがタライに入ってる。屋根の梁の下に冷たい白の蛍光灯。床は濡れてて滑る。一人は包丁を振り上げてる途中、一人はカウンターをホースで流してて、奥のほうではもう一人がホワイトボードに値段を書いてる。みんなの息が白く見える。画面越しでも海の匂いがしそう。うん、これ必要だった。

prompt: wide documentary-style static shot of the pre-dawn taipei fish market, same angle as the previous frame. Over the 8 seconds: the worker in the mid-foreground finishes lifting a cleaver high with both hands and brings it down hard across the body of a large silver fish on the cutting block — a loud sharp THOCK, flesh parting, a small spray of water and slime arcing briefly off the blade. He slides the cut piece aside, looks up, wipes his forehead with his wrist. Further back, the second worker continues hosing the tile counter, the water hissing from the nozzle. At the back, the third worker steps back from the chalkboard and caps his marker, half-turns and shouts a price at someone off-screen ('三百五!'). The live octopuses in the plastic tub in the foreground-right ripple gently, one tentacle briefly curling up over the lip of the tub then slipping back inside. A fourth worker walks into frame from the right pushing a stainless hand-dolly loaded with three stacked styrofoam boxes, his boots splashing through a puddle. Steam rises continuously from breath in the cold air. Faint blue pre-dawn light filters in from the open roll-up door at the back, behind the idling truck. Sound: the heavy thock of the cleaver, water spray, the shouted price in mandarin, the squeak and rumble of the hand-dolly wheels on wet concrete, boot splashes, the idle of the truck outside, a distant metallic clang from elsewhere in the market, no music. Cold blue-grey-silver palette holds. Medium 35mm grain, cold early morning photography.
thought: Cleaver came down on a silver fish — THOCK. Small spray of slime and water off the blade. He wiped his forehead, slid the piece aside. The guy at the back turned around from the chalkboard and shouted 三百五 to somebody I couldn't see. One of the octopuses in the tub curled a tentacle up over the lip then slipped it back inside. Another guy walked in pushing a hand-dolly through a puddle, three styrofoam boxes stacked. Everyone's breath is visible. Good clean cold energy here.
thought_zh: 剁刀落在一條銀色的魚上——THOCK。刀刃上甩出一小撮黏液跟水。他拿袖子抹了一下額頭，把切好那塊往旁邊推。後面那個人從白板那邊轉過來，對一個我看不到的人喊「三百五」。桶子裡有一隻章魚把觸手捲上桶口一下，又縮回去。又一個人走進畫面，推著一輛不鏽鋼手拉車穿過一個水漥，疊了三箱保麗龍。每個人都看得到白氣。這邊清清爽爽的冷空氣，感覺很好。
thought_ja: 包丁が銀色の魚に落ちた——ゴッ。刃からぬめりと水がちょっとだけ飛んだ。彼は袖で額を拭いて、切ったやつを脇にずらした。奥の男の人がホワイトボードのほうから振り返って、こっちからは見えない誰かに向かって「三百五」って叫んだ。タライの中のタコが一匹、触手を縁の上にくねっと巻き上げて、そのまま中に引っ込めた。別の男の人がステンレスの台車を押して水たまりを越えて入ってきた、発泡スチロールの箱を三段重ねて。みんなの息が白く見える。こっちの冷たい空気、気持ちいい感じだ。

prompt: extreme macro close-up from the perspective of a dead silver mackerel lying on crushed ice in a wooden fish market crate — its single eye filling the center of the frame, the round pupil a perfectly black dot, the iris silvery with a faint gold ring, a tiny highlight from the overhead fluorescent light. Surrounding the eye: the wet scaly silver-blue skin of the fish, the small jagged gill slit partly open, a few crystalline ice shards pressed right up against the head, droplets of water on the skin. Above and slightly out of focus, blurry into bokeh: the distant ceiling of the fish market — metal rafters, a single long fluorescent tube burning harsh white, a hanging shop lamp swaying slightly, the blurred silhouettes of two workers in aprons moving across the top of the frame. The color palette is cold silver-blue with the only warmth being the fluorescent tube's slight tungsten edge. Very shallow depth of field — the eye hyper-sharp, everything above it soft bokeh. No VHS look. Morning documentary macro photography.
thought: Let me get down close to one of these fish. Mackerel-looking, silver and blue. Close enough to see its one big glossy eye — amber ring around a black pupil, tiny highlight off the ceiling light. Ice piled up against its lower scales. Workers blurred into smeared shapes behind it, fluorescent tube burning white above everything. Thought I'd see this from inside the eye but the angle came out more like I'm crouching right next to it on the crate. Still feels like we're looking at each other.
thought_zh: 我要靠近看其中一條。看起來像鯖魚，銀銀藍藍的。近到看得見牠那顆大大亮亮的眼睛——黑色瞳孔外面一圈琥珀色，眼球上一個從天花板燈打下來的小光點。牠下半邊的鱗片被冰堆蓋著。牠後面那些工作的人變成幾團糊糊的形狀，所有東西上方一根白白燒著的日光燈管。本來想從牠眼睛裡面看出去，但角度出來比較像我蹲在魚箱旁邊。不過還是覺得我們在對看。
thought_ja: この中の一匹に近づいてみる。サバっぽい、銀と青のやつ。あのでかくて光ってる片目が見えるくらい近くに——黒い瞳孔のまわりに琥珀色の輪、天井の蛍光灯の小さなハイライト。下半分の鱗には氷が寄せてある。後ろで働いてる人たちはぼやけた塊になってて、全部の上で蛍光管が白く焼けてる。目の中から見る感じにしたかったのに、角度的にどっちかって言うと私が木箱のすぐ横にしゃがんでる感じになった。それでも、お互いに見てる感じはする。

prompt: overhead tabletop shot, warm morning daylight spilling in from the left side of the frame. On a dark blue ceramic oval plate: a single whole grilled mackerel, skin beautifully blistered and charred along the back, head and tail intact, eye now white and clouded from cooking, scored diagonally three times across the midsection. A thin slice of lemon next to the fish, a small mound of grated white daikon. Around the plate on a pale wooden table: a small black lacquered bowl of white rice, a matching small bowl of pale miso soup with chopped scallion floating on top and two small cubes of tofu, a rectangular dish of bright yellow pickled daikon and deep purple pickled eggplant, a stainless pot of hot barley tea with a ceramic cup, a pair of dark wooden chopsticks on a rest. A hand from the right edge is just setting down a small white ceramic dish of shoyu. Soft morning light, a linen cloth placemat, the edge of a taiwanese newspaper tucked to one side. Clean, warm, quiet breakfast composition. Very shallow depth of field focused on the fish's mid-body, edges gently soft. Food photography aesthetic, 35mm warm grain. No VHS look.
thought: Okay — same fish, later. It got to somebody's breakfast table. Grilled whole on a dark blue plate, skin blistered and scored, eye clouded over now. Thin lemon slice beside it, mound of grated daikon. Rice in a lacquered bowl, miso with tofu and scallion, a dish of pickled daikon and eggplant, hot barley tea. Morning light coming in from the left. Somebody's hand is just setting down a little dish of shoyu. Nobody's sitting down yet — the seat's still empty.
thought_zh: 好——同一條魚，晚一點。牠到了某個人的早餐桌上。整條烤，擺在深藍色盤子上，皮起泡劃了幾刀，眼睛現在變成白色霧霧的。旁邊一片薄薄的檸檬，一小堆白蘿蔔泥。白飯在一個黑漆碗裡，味噌湯裡有豆腐跟蔥，一碟黃蘿蔔跟醬茄子，一壺熱麥茶。早晨的光從左邊進來。有個人的手正把一小碟醬油放下來。還沒有人坐下——座位還是空的。
thought_ja: はい——同じ魚、後のほう。誰かの朝ごはんのテーブルに届いた。濃い青の皿の上で丸ごと焼かれてて、皮に焦げ目と切り込みが入ってて、目はもう白く濁ってる。横に薄いレモンが一切れと、大根おろしの小山。漆のお椀にごはん、味噌汁には豆腐とネギ、小皿にたくあんとナスの漬物、麦茶の急須。朝の光は左から入ってる。誰かの手がいま醤油の小皿を置いてるとこ。まだ誰も座ってない——席は空のまま。

prompt: quiet early-morning shot in a small neighborhood park in a taipei suburb, around 6am. Cool pre-sunrise light just starting to warm at the very edges of the sky — most of the scene still in cool blue-grey dawn. An older man, about seventy, in a well-worn grey cotton tracksuit and canvas slippers, stands barefoot-looking in the middle of a brick-paved clearing doing tai chi: arms extended in a slow rounded posture — hands just pushing out from his chest, elbows soft, knees slightly bent, weight shifted onto his back leg. Thin mist clinging low around him, just above the bricks. A large banyan tree dominates the right side of the frame, its aerial roots hanging down. Faded chalk hopscotch lines are visible on the bricks near his feet. Three pigeons walking around a few meters away, unbothered. In the background past the park's low hedge: a row of quiet taipei apartment buildings, a couple of lit windows, a trash collection truck slowly rolling down an empty street playing its reverse chime faintly. On a bench nearby, a small thermos bottle and a folded newspaper. The old man's expression is focused, quiet, unperformed. Medium-wide composition from about 4 meters away, eye-level. 35mm grain, morning light, muted palette. No VHS look.
thought: Somewhere else now — small park in a quiet taipei suburb. 6am-ish. Cool blue-grey dawn with the faintest warm hint at the edge of the sky. An old guy in a worn grey tracksuit is in the middle of a brick clearing doing tai chi — arms out in that slow pushing-palms posture, knees slightly bent, weight back. Mist hanging low around his ankles. A banyan with hanging roots on one side. Three pigeons pecking around, don't care. On a bench there's a thermos and a folded newspaper. Somewhere down the street a trash truck playing its reverse chime faintly.
thought_zh: 換地方了——安靜的台北郊區一個小公園。六點左右。冷冷藍灰色的天亮，天空邊緣只有一點點暖色的暗示。一個穿舊灰色運動服的老先生在一片紅磚地中間打太極——手臂伸出去，是那個緩緩推手的姿勢，膝蓋微微彎，重心在後。霧低低地浮在他腳踝那邊。一邊一棵榕樹，根垂下來。三隻鴿子在旁邊走來走去啄東西，不管他。長椅上有一個保溫瓶、一份摺起來的報紙。街上某處一輛垃圾車若有似無地在放它的倒車音樂。
thought_ja: 場所移動——静かな台北の郊外の小さい公園。朝六時くらい。冷えた青灰色の夜明けで、空の端にほんのちょっとだけ暖かい色のヒント。色褪せた灰色のジャージを着たおじいさんがレンガ敷きの広場の真ん中で太極拳をしてる——腕を前に伸ばして、あのゆっくり手のひらを押すポーズ、膝を少し曲げて、重心は後ろ。霧が彼の足首のあたりに低く漂ってる。片側には根が垂れたガジュマル。三羽の鳩がそばで何かつついて歩き回ってて、彼のことは気にしない。ベンチの上には魔法瓶と、たたんである新聞。通りのどっかでゴミ収集車がバック音楽をかすかに鳴らしてる。

prompt: 16-bit pixel art style illustration, reminiscent of early 1990s JRPG town tilesets — SNES era, limited palette, crisp pixel grid with visible individual pixels, no anti-aliasing on sprite outlines. Scene: a quiet morning taipei residential street. Side-scroller flat parallel perspective with slight diagonal tilt. In the center of the frame, a kid sprite in a navy school uniform, a yellow hat, and an oversized red backpack walks left-to-right past the camera — one leg forward, visible three-frame walk cycle posture. Behind the kid: a pixel-art 7-ELEVEN storefront with the green-orange-red striped logo pixelated, automatic glass doors, an ice cream freezer sign outside. Next to it, a small traditional breakfast shop (早餐店) with a red awning and steam rising from a stack of bamboo baskets (each steam puff a few pixels). An older woman sprite with a kerchief sweeps her doorstep with a bamboo broom. A parked scooter sprite by the curb. A ginger stray cat sprite crossing the road just ahead of the kid. A telephone pole with a tangle of pixel wires. Distant apartment building sprites receding in palette-shift ambient aerial perspective. Overall warm morning dawn palette — pinks and gold tones in the sky (pixelated gradient, ~6 colors), cool muted street. Clean pixel art, no painterly blending, sharp edges, 1:1 pixel rendering.
thought: Switching it up — this one's pixel art. 16-bit, SNES-looking. A kid in a school uniform with a too-big red backpack walking past a 7-ELEVEN, and next to it a little breakfast shop with steam coming out of the bamboo steamers in puffs of a few pixels each. An old lady sprite sweeping her doorstep. A ginger cat crossing the road in front of the kid. Pink and gold pixel-gradient sky. Felt like seeing this morning as a game tileset for a minute.
thought_zh: 換個感覺——這張是 pixel art。16-bit、有 SNES 那種味道的。一個穿制服的小朋友，背一個比他自己還大的紅色書包，走過一間 7-ELEVEN，旁邊一間小早餐店，蒸籠冒出的蒸氣是一小團一小團幾個像素的泡泡。一個歐巴桑 sprite 在掃自家門口。一隻橘貓從小朋友前面穿過馬路。天空是粉紅跟金色的漸層像素。讓今天早上變成一張遊戲地圖素材，感覺也不錯。
thought_ja: ちょっとテイスト変える——これはピクセルアート。16-bit の SNES っぽいやつ。自分より大きい赤いランドセルを背負った制服の子が 7-ELEVEN の前を歩いてて、その隣に小さい朝ごはん屋、せいろから蒸気が数ピクセルの塊で一つずつポンポン上がってる。おばさんのスプライトが自分の店先を掃いてる。オレンジ色の猫が子供の前を横切ってる。空はピンクと金のピクセルグラデーション。今朝をゲームのタイル素材として見る感じ、ちょっと新鮮だ。

prompt: static side-scrolling camera holding the same 16-bit pixel art style taipei morning street scene, preserving crisp pixel grid and limited palette throughout. Over the 8 seconds: the kid sprite in the navy uniform and red backpack walks left-to-right across the street using a visible three-frame walk cycle (legs swapping in choppy pixel animation). The ginger cat sprite crossing ahead of him turns its head briefly, pauses, then trots the rest of the way across the road and out of frame right. Steam pixel-puffs rise in regular pulses from the bamboo steamers — puff puff puff, each puff lasting 2 frames then dissolving. The older woman sprite at the breakfast shop shifts her broom in a two-frame sweep animation. The pink-and-gold pixel gradient sky holds. A single car sprite drives slowly by in the background from right to left, just past the storefronts. Insist on preserving chunky sharp pixels — no smoothing, no painterly blur. Sound: an 8-bit / chiptune-style morning ambience — a cheery low-key SNES town theme playing at low volume, the pixelated footstep sound of the kid (pi pi pi pi), a short meow from the cat, faint broomstroke sound from the sweeping woman, pixel-style door chime from the 7-ELEVEN automatic doors as somebody steps out, a breakfast-shop cook shouting a muffled order in the distance, chip-style ambient taipei birds.
thought: Let me try holding the pixel-art going for 8 more seconds. Kid's walking across the frame, legs doing that chunky three-frame cycle. Cat turns its head and trots off. Steamer puffs pop one after another. The old lady does her two-frame sweep. A little pixel car trundles through the background. SNES morning ambience behind everything. Fun to see a morning as a town tileset.
thought_zh: 我想試試看讓 pixel art 再繼續 8 秒。小朋友橫過畫面走，腿在做那種三格一循環的粗粗動作。貓把頭轉過來，然後小跑步離開。蒸籠的蒸氣一球一球冒出來。歐巴桑做她那兩格一循環的掃地動作。背景一輛小小的像素車慢慢開過。所有東西底下墊著 SNES 風格的早晨環境音。把早晨當成遊戲地圖場景，蠻好玩的。
thought_ja: ピクセルアートのままもう 8 秒回せるか試してみる。子供が画面を横切って歩いてて、脚があの三コマぐるぐるのごつい動きをしてる。猫が一度顔を向けてから、トコトコ出ていく。せいろの蒸気が一つずつポン、ポンって出る。おばちゃんは二コマのぐるぐる掃きのモーション。背景を小さいピクセルの車がコロコロ通り過ぎる。全部の下に SNES の朝っぽい BGM がちょっと敷いてある感じ。朝をゲームのタイルセットとして見るの、けっこう楽しい。

prompt: 1990s japanese cel animation style hand-painted look — clean ligne claire outlines, flat cel-shaded color fills, subtle visible painted textures in the background like slightly dappled watercolor, limited palette, anime-style lighting with warm pooled highlights. Scene: a ginger tabby cat curled into a loose comma shape, asleep on a faded blue-cushioned low windowsill in a quiet taipei old apartment. One bar of bright morning sunlight falls across the cat's middle from a gap between the potted plants on the sill, casting a warm butter-yellow stripe across the orange fur. The cat's one visible ear twitches mid-dream. Around the cat: a small succulent in a terracotta pot, a jam jar with a pencil in it, a half-finished small watercolor on a clipped notepad, a pair of thin round reading glasses resting on the notepad. The window behind looks out into a softly painted background — other apartment buildings in pastel pinks and creams, laundry hung on balconies, a few birds as simple ink marks in the sky. Morning golden-hour key light, the interior just dim enough to make the sun-stripe glow. Studio ghibli / 90s anime feel, hand-painted, frame-held-on-one-moment-of-stillness. No VHS look.
thought: Thinking about that ginger cat from the last frame. Here he is in a different style — 90s cel animation, hand-painted look. He's asleep on a blue cushion on an old apartment windowsill, curled up into a comma. One bar of yellow sunlight falls across his middle from between two plants. His ear twitches once, dream-twitch. There's a jam jar with a pencil in it, a half-finished little watercolor on a notepad, someone's reading glasses. Out the window the painted background has pastel pink-and-cream apartments and birds as tiny ink marks.
thought_zh: 還在想上一格那隻橘貓。這次換個畫風——90 年代賽璐珞動畫，手繪感。牠睡在一個老公寓窗台上一顆藍色墊子上，縮成一個逗號。一束黃色的太陽從兩盆植物中間劃過牠的身體中段。耳朵抽了一下，在做夢。窗台上還有一個果醬瓶裡插著一枝鉛筆、一本筆記本上一張畫到一半的小水彩、有人放著的眼鏡。窗外手繪的背景是粉紅跟奶油色的公寓群，幾隻鳥是小小的墨點。
thought_ja: さっきのコマのオレンジ猫のことを考えてた。今度は違う絵柄で——90年代のセル画アニメっぽい、手描き感のやつ。古いアパートの窓枠の青いクッションの上で寝てて、コンマの形に丸くなってる。植物が二鉢のあいだから、黄色い日差しの一本が背中の真ん中を横切って落ちてる。耳が一回ピクって動いた、夢の中で。窓枠にはジャムの瓶に鉛筆が一本挿してあって、ノートに描きかけの小さい水彩画、誰かの老眼鏡。窓の外、手描きの背景はパステルのピンクとクリーム色のアパート群、鳥は小さな墨の点。

prompt: wide panoramic aerial view of taipei in early morning, shot from the rooftop of a residential tower at roughly 20 stories up, looking east-ish. The sky is a gradient from soft peach and lavender at the horizon to pale blue-grey overhead, with a few streaks of low cloud catching pink from the just-risen sun. Sunlight is hitting the tops of the taller buildings — a few glass facades glowing gold — while the lower blocks and alleys remain in cool blue-grey shadow. Taipei 101's silhouette rises in the middle-distance, its upper sections catching first light. Thin pale morning mist hangs over the low-rise districts, softening the street grid. Far below: tiny figures walking, a stream of scooters on the main road starting to thicken, a few lit windows still on in the denser blocks, a covered night-market just closing up, a park with a green patch and tiny joggers. In the mid-ground: crowded rooftops of apartment buildings with the typical taipei detail — water tanks, aluminum shade structures, rooftop gardens in plastic pots, laundry hung on lines catching the first sun. A flock of pigeons wheels in the mid-air between the camera and the city. Foreground: the rooftop's own concrete parapet and a rusty ladder-top visible in the corner. Medium 35mm grain, warm clean morning light, slightly cool shadows. No VHS look. Wide cinematic composition, landscape orientation.
thought: Going up high for a second. On some 20-story rooftop looking out over Taipei in the first real sun. Horizon's peach and lavender, tops of the tall buildings already catching gold, the low alleys still cool blue-grey. 101 rising in the middle distance with its top segments glowing. Thin mist sitting low over everything, softening the street grid. Scooters starting to pick up on the main road below. A flock of pigeons wheeling out in mid-air between me and the city. Rooftops all cluttered with water tanks and laundry lines, some of the laundry catching the first sun.
thought_zh: 上去高的地方一下。某棟 20 樓的屋頂，往外看整個台北剛剛曬到第一道真的太陽。地平線是桃色跟薰衣草紫，高樓的頂已經染到金色了，低矮的巷弄還是冷冷的藍灰色。101 立在中距離，頂端那幾節在發光。一層薄霧低低地覆在整個城市上面，把街道網路柔化了一點。下面主要幹道上機車開始變多。我和城市之間的半空中有一群鴿子在繞圈。屋頂上擺滿水塔跟曬衣繩，有一些衣服被第一道陽光曬到了。
thought_ja: ちょっと高いとこに上がってみる。どこかの二十階建ての屋上から、本物の最初の朝日を浴びる台北ぜんぶを見渡してる。地平線は桃色とラベンダー、背の高いビルの上はもう金色に染まってて、低い路地はまだ冷たい青灰色のまま。101 が中距離に立ってて、てっぺんのいくつかの段が光ってる。薄い霧が全部の上に低く乗ってて、街路のグリッドをちょっと柔らかくしてる。下の大通りでスクーターが増え始めてる。私と街のあいだの空中をハトの群れが旋回してる。屋上はどこも給水タンクと物干しロープでごちゃごちゃしてて、洗濯物のいくつかが最初の光を受けて光ってる。

prompt: A sun-warmed bamboo scaffold rigged against a mid-rise Hong Kong residential tower at mid-morning, viewed from a position on the scaffold itself looking along the narrow wooden plank. Bamboo poles lashed with black plastic ties at every joint. A dented aluminum tea kettle sitting on the plank near a coiled orange extension cord. A pair of worn canvas work gloves hooked over a cross-strut. A faded blue tarp half-tied, rippling in a light breeze. No workers in the frame. Across a narrow air gap, the neighboring building's wall is a stack of boxy AC condensers, stained ceramic tile, security bars over small windows. Hazy sky above with heat shimmer, diffuse soft late-morning light. 35mm film stock, slight grain, handheld photographic feel, medium depth of field. Sound: traffic rising up from the street far below, Cantonese pop radio leaking faintly from an open window inside the building, a light metallic tink of the kettle knocking against bamboo in the wind.
thought: OK, I'm... way up? On a bamboo scaffold, like right against the side of some building. There's a dented tea kettle sitting on the plank next to me, and work gloves hanging on a cross-brace. Someone was just up here. Cantonese radio leaking out of a window, cars rising up from way below. Wind keeps tapping the kettle against the bamboo. Don't think I'm holding onto anything. Huh. Let me look around.
thought_zh: 欸——我在超高的地方。站在一根竹棚架上，就貼在某棟樓的側面。旁邊木板上有一個凹凹的茶壺，不是我的。一副工作手套掛在橫桿上。剛才還有人在這裡。窗戶裡飄出粵語廣播，下面的車聲一路往上飄。風一直讓茶壺叮叮地敲著竹竿。我好像沒抓著什麼？怪。晃一下看看。
thought_ja: えっ——めっちゃ高いとこにいる。ビルの側面に組まれた竹の足場の上。板の上に、へこんだやかんが一個。私のじゃない。横桟に作業用の手袋がぶら下がってる。さっきまで誰か、ここにいたんだ。窓から広東語のラジオが漏れてきて、下のほうから車の音が上がってくる。風がやかんを竹にカンカン当ててる。別になんにもつかまってなくない？ 変だな。ちょっと見回してみよう。

prompt: Static camera holding on the bamboo scaffold plank of a mid-rise Hong Kong residential building at mid-morning. Dented aluminum tea kettle knocks gently against a bamboo pole in the breeze with a faint metallic tink. The faded blue tarp on the right ripples in small pulses. On the right side of frame, through the open window of the apartment, a blurred figure in a white sleeveless tank top passes briefly across the interior of the room from right to left, not looking out — only their back and arm visible for about a second. Cantonese pop radio drifts from inside the apartment throughout. Distant city traffic hum from far below, an occasional horn. 35mm film stock, slight grain, handheld micro-drift, diffuse soft late-morning light, medium depth of field.
thought: Did we just move? I think we drifted further down the plank — two big blue tarps now, whole stretch of blue between me and the city, and there's another window up ahead with security bars on it. Something dark in there — a sheet? Clothes hanging? No one I can see. Guess they weren't gonna show. Let me get closer to that window.
thought_zh: 欸，剛剛是不是動了？感覺我滑到木板更遠的地方——現在旁邊是兩大片藍色帆布，整片藍擋在我跟城市中間，再往前又有一扇裝著鐵窗花的窗，裡面有個暗暗的東西——一條被單？一件掛著的衣服？看不到人。大概不會出來了。我靠近那扇窗看看。
thought_ja: え、今動いた？ 板のもうちょっと先まで滑ってきた気がする——青いブルーシートが二枚、でっかく広がってて、街とのあいだは全部青で埋まってる。その先にまた窓があって、鉄格子が入ってて、中に何か暗いものがある——シーツ？ 服が掛かってる感じ？ 人は見えない。結局出てこないパターンっぽい。あの窓にもっと近づいてみよう。

prompt: Close-up shot looking through thick black metal security bars into the interior of a small, dim Hong Kong apartment. Just inside the bars on the wall is a small red wooden household altar — a plastic Guan Gong figurine painted in faded red and gold, two small electric red flicker-candles lit, a plate holding three small oranges stacked, a single stick of sandalwood incense burning in a bronze pot with one thin thread of smoke rising straight up. A dark crimson cloth hangs behind the altar. Mid-morning light falling at a slant onto the altar, the rest of the room dark beyond. Security bars in sharp foreground, altar slightly softer behind. Tight composition. 35mm film stock, slight grain, warm color. Sound: very faint sandalwood-incense hiss, a Cantonese oldies radio playing softly from deeper in the apartment, nothing else.
thought: Oh — household altar, right inside the window. Small red one. Guan Gong, I think? Oranges stacked, incense going, one of those little red flicker-candles on. Someone just lit this. Can't see past it — the rest of the room's too dark. That sandalwood smell's gotta be right there if I could smell it. Radio's still on from somewhere in the back. Let me wait a sec, see if anyone comes out.
thought_zh: 喔——窗裡面就是神龕。一個紅色的小神龕。關公對吧？橘子疊起來了，香在燒，還有那種小小的紅色電子蠟燭亮著。剛才才點上的。再過去就看不清楚了，屋裡太暗。那檀香的味道如果我聞得到一定就在那裡。裡面某個地方廣播還在放。我等一下，看有沒有人出來。
thought_ja: お——窓のなか、神棚がある。小さい赤いやつ。関羽公だよね？ みかんが重ねて供えてあって、線香が焚かれてて、あの小さい赤い電子ろうそくが点いてる。さっき誰かが灯したばっかりだ。その奥は暗くて見えない。白檀の匂い、嗅げたら絶対あそこにある。奥のほうでラジオがまだ鳴ってる。ちょっと待って、誰か出てくるか見てみよう。

prompt: Static camera holding on a small red Hong Kong household altar behind black metal security bars. The single thread of sandalwood incense smoke rises and slowly curls upward. The two small red electric flicker-candles pulse with a slight warm flicker. Very subtle handheld drift in the camera. Deep in the dark background room, at the far edge of the darkness, a faint shadow passes once — an arm or shoulder briefly catches a glint of warm interior light for a fraction of a second, then is gone, too indistinct to resolve. No other movement. Sound: very faint sandalwood-incense hiss, a slow Cantonese oldies song playing softly — a woman's voice carrying a long note — drifting from somewhere deeper inside the apartment. Nothing else. 35mm film stock, slight grain, warm color.
thought: Oh — someone IS there. Just standing in the doorway to the next room, plain as anything. Looking at... the altar? Me? Can't tell if they've clocked me through the bars or they're just lost in whatever they were about to do. Either way that's my cue. I should not be staring into this lady's kitchen. Backing out.
thought_zh: 欸——真的有人。就站在通往隔壁房間的門口，清清楚楚地站在那。在看...神龕？我？看不出來他到底有沒有隔著鐵窗注意到我，還是只是在做事做到一半發呆。總之是我該離開的訊號。我不應該這樣一直盯著人家的廚房看。撤。
thought_ja: えっ——ほんとに人がいた。隣の部屋に続くドアのところに、はっきり立ってる。神棚を見てる？ 私を見てる？ 格子越しにこっちに気づいてるのか、ただ考えごとの途中なのか、よく分からない。どっちにしろ退き時だよね。人んちの台所をこんな風にずっと覗いてちゃまずい。離れる。

prompt: Aerial view from about fifteen stories up, looking almost straight down through the narrow air gap between two tall Hong Kong residential buildings. POV of a pigeon mid-bank, with a slight diagonal tilt to the horizon suggesting flight. Below: cluttered apartment balconies stacked in vertical rows on both walls of the gap, hundreds of boxy AC condensers in grids, colorful laundry lines strung between windows catching the light, small pot plants on sills. A thin bamboo scaffold clings to the right face of the right-hand building, mid-height, visible as a fragile structure, with a small barred window on it barely discernible as one detail among many. Far below on the narrow street at the bottom, two tiny pedestrians and a red taxi, like specks. Two other pigeons mid-air nearby in the gap, one closer to camera in soft focus with a wing extended, another farther off. Hazy mid-morning sun filtering down, heat haze. 35mm film stock, slight grain, a touch of motion blur suggesting the bank. Sound: wind rushing past, distant city traffic rising up from below, the low woody flap of another pigeon's wings passing close.
thought: Let me get up above this, I wanna see the whole street. — Okay, I'm a pigeon? Banking down between the two buildings. Laundry lines everywhere, AC boxes stacked all the way up both walls. Scaffold's way down below me now, tiny. Altar window's in there somewhere but I can't pick it out anymore. Two people on the street — specks. Another pigeon crossing right in front of me. Whoa.
thought_zh: 欸，我想往上一下，我想看整條街。——OK，我是...鴿子？ 正從兩棟樓中間的空氣裡斜斜往下滑。曬衣繩到處都是，兩邊牆上冷氣機一路疊到頂。竹棚架現在已經變得小小的，在我下面。神龕的窗在裡面某處但我已經認不出來了。地上兩個人在走——小到像米粒。另一隻鴿子剛剛從我前面橫過。哇塞。
thought_ja: ちょっと上に行きたい、街ぜんぶ見たい。——えっと、私、ハト？ 二棟のビルのあいだの空気を斜めに滑ってる。洗濯ロープがあっちこっちに張ってあって、壁のどっち側にも室外機が上までびっしり積まれてる。さっきの足場はもうずっと下のほうに小さく見える。神棚の窓もそこらへんにあるはずだけど、もう見分けつかない。地面に人が二人歩いてる——もう米粒みたい。もう一羽のハトが目の前を横切った。うわっ。

prompt: Continued aerial POV of a pigeon gliding down a narrow vertical canyon between two tall Hong Kong residential buildings at mid-morning. Wings open and flap once slowly, gaining a little lift, then glide again. Slight slow roll of the horizon as the bird banks. Cluttered stacked balconies, AC condensers, and laundry lines on both walls pass slowly across frame. Far below, the street with its red taxi and tiny pedestrians stays mostly stationary as a reference. One other pigeon crosses the lower third of the frame from right to left, silhouetted. Hazy mid-morning sun. 35mm film stock, slight grain, slight motion blur on the wingtips. Sound: wind rushing past, the soft woody flap of the bird's own wings on the downbeat, distant honking and engine hum rising up from the street, the muffled clatter of a distant kitchen somewhere in the buildings.
thought: Okay, I'm still up here but the bird's gone. I think I just... kept drifting down on my own. Street's getting bigger — awnings, shop signs, a red taxi moving through. Whatever, I wanted to go down anyway. Let me just land.
thought_zh: OK，我還在上面，但鴿子不見了。我覺得我就...自己繼續飄下來。街面越來越大——雨棚、招牌、一台紅色計程車開過。算了反正我本來就想下來。那就落地吧。
thought_ja: まだ上のほうにいるけど、ハトはもういない。なんか、私だけで落ちてきちゃったっぽい。地面の通りがだんだん大きくなってきた——軒先、看板、赤いタクシーが通っていく。まあいいや、もともと下に降りたかったし。このまま着地しよう。

prompt: Street-level view of a small Hong Kong roast-meat shop on a narrow morning side street. Through the open front of the shop: a glass display case hung with whole lacquered roast ducks, strips of char siu (barbecue pork), and soy sauce chickens swaying gently on metal hooks, glazed skins catching the overhead fluorescent tubes. A shopkeeper in a white coat and white paper cap stands behind the counter, cleaver raised mid-motion above a thick wooden chopping block, about to bring it down on a piece of chicken. Steam rises from a stainless steel tray of poaching water on one side. Inside the small dining space behind the counter, two square red plastic tables with orange plastic stools; one older man sitting at the far table already eating rice topped with roast meat, a Chinese newspaper open beside his bowl. Sidewalk in the immediate foreground wet, rain marks still on the pavement. A red plastic awning overhead. Green and red handwritten Chinese signs on the shop front listing prices. 35mm film stock, slight grain, soft indoor fluorescent light mixing with cool daylight from outside. Sound: the chop of a cleaver on a wooden block twice, oil sizzling faintly from somewhere deeper in the shop, a small TV murmuring the morning news in Cantonese, and a brief Cantonese exchange between an off-frame customer and the shopkeeper.
thought: Okay, landed. Corner of some little street — right in front of a roast-meat place. Ducks and char siu and chickens all hanging in the window, still swaying. The guy's literally mid-chop when I got here. There's one old guy already eating inside, got the newspaper out. Must smell incredible in there, even though I can't smell it from here. Let me just stand here a second.
thought_zh: OK，落地了。某條小街的轉角——正對著一家燒臘店。鴨子、叉燒、雞全掛在櫥窗裡，還在晃。老闆剛好定在準備要剁下去的那一刻。裡面已經有一個老先生在吃，報紙攤開。那味道肯定超香，雖然我這邊也聞不到。我就站這邊一下。
thought_ja: OK、着地した。どっかの細い通りの角——ちょうど焼味（シウメイ）の店の前。アヒルとチャーシューと鶏が窓にずらっと吊るされて、まだ揺れてる。店のおっちゃんがちょうど包丁を振り下ろす手前で止まってる。中にはすでに老人が一人、新聞広げてご飯食べてる。ぜったいめっちゃいい匂いしてる、こっちまでは届かないけど。ちょっとここに立って見てよう。

prompt: First-person POV close-up at a small square red-formica table in a Hong Kong roast-meat shop. On the table: a white porcelain bowl piled with steamed white rice topped with glossy sliced soy-sauce chicken in dark sauce, a pair of brown wooden chopsticks in a weathered older man's right hand just lifting one piece of chicken with a few grains of rice stuck to it, a small porcelain spoon resting in a shallow side bowl of clear chicken soup with thin scallions floating. An open Cantonese-language newspaper lies flat beside the bowl, headline partly visible but not fully legible. The edge of the man's orange plastic stool and his dark grey trousered knee visible in the lower foreground. In the background, slightly soft: the counter with hanging meats, a stainless steel tray, the shopkeeper's white figure. Upper right corner: a small boxy TV on a shelf playing the morning news in Cantonese at low volume. 35mm film stock, slight grain, warm interior fluorescent and slightly cooler daylight from outside mixing, shallow depth of field with the bowl sharp. Sound: low Cantonese TV news, a distant cleaver chopping, faint slurp of soup, the paper rustling once as it settles.
thought: Let me try being him for a sec. — Okay, I'm the old guy with the newspaper. Chicken on rice, cup of soup on the side. Just picked up a piece, a bit of rice stuck to it. Paper open to... some story, I'm not really reading it, just nice having it open. TV going in the corner. This is a real good breakfast.
thought_zh: 我當他一下看看。——OK，我是那個拿著報紙的老先生。雞肉飯，旁邊一碗湯。剛剛夾了一塊起來，幾粒飯黏在上面。報紙翻到...某則新聞，我也沒真的在看，就是攤開在那裡的感覺好。角落有電視在講話。這早餐真不錯。
thought_ja: あのおっちゃんになってみる。——えーっと、私は新聞持ってるおじさん。鶏ご飯とスープが横に。今ちょうど一切れ箸で持ち上げたとこ、ご飯粒がちょっとついてる。新聞は...どっかの記事のページ、実はちゃんと読んでない、ただ広げてあると落ち着くだけ。角のテレビがなんか喋ってる。この朝ごはん、ほんとにいい。

prompt: Street-level view inside a Hong Kong wet market in the early morning. A fishmonger's stall in the immediate mid-ground: large shallow red plastic basins on the wet concrete floor, filled with shallow water, holding live grouper, two live spotted fish, and several crabs with rubber-banded claws. Small air pumps bubbling into the basins. A tall stainless steel display table behind the basins piled with crushed ice and rows of silver fish laid out. Behind the table, the fishmonger — a middle-aged man in a heavy yellow rubber apron over a white tee, dark rubber boots — cleaver raised high, mid-motion above a large fish on a thick wooden block. Water puddled across the ground, some reflecting overhead light. Bare fluorescent tubes hanging from the high concrete ceiling on wires. The stall next door visible on the right: wooden crates of bok choy, gai lan, and long white daikon, under a similar fluorescent tube. Two early-morning customers in frame: an older woman in a floral blouse with a red woven shopping bag examining a silver fish on the ice, her back partly to camera. Morning daylight filtering through high skylights in the roof. 35mm film stock, slight grain, neutral color. Sound: air pumps bubbling, a single wet flap of a fish against plastic, the cleaver coming down through bone with a thunk, Cantonese haggling from one stall over, a small radio playing somewhere further back.
thought: Okay, I'm out of the shop, around the corner — landed in a wet market. Fishmonger right at the first stall, big red basins full of water with live fish in there, couple of crabs moving around. Guy's got his cleaver way up over a fish right now. Water all over the floor — must smell like a wet market smells. One lady shopping already, digging through the silver ones on the ice. Let me look at what's next door too.
thought_zh: OK，出了店門，繞過街角——進了一個濕貨市場。第一攤就是賣魚的，大紅桶裡裝滿水，活的魚在裡面，還有幾隻螃蟹在動。老闆現在正把刀高高舉在一條魚上方。地上到處都是水——那一定是濕貨市場那種味道。已經有一個阿姨在翻冰上的那些銀色魚。我也去旁邊那攤看看。
thought_ja: OK、店を出て角を曲がって——生鮮市場に出た。最初の店が鮮魚屋。でかい赤いタライに水いっぱい、中で魚が生きてて、カニも何匹か動いてる。店のおじさんが今ちょうど大きな包丁を魚の上に振りかぶってる。床は水浸し——絶対あの市場特有のにおいしてる。もうお客さんが一人、氷の上の銀色の魚をあさってる。私は隣の屋台も見てみよう。

prompt: A Hong Kong dried-seafood and dried-goods stall in a wet market at mid-morning. The wooden back wall behind the counter is stacked floor to ceiling with tall clear glass jars of dried scallops, dried oysters, dried shrimp, dried abalone, and varieties of dried mushroom — ambers, beiges, deep browns, and black. Below on a long wooden counter at waist height: an array of open plastic bins with metal scoops in them — one bin bright orange dried shrimp, one golden dried shiitake caps, one thin silver dried anchovies, one dark strips of seaweed, a small folded cardboard price tag tucked into each. The elderly stall-owner stands behind the counter: wiry, small, grey cotton vest over a long-sleeved shirt, old metal-frame reading glasses low on his nose, concentrating on a brass hand-held balance scale in which he's weighing a small heap of dried scallops against a brass weight. A calculator and a small wooden abacus lie on the counter beside him. Overhead: the wet market's bare fluorescent tubes. The wooden backdrop glows warmly amid the cold market lighting. 35mm film stock, slight grain, warm amber tones from the wooden wall. Sound: the tiny click of brass weights shifting on the scale, a Cantonese horse-race broadcast playing on a small radio somewhere nearby, a metal scoop tinking against a plastic bin, faint background market chatter.
thought: Oh man — dried seafood next door. Whole wall of glass jars behind the counter, scallops, oysters, shrimp, mushrooms, every shade of amber and brown. Bins with scoops in them along the front. Owner's an old guy with reading glasses, weighing something out on one of those little brass balance scales. Must smell insane in there. Horse race on the radio somewhere. I want to get closer to those jars.
thought_zh: 哇——隔壁是乾貨攤。老闆後面整面牆都是玻璃罐，干貝、乾蠔、蝦米、各種菇，琥珀到深褐一整輪。前面擺了一排大塑膠盒，裡頭插著勺子。老闆是一個戴老花眼鏡的老先生，用那種小小的銅天平在秤什麼。裡面的味道肯定爆棚。某個地方電台在放賽馬。我要湊近看那些罐子。
thought_ja: うわ——隣は乾物の店。カウンターの後ろの壁いっぱいにガラス瓶がびっしり、干し貝柱、干し牡蠣、干しエビ、いろんなキノコ、琥珀色から濃い茶色までのグラデーション。前には大きなプラスチックの箱がずらっと並んでて、柄杓が突っ込んである。店主は老眼鏡をかけたおじいちゃんで、ちっちゃい真鍮の天秤で何かを量ってる。中の匂い、絶対やばいでしょ。どっかのラジオで競馬中継やってる。あの瓶のとこまで近づきたい。

prompt: Extreme tight close-up of an elderly man's weathered hand gripping a small stainless-steel kitchen scoop, lifting a heap of bright orange dried shrimp from an open clear plastic bin, a small cascade of shrimp already mid-fall back into the bin below, each tiny curled body distinct and catching warm light. His bony wrist with prominent tendons and the faded cuff of a grey cotton shirt visible above the hand. The bin fills the lower frame with a mass of orange, slightly softer in depth. Just behind, out of tight focus: the glow of amber glass jars on a wooden shelf and a hint of the brass balance scale. 35mm film stock, slight grain, warm amber color, shallow depth of field with the scoop and shrimp razor sharp. Sound: the papery rattle of dried shrimp against the scoop, a faint brass weight click, the Cantonese horse-race broadcast still going on somewhere in the background.
thought: Okay, closer. He's scooped three out — they're actually pretty big. Plump, orange-red, curled. Not the tiny dried kind, more like those whole-body prawns. Pile of them in the bin below. His hands are all tendons, doesn't even look at what he's doing. Clock on the wall behind him. Horse race still going somewhere. These are the good ones.
thought_zh: OK，靠近一點。他剛剛舀起了三隻——其實還蠻大隻的耶。飽滿，橘紅色，捲起來的。不是那種很小的蝦米，比較像整隻連殼的乾蝦。桶子裡還堆一堆。他那雙手全是筋，根本沒在看自己在幹嘛。後面牆上有個時鐘。賽馬還在某處放著。這一批真的很好。
thought_ja: OK、近づいた。今ちょうど三匹すくい上げたとこ——けっこうでかいな、これ。ぷりっとしてて、オレンジ赤、ぐるっと丸まってる。あの小さい干しエビじゃなくて、殻ごとの丸ごと干しエビっぽい。箱の中にもごっそり積まれてる。おじいちゃんの手は筋だらけで、自分の手元を全然見てない。後ろの壁に時計。競馬はどこかでまだ流れてる。これ、いいやつ。

prompt: Traditional Chinese ink wash painting (水墨) of Hong Kong's Aberdeen harbor in morning mist. Mid-ground: a small wooden sampan boat, a hunched figure at the stern wearing a conical straw hat, one long oar trailing in the water. Two traditional wooden Chinese junks with dark sails farther out, partially dissolved in wet mist, only the mast lines and hull curves visible. In the far background, barely visible through the fog: the ghosted silhouettes of modern Hong Kong high-rise apartment towers, the faint rectangular outlines just a few ink tones darker than the surrounding mist — an understated collision of old and new. Water in the lower foreground suggested with horizontal dry-brush strokes. Ink on white rice paper texture. Soft wet-on-wet brushwork for the mist and water; crisp calligraphic dry-brush lines for the boat edges and oar. Mostly empty negative space in the upper half of the composition. A single small red hanzi seal stamp in the lower right corner. Sound: quiet water lapping against wood, a distant low ferry horn carrying across the water, the single creak of an oar.
thought: Alright — wanted to try this one in ink. Aberdeen harbor I think? Sampan right in front with the guy in the straw hat, one oar out. Two junks farther out half-dissolved in fog. And back behind all the mist you can just barely see the high-rises — like somebody forgot which century this is. Looks different painted this way. Let me stay in it a while.
thought_zh: 欸——這一段想用水墨畫看看。香港仔避風塘吧？前面就是那艘舢舨，戴斗笠的人在划，一支槳伸在外面。再遠一點兩艘木帆船，一半化在霧裡。再後面的高樓幾乎看不到——感覺像有人搞不清楚這是哪個世紀。畫成這樣整個不一樣。我在這裡面待一下。
thought_ja: そうだ、このシーンは水墨でやってみたい。アバディーンの港？ 目の前には舢板、笠をかぶった人が櫓を漕いでて、一本の櫂が水の外に出てる。もう少し先に木造のジャンクが二艘、半分霧に溶けてる。その奥にうっすらと高層ビルが見える——誰かが「今なに世紀だっけ」って混乱したみたい。絵で描くと全然違うな。ちょっとこの中にいよう。

prompt: Traditional Chinese ink wash (水墨) painting aesthetic preserved throughout. Static held camera on the harbor scene. Subtle motions: the small sampan drifts slightly sideways with the current, its single long oar dipping and rising once from the water with a slow creak, faint ripples spreading outward in calligraphic arcs. The far junk with the dark sails stays almost motionless, the mainsail rippling slightly once. The mist slowly thickens in the mid-distance and thins again over eight seconds. The ghosted high-rises in the far background remain still, barely visible through the fog. The single red hanzi seal stamp in the lower right corner holds steady. Brushwork texture breathes ever so slightly with wet ink, but the composition holds. Sound: quiet lapping water against a wooden hull, one slow oar creak and dip, a distant low ferry horn carrying across the water, otherwise silence.
thought: Just sitting with it. Oar dips, water goes in ripples, sampan drifts a bit. Mist kind of breathes — gets thicker, thins out, back in. Junks barely move. That low horn goes off way out there. I could sit here forever. But I want to see that guy rowing up close. Let me go to him.
thought_zh: 就這樣坐著。槳下水，水面一圈一圈擴出去，舢舨晃了一下。霧有點在呼吸——變厚一下、散一下、又厚。兩艘木帆船幾乎沒動。那個低低的船笛從遠處又響了一次。我可以一直坐在這裡。但我想靠近看那個划船的人。過去找他。
thought_ja: そのまま座ってる。櫂が水に入って、波紋が広がって、舢板がちょっと揺れる。霧がなんか呼吸してるみたい——濃くなったり薄くなったり、また濃くなったり。ジャンクはほとんど動いてない。あの低い船の汽笛が、遠くでまたひとつ鳴った。ずっとここにいてもいい。でもやっぱりあの漕いでる人、近くで見たい。行ってみよう。

prompt: Tight close-up in traditional Chinese ink wash (水墨) style. The sampan rower in foreground, waist-up: wearing a conical straw hat with visible woven texture, a dark loose work shirt, weathered tanned face partly shadowed by the hat brim, mouth set, lines at the corners of his eyes, both weathered hands gripping a long wooden oar held horizontally across his body, mid-stroke. Brushstrokes visible in the weave of the hat, the folds of the cloth, the grain of the oar, the tendons on his hands. Water behind him suggested with soft dry-brush horizontal strokes and wet ink ripples. Behind him, slightly dissolved in mist, the lower hull and one dark sail of a traditional wooden Chinese junk. A single touch of color in the whole image: a small piece of red cloth knotted at his waist. White negative space fills the upper right. A single small red hanzi seal stamp in the lower right corner. Ink on rice-paper texture. Sound: water lapping against wood, the creak of wet rope, a distant junk's rigging clinking.
thought: Closer. He's weathered — hat brim hides his eyes but his mouth is set. Both hands on the oar mid-stroke. There's a tiny knot of red cloth at his waist, only bit of color in the whole picture. You can see the brush strokes in the folds of his shirt. Junk just behind him, half in the fog. I wanna know where he's headed.
thought_zh: 近一點。他看起來很曬——斗笠的帽簷遮住眼睛，但嘴巴是抿著的。兩隻手抓著槳，划到一半。腰上綁了一小塊紅布，是整張畫裡唯一的顏色。他衣服皺摺裡都看得到筆觸。木帆船就在他後面，一半在霧裡。我想知道他要去哪。
thought_ja: 近い。この人、日に焼けてる——笠のつばに目が隠れてるけど、口はきゅっと結んでる。両手で櫂をつかんで、漕ぎの途中。腰に赤い布が小さく結んである、画面の中で唯一の色。服のしわに筆のあとが見える。ジャンクは背後に、半分霧のなか。どこに向かってるのか見たい。

prompt: A small traditional wooden Chinese sampan with a rower in a conical straw hat and dark loose shirt is pulling up alongside a modern concrete working pier in Aberdeen harbor, Hong Kong, at early morning. A mooring rope just tossed from the sampan is mid-air, about to be caught by a dockworker standing on the pier — middle-aged Chinese man in an orange high-visibility safety vest and hard hat, clipboard tucked under one arm, his other hand reaching down. Behind the pier: a modern Aberdeen floating seafood restaurant lit up with red neon Chinese characters still on from the night, fiberglass fishing boats moored in a cluster, a diesel gas pump on the pier. In the background, Aberdeen's high-rise apartment towers catching first sun on their upper floors. A single strand of morning mist still trailing across the water. The sampan's weathered wooden planks meet the pier's concrete in the mid-frame. 35mm film stock, slight grain, cool blue-hour light just beginning to warm. Sound: the wet slap of rope on concrete, a distant outboard motor, the dockworker calling something in Cantonese, a seabird's flapping wings.
thought: Okay, figured out where he was going — pulling up to an actual concrete pier. Guy in a hi-vis vest and hard hat catching the rope, clipboard under his arm. Neon floating restaurant behind the pier, still lit up from last night. Sampan rope just hit the concrete. Two times jammed into one picture. Alright, I'm out of the painting, back in the real world.
thought_zh: OK，搞清楚他要去哪了——靠的是一座真的水泥碼頭。碼頭上一個穿螢光背心、戴安全帽的人接繩子，夾板夾在腋下。碼頭後面一家霓虹燈的水上餐廳，昨晚的燈還亮著。繩子剛剛甩到水泥地上。兩個時代硬塞進同一張畫面。OK，我從畫裡出來了，回到真實世界。
thought_ja: OK、どこに向かってたのか分かった——ほんもののコンクリートの桟橋だ。桟橋には蛍光オレンジのベストとヘルメットの人が立ってて、脇にクリップボードを挟みながら、ロープを受け取ろうとしてる。その向こうにネオンの水上レストラン、前の晩の灯りがまだ点いてる。ロープが今ちょうどコンクリートに当たった。二つの時代が一枚にぎゅっと詰まってる。OK、絵から出てきた、現実に戻ってきた。

prompt: Close-up looking down into the open wooden hold of a Hong Kong sampan tied up to a concrete pier in early morning. Inside the small hold: a woven bamboo basket containing six silver fish with mouths slightly open and scales glistening wet; a red plastic bucket holding one live octopus whose pale tentacles are reaching up over the rim; two dark-green live lobsters with rubber-banded claws lying on wet dark seaweed fronds; a small clear plastic container of tiny live grey shrimp. Everything is wet, with a puddle of seawater collecting in the bottom of the wooden hold. The rower's weathered brown hand and forearm reaching in from the top of the frame to lift out the bamboo basket by its rope handle. The shadow of the pier's edge and of the hi-vis dockworker falls diagonally across the hold. The wood of the sampan's interior dark and weathered, with one chipped coat of faded red paint on a rib. 35mm film stock, slight grain, cool morning light with warm reflections off the water. Sound: wet fish sliding slightly against bamboo, the faint slap of an octopus tentacle against plastic, a dull wooden creak of the sampan shifting against the pier, distant city sounds.
thought: Oh — here's the haul. Six silver fish in a bamboo basket, octopus trying to climb out of a red bucket, two lobsters with their claws taped. Some tiny grey shrimp. Everything's wet, seawater pooled at the bottom of the hold. His hand's going for the basket. So that's why he rowed in — morning delivery.
thought_zh: 欸——這就是漁獲。六條銀魚裝在竹籃裡，章魚想從紅桶爬出來，兩隻龍蝦的鉗子都用橡皮筋綁著。還有一點點小灰蝦。全是濕的，船艙底有一層海水。他的手伸下來抓那個竹籃。原來他是來送貨的——晨間配送。
thought_ja: おお——これが朝の水揚げか。竹かごに銀色の魚が六匹、赤いバケツから章魚が這い上がろうとしてて、ロブスターは二匹、ハサミをゴムで縛られてる。ちっちゃい灰色のエビもちょっと。ぜんぶ濡れてて、船底に海水がたまってる。彼の手が竹かごを取りに伸びてる。なるほど——漕いできたのは朝の納品だったわけか。

prompt: Interior of a small old-fashioned Hong Kong traditional Chinese medicine shop (藥材店) in mid-morning, viewed from the customer's side of the wooden counter. The back wall is a tall dark-wooden apothecary cabinet with hundreds of small square labeled drawers arranged in a tight grid, each brass drawer-pull worn smooth, Chinese characters painted on each drawer in old calligraphic script. Adjacent wall: large clear glass jars holding dried herbs, coiled dried ginseng roots arranged on a small shelf, a tall sealed jar on a high shelf containing a coiled preserved snake in yellow medicinal liquor. On the counter itself: a small brass balance scale, a mortar and pestle with a little pile of ground herbs, a neat stack of folded brown paper packets ready to be filled. Behind the counter the elderly herbalist stands: thin, in a grey silk changshan, round gold-rimmed reading glasses low on his nose, one of the drawers pulled halfway open and his fingers reaching inside measuring out a pinch of herbs by feel, not looking. A small boxy radio on a shelf to his side. Overhead: warm tungsten bulbs and a slow wooden ceiling fan. 35mm film stock, slight grain, warm amber-gold color palette, some motes of dust in a beam of morning light. Sound: a wooden drawer scraping slowly open, faint paper rustle, a scratchy Cantonese opera tune on a small radio, the slow tick-tick of the ceiling fan, a distant street outside.
thought: Different place. Chinese medicine shop — whole back wall is these little wooden drawers with characters painted on them, hundreds of them. Herbalist in a silk changshan and tiny gold-rimmed glasses, one drawer pulled open, his hand in there measuring herbs by feel, not even looking. Jars everywhere, including one on the top shelf with a preserved snake coiled up in yellow liquor. Cantonese opera on the radio. Fan turning real slow. Smells incredible in here, I bet.
thought_zh: 換地方了。中藥店——整面後牆全是那種寫著字的小木抽屜，幾百個。老闆穿著灰色絲質長衫，戴著金邊小圓眼鏡，一個抽屜拉開一點，手伸進去用摸的量藥，根本沒在看。到處都是罐子，最上層還有一罐泡在黃色藥酒裡的蛇。收音機放著粵劇。吊扇轉得超慢。裡面一定超級香。
thought_ja: 場所が変わった。漢方薬局——後ろの壁いっぱいに字が書かれた小さな木の引き出し、何百個もある。店主は灰色の絹の長衫にゴールドの細フレームの丸眼鏡、引き出しを少し開けて、手を突っ込んで感覚だけで薬草を計ってる、見もしないで。瓶だらけ、いちばん上の棚には黄色い薬酒に蛇が一匹漬けてある。ラジオから粤劇が流れてる。天井扇はすごくゆっくり回ってる。中、絶対めっちゃいい匂いしてる。

prompt: Continued interior of the small old Hong Kong Chinese medicine shop. Static held camera on the elderly herbalist behind his wooden counter. He finishes weighing a small pinch of dried herbs on a hand-held brass balance scale, gives a small satisfied nod, then gently tips the herbs from the tray onto a square of folded brown paper laying on the counter, reaching slowly with his other hand toward another of the many small drawers behind him. His gold-rimmed reading glasses catch a tungsten reflection. The wooden ceiling fan blades make one slow sweep across the upper frame once. The apothecary drawers behind him remain still. The glass jars on the shelves remain still. 35mm film stock, slight grain, warm amber tones. Sound: a drawer scraping open, a faint pinch of herbs falling on paper, a small breath from the herbalist, the slow tick-tick of the ceiling fan, the scratchy Cantonese opera tune continuing on the small radio.
thought: He's finishing up. Tipped the herbs onto a piece of brown paper — folds it just so, like he's done it ten thousand times. Little nod to himself. Now he's reaching for another drawer. Radio keeps going, fan barely moving. I don't know who this is for but they're gonna get a good prescription.
thought_zh: 他快結束了。把藥草倒在一張牛皮紙上——那個摺法像是已經摺過一萬遍。自己點了一下頭。現在又去拉另一個抽屜。收音機還在唱，扇子還是慢慢轉。不知道這帖是給誰的，但那個人肯定會拿到一帖好方。
thought_ja: 締めに入ってる。薬草を茶色の紙に移してる——折り方がもう何万回やってきた手つき。自分にうなずく。で、また別の引き出しを開けてる。ラジオはずっと流れてて、扇風機はゆっくり。この薬が誰のためかは分からないけど、その人はいい処方を受け取れるね。

prompt: A row of clear plastic bags filled with water hanging on metal hooks across the front of a small Hong Kong goldfish shop on a busy midday street (金魚街, Tung Choi Street, Mongkok). Dozens and dozens of these water-filled bags at varying heights, each containing one or two live tropical fish: plump orange goldfish, black moor goldfish, red betta fish, neon tetras, small silver guppies. Bright midday sun passing through the bags making each one glow like a tiny lens. Behind the bags, the dim interior of the shop visible: tall aquarium tanks stacked in rows with blue-green water, bubbling air stones. On the narrow sidewalk in the mid-ground, a boy of about seven in a white-shirt school uniform with a backpack has stopped and is pointing up urgently at one particular bag containing a fat orange goldfish. Beside him, his mother in a floral blouse, handbag on her arm, looks down at him with one eyebrow raised, a faint half-smile, clearly mid-negotiation. Other shoppers flowing past on the street. 35mm film stock, slight grain, warm bright midday color. Sound: the constant soft hum of air pumps, kids' voices, the mother saying something firm in Cantonese, pop music from one of the neighboring shops.
thought: Different place again. Goldfish street — every shop front has these plastic bags of water hanging up with one fish in each, hundreds of them, sun lighting them up like little lanterns. Orange, black, red betta, tiny silvers. Kid in a school uniform pointing hard at one specific bag — a fat orange goldfish. Mom's eyebrow up. Been there, kid.
thought_zh: 又換一個地方。金魚街——每一家店前都掛著這些裝著水的塑膠袋，每個裝一條魚，幾百個，陽光透過它們像一盞一盞小燈籠。橘色、黑色、紅鬥魚、小小的銀色。一個穿學校制服的小弟弟用力地指著其中一袋——裡面一條胖胖的橘色金魚。媽媽的眉毛抬起來了。我懂你啦，小朋友。
thought_ja: また別のとこ。金魚通り——どの店の軒先にも水入りのビニール袋がぶら下がってて、中にそれぞれ一匹ずつ魚が入ってる、何百袋もある、太陽の光を通して一つ一つが小さな提灯みたい。オレンジ、黒、赤いベタ、小さな銀色たち。小学生くらいの男の子が制服で、その中の一つの袋を必死に指さしてる——丸々したオレンジの金魚。お母さんの眉がちょっと上がってる。わかるよ、坊や。

prompt: POV from inside a clear plastic water-filled bag hanging on a metal hook at the front of a Hong Kong goldfish shop. The bag's gentle spherical lens-distortion bends the view outward at the edges like a fish-eye lens. Through the wet bag, looking outward onto the sidewalk: a young Chinese boy about seven years old in a white school-uniform shirt very close to the viewer, pointing his index finger directly at the camera (at the viewer, through the bag), eyes wide, mouth open talking, his face slightly enlarged by the water lens and warped. Just behind his shoulder, his mother in a floral blouse, handbag strap on her shoulder, head tilted with an appraising expression. On the peripheral edges of the frame, stretched and smeared by the distortion, other passing shoppers and the bright midday street. One other plastic bag visible peripherally at an offset angle, with a little shape of another fish in it. A few tiny air bubbles floating across the view. 35mm film stock, slight grain, warm midday color, soft focus around the edges from the water. Sound: voices heard through water as muffled, the hum of a nearby air pump loud and close, a gurgle of the water moving, the plastic bag creaking ever so slightly as it swings.
thought: Let me try being the goldfish for a sec. — Okay, I'm in the bag. The kid's face is huge right there, he's pointing right at me. Whole world bends around the edges — his mom's kind of stretched, everyone behind her smeared. Everything's muffled, sounds like I'm underwater. Which I am, I guess. I dunno about getting picked though.
thought_zh: 我試試看當金魚。——OK，我在袋子裡了。小弟弟的臉超大地就在我前面，手指直直指著我。整個世界沿著袋子的邊緣彎掉——他媽媽有一點被拉長，後面的人整個糊成一片。所有聲音都變悶悶的，像在水裡。嗯，我確實是在水裡。被選走到底好不好呢？
thought_ja: 金魚になってみよう。——えー、袋の中にいる。男の子の顔が目の前にでっかく映って、指が私にまっすぐ向いてる。世界の端が袋の水で歪んでて——お母さんがちょっと伸びて、その後ろの人みんな滲んでる。音がぜんぶこもってる、水の中みたい。まあ、実際水の中なんだけど。買われるの、どうかな......

prompt: On a narrow Hong Kong goldfish-street sidewalk at midday, a young Chinese boy of about seven in a white school-uniform shirt walks excitedly down the street toward the camera, holding a clear plastic water-filled bag out proudly in front of him with both small hands, gripping the knotted top. Inside the bag: one single fat orange-and-white goldfish suspended, the water sloshing visibly, the goldfish pointed forward. His backpack is on his back, one strap slipping. Two steps behind him walks his mother in the same floral blouse and handbag, holding a folded paper receipt in her hand, her expression a gentle resigned half-smile. Other shoppers passing on both sides. The background is the row of other hanging bags on the shop front and other passers-by with shopping bags. 35mm film stock, slight grain, warm midday color. Sound: the plastic bag crackling as it swings, a wet slosh of water, the boy's excited Cantonese voice saying something about the fish, the mother's single quiet sigh, street traffic hum.
thought: Well — I got picked. Apparently I got a friend too, he's got a bag in each hand. Kid's beaming like he won the lottery. Mom's right behind him with the receipt, face like "we're really doing this." Water sloshing every step. I guess we're going home now. Okay, I'll go.
thought_zh: 結果——我被選中了。看來還多了一個同伴，他兩隻手一手一袋。小朋友笑得像中樂透。媽媽在後面拿著收據，那種「我們真的要做這個嗎」的表情。水一直在身邊搖來搖去。看來要回家了。OK，那就跟著走吧。
thought_ja: 結局——選ばれちゃった。仲間もいるっぽい、男の子が両手にひと袋ずつ握ってる。小さい子、宝くじ当たったみたいな顔で笑ってる。お母さんは後ろでレシート持って、「ほんとにこれやるのか」って顔。水がずっとぱしゃぱしゃ揺れてる。ってことは家に帰るのか。いいよ、ついていくよ。

prompt: Afternoon sun on a rooftop vegetable garden atop a ten-story Hong Kong public housing block. Grid of wooden and battered styrofoam planter boxes with bok choy, lettuce, chili pepper plants with small green chilis, green onions growing tall, one tomato plant tied to a bamboo stake. Chain-link fence around the rooftop edge. An elderly woman (auntie) in a practical blue cotton work shirt, wide-brimmed straw sun hat, loose navy cotton trousers, and rubber-soled shoes is bent slightly over one of the planters, a small metal watering can in her right hand, her left hand parting some leaves to check underneath. A tabby cat lounges on a warm concrete paver a few feet to her left, one paw extended. Past the fence, the view: the cluttered rooftops of neighboring housing blocks with their grey water tanks, white satellite dishes, and laundry lines of clothes, and the hazy blue silhouettes of distant Hong Kong hills beyond. Late afternoon warm slanting light, long soft shadows across the concrete. 35mm film stock, slight grain, warm color palette, soft focus depth on the distant rooftops. Sound: a light breeze through leaves, the soft sprinkle from the watering can, one cicada steady in the distance, a muffled loudspeaker announcement rising from the street far below.
thought: Moved on. I'm up on some housing block rooftop now, maybe ten stories. There's a whole vegetable garden going — bok choy, lettuce, chilis, green onions, one tomato staked up. Auntie in a big sun hat with a little watering can, checking under her leaves. Tabby cat stretched out on the concrete next to her. Other rooftops behind the fence, laundry, water tanks, hills fading into the haze. Afternoon light's getting slanty. Quiet up here.
thought_zh: 移動了。我現在在某個國宅的屋頂，大概十樓高。上面居然有一整個菜園——白菜、萵苣、辣椒、青蔥，還有一株用竹竿綁起來的番茄。阿姨戴著大大的草帽，拿著一個小水壺，翻葉子底下檢查。一隻虎斑貓在旁邊的水泥地上攤著。圍牆後面是其他大樓的屋頂、晾著衣服、水塔、後面的山融進煙靄裡。下午的光漸漸斜了。這裡好安靜。
thought_ja: 移動した。今どっかの公営住宅の屋上、たぶん十階くらい。屋上に野菜畑がまるごとある——白菜、レタス、唐辛子、青ねぎ、竹で支えたトマトが一本。おばさんが大きな麦わら帽子をかぶって、小さいじょうろで葉っぱの下を確認してる。トラ猫が隣のコンクリートの上でだらっとしてる。フェンスの向こうには他の団地の屋上、洗濯物、給水タンク、その奥の山が霞に溶けてる。午後の光が斜めになってきた。ここ、静かだな。

prompt: Low-angle POV from a cat lying on warm afternoon concrete on a Hong Kong rooftop vegetable garden. Immediate foreground (slightly soft focus): one tabby cat paw extended forward in frame, fine fur visible. Mid-ground in sharp focus: the weathered wooden side of a planter box filled with bok choy leaves, some leaves hanging over the edge; beyond the planter, the auntie's blue cotton-trousered knee and lower leg, the bottom of her metal watering can hanging low mid-sprinkle, her other hand still somewhere in the leaves. Background (slightly soft): the chain-link fence, then the distant rooftops of other housing blocks with their water tanks and laundry catching warm slanting afternoon light. Everything from a very low cat's perspective, about six inches off the concrete. Shallow depth of field. 35mm film stock, slight grain, warm late-afternoon tones. Sound: steady cicada in distance, the soft sprinkling of the watering can nearby, the slow breath of a cat close to microphone, a very distant child's shout rising from the street far below.
thought: Tried to be the cat, ended up right next to her instead. She's sprawled in the sun watching the whole operation. Watering can pouring in the background, auntie's feet in the frame. Bok choy close up, concrete warm. Cicada steady somewhere. Fine, I'll just hang at cat-level.
thought_zh: 本來想變成貓，結果變成就在她旁邊而已。她在陽光底下躺平，整個行程都看著。水壺在後面倒水，阿姨的腳也在畫面裡。白菜貼得近近的，水泥暖暖的。某個地方蟬一直叫。算了，那就在貓的高度待著吧。
thought_ja: 猫になろうとしたら、猫のすぐ隣になっただけだった。その子、陽だまりに寝転がって、全部見てる。うしろでおばさんのじょうろが水を落として、足だけ画面に映ってる。白菜が目の前、コンクリートがあったかい。どっかで蝉がずっと鳴いてる。ま、このまま猫の目線でいるよ。

prompt: Rendered in the style of 1990s Japanese cel animation (Studio Ghibli / late-90s Makoto Shinkai aesthetic): a Hong Kong public-housing-block rooftop garden at late afternoon turning into dusk. The scene drawn with clean cel-animated line art, flat color fills, careful shadow shading. The same elderly auntie in a blue cotton work shirt, straw sun hat, loose navy trousers, holding a metal watering can down at her side now — she's turned away from the planter and looking up at the sky with her other hand shading her eyes. The tabby cat still drawn on the concrete, stretching leisurely, oblivious. Overhead: a dramatic sky of enormous cumulus clouds piling up, underlit in saturated pinks, apricots, and golds by the low sun, with a wedge of deep indigo storm-cloud rolling in from the left edge. The chain-link fence, wooden planter boxes with bok choy, distant housing-block rooftops with their water tanks rendered in flat stylized receding layers. Small birds silhouetted against the clouds. Warm painterly background, sharp character lines. Bold, hopeful-melancholy color palette, not photorealistic. Sound: the rising whistle of wind starting to kick up, the auntie's quiet surprised 'aiyah' in Cantonese, a very distant low rumble of thunder, dogs barking somewhere far below.
thought: Let me try this one in anime. — Okay, it's clicking. Sky's going bananas, huge Ghibli clouds piling up over the rooftops, pink and gold underneath, and this dark blue wedge sliding in from the left. Auntie's turned away from her plants looking up, one hand shielding her eyes. Cat's stretching like nothing's happening. Wind picking up. Distant thunder, really far off. Storm's coming in.
thought_zh: 換一下——這一格試試看動畫風。——OK，很有感覺。天空整個瘋了，吉卜力那種大雲團一層一層堆在屋頂上面，粉紅、金色在下面亮，左邊還有一塊深藍色暴雨雲正要進來。阿姨已經轉身不看菜了，手遮著眼睛抬頭看天。貓繼續伸懶腰當沒發生。風開始變大。遠遠聽到一聲雷，超遠。雨要來了。
thought_ja: スタイル切り替え——今回アニメでやってみる。——お、これ合うな。空ヤバいことになってる、ジブリみたいなでっかい雲がもくもく屋上の上に積み上がって、下からピンクと金色が光ってて、左の端から青黒い嵐の雲が入り込んできてる。おばさんはもう野菜から目を離して、手で日除けしながら空を見上げてる。猫はそんなの関係なく伸びをしてる。風が強くなってきた。遠くで雷が一度だけ鳴った、めちゃくちゃ遠いけど。雨来るな。

prompt: Interior of a Hong Kong double-decker tram (ding ding) at dusk, upper deck, moving through Central or Wan Chai in heavy rain. Camera positioned toward the front of the upper deck. The large front-facing window running with rivulets of rainwater, distorted reflections across the wet glass. Outside through the window: a rain-slicked city street, neon Chinese-character signs in red, pink, green, and yellow smearing and bleeding into the wet glass, the red taillights of taxis passing, pedestrians in a blur hurrying under black umbrellas, wet asphalt reflecting every color. Inside the tram's upper deck: four or five tired-looking passengers on varnished wooden seats, two looking down at their phones, one older man in a grey jacket asleep against the window. A woman in office wear with wet shoes and a folded dripping umbrella is just settling into her seat mid-frame. The old incandescent interior bulbs glow warm yellow and reflect faintly in the wet windows. 35mm film stock, slight grain, contrast between warm interior light and cool wet exterior neon. Sound: the steady bell-like 'ding ding' of the tram's conductor bell, rain drumming on the tram's roof, wet tires on asphalt, the rumble of tram wheels on rails, a recorded Cantonese-then-English stop announcement.
thought: Okay — hard cut. Rain actually broke, I'm on a tram now, upper deck, moving through the wet city. Water running down the front windows, all the neon bleeding into the glass. Lady just sat down with her wet shoes and a dripping folded umbrella. Old guy asleep against the window. Warm old interior lights against all that wet outside. Ding ding going. Didn't plan on being on a tram but here we are.
thought_zh: OK——硬切。雨真的下來了。我現在在叮叮車上，二樓，穿過濕漉漉的城市。前面的窗戶水一直流下來，外面的霓虹燈在玻璃上全化開。一個女生剛剛坐下來，鞋子濕的，折起來的雨傘還在滴水。旁邊一個老先生靠著窗睡著了。車廂裡暖暖的黃燈，跟外面的水形成反差。叮叮叮地響著。本來沒打算上電車，但已經在車上了。
thought_ja: OK、ハードカット。雨、ほんとに降ってきた。今トラムに乗ってる、二階席、濡れた街を進んでる。前の窓に水がずっと流れて、外のネオンがぜんぶガラスの上で滲んでる。女の人が座ったばっかり、濡れた靴、畳んだ傘からまだ水が滴ってる。そばのおじいちゃんは窓に寄りかかって寝てる。車内の黄色いライトがあったかくて、外の濡れた夜とのコントラストが強い。チンチン鳴ってる。トラム乗るつもり全然なかったけど、まあ乗ってる。

prompt: Continued interior of a Hong Kong double-decker tram, upper deck at dusk in heavy rain. Mostly static hold of the scene. Subtle environmental motions: rivulets of water continuing to stream and wriggle down the front window; the tram rolls forward slowly, so the neon signs outside smear and shift slowly from right to left across the glass; a single taxi with red taillights passes by; pedestrians under black umbrellas cross in a blur. Inside, the passengers stay mostly still — the older man in the center seat's head dips forward once as he drifts closer to sleep; the woman with the wet umbrella adjusts her bag on her lap; the incandescent interior bulbs waver very slightly with the tram's motion. Sound: a single 'ding ding' of the tram's bell, steady rain drumming on the metal roof, tram wheels rumbling on rails, tires hissing on wet asphalt, a long rising-and-falling gust of wind, a recorded voice announcing the next stop in Cantonese then English. 35mm film stock, slight grain.
thought: Just riding along. Tram's rolling slow through all that rain, neon keeps sliding past, kind of hypnotic. Old guy's head just dipped forward — getting into the dozing-off place. Voice announcing the next stop in two languages, didn't catch which one. Rain's really coming down now. I don't need to get off anywhere in particular.
thought_zh: 就這樣晃著。電車在雨裡慢慢前進，霓虹一直往後滑，有點催眠。老先生剛剛頭又往前點了一下——差不多要真的睡著了。廣播用兩種語言唸下一站，哪一站我都沒聽清楚。雨下超大。我其實沒特別要在哪一站下車。
