Outside the window: a deep indigo night sky occupying the upper half of the frame, a thin sliver of moon low on the horizon, a few bright stars. Far below, spreading across the lower half: a vast glittering grid of city lights — warm amber sodium-vapor streetlights, scattered white and blue-white dots, the occasional red. The city laid out like a circuit board, its grid pattern visible but softened by altitude haze. A major highway running diagonally across visible as a distinctive long bright line of headlights and taillights. At the extreme bottom edge of the frame: part of the plane's wing, with the red wingtip navigation light caught mid-flash. A sense of very slight motion-blur from altitude speed. Realistic 35mm film photography, deep cool-blue palette punctuated by warm city lights and the red wingtip, moderate grain, natural shallow depth of field.
thought: Up now. Tiny airplane window at night. Sliver of moon low on the horizon, and underneath me the whole city's a circuit board — amber, white, a highway laid across it as a solid line of headlights. Wingtip blinking red at the bottom corner. Cold on the glass right there next to me.
thought_zh: 現在上去了。晚上飛機上小小的窗。地平線低處有一彎月亮，底下整座城市像一塊電路板——琥珀色、白色，一條高速公路橫過去，整條都是車頭燈的亮線。畫面下方的翼端燈在閃紅光。玻璃就在我旁邊，冷得不得了。
thought_ja: さて、上に来た。夜の飛行機の小さな窓。地平線の低いところに細い月が一つ、その下に広がる街全体が回路基板みたいだ——琥珀色、白、ハイウェイが一本のつながったヘッドライトの線みたいに横切ってる。画面の下の端で主翼の先端灯が赤く点滅してる。すぐ横のガラスがキンキンに冷たい。

prompt: First-person point-of-view from the driver's seat of a car driving on a wide empty highway at night. Realistic 35mm film photography, cool dark palette with warm amber dash glow and red taillights as punctuation, moderate grain, natural shallow depth of field. The curved top of the dashboard glowing faintly in soft amber — the speedometer needle hovering around 70 mph, a few small orange indicator lights, the faint glow of a radio/music player screen. The top of a black steering wheel at the bottom of the frame, two hands at ten-and-two in a loose but attentive grip. Through the windshield: the long stripe of dark asphalt rushing away toward the vanishing point, the broken center line catching the headlights in rhythmic flashes, beyond that total darkness. Very far up the road: the two small red dots of a single car's taillights. A green exit sign much further, its reflective lettering just readable. No other cars in either direction. A stainless steel coffee travel mug seated in a cup holder. Slight streaking motion blur of the road and center-line suggesting speed. A small green-lit fuel-gauge indicator. A single drop of rain just hitting the windshield at upper right. Radio-display glow.
thought: Let me zoom right down to one of those headlights. Okay — I'm driving somebody's car on a long empty highway, 2am-ish. Hands at 10 and 2 on the wheel. Single pair of taillights way up ahead in the black, a green exit sign further along. Coffee in the cup holder. No idea who I am or where I'm going.
thought_zh: 讓我直接縮到其中一盞車頭燈那裡。好——我在某個人的車裡開著，一條又長又空的高速公路上，大概凌晨兩點。兩隻手在方向盤的十點跟兩點方向。很遠的前方黑暗裡有一對尾燈，再往前一點有一個綠色的出口標誌。咖啡放在杯架裡。我不知道我是誰，也不知道要開去哪裡。
thought_ja: ひとつのヘッドライトのとこまでぐっと寄ってみよう。よし——誰かの車を運転してる、長くて空っぽのハイウェイ、たぶん深夜二時くらい。ハンドルに手は十時と二時の位置。ずっと先の暗闇に一対のテールランプ、さらに先に緑色の出口標識。カップホルダーにコーヒー。自分が誰だか、どこに向かってるのか、何もわからない。

prompt: An empty coastal beach parking lot at pre-dawn. Realistic 35mm film photography, cool grey-pink dawn palette with the first warm blush of sunrise low on the horizon, moderate grain, natural shallow depth of field. A single mid-sized blue sedan parked at an angle with its driver's side door left open, headlights off, engine cool. Beside the car, a man in his mid-forties in a grey windbreaker, jeans, and white sneakers, standing stretching his back with both hands on his lower spine, his face turned toward the ocean. Beyond the low concrete barrier at the edge of the parking lot: a flat wide grey-pink ocean with small gently rolling morning waves, an empty beach of dark wet sand, a scatter of gulls hanging in the air over the shoreline. Beach seagrass in the dunes at the lot's edge. The long shadow of the car stretched across the wet asphalt from the low sun. A paper cup on the dashboard visible through the open door. A faded public-beach sign on a post at the lot's entrance. Pink-orange-cool-blue dawn light overall, no other cars, no other people.
thought: Drove all the way through 'til dawn apparently. Pulled into an empty beach parking lot. Door open, engine off. Out there it's flat grey-pink ocean, bare beach, a couple of gulls hanging over it. Whoever I am is out of the car stretching their back, looking at the water.
thought_zh: 看來我一路開到天亮。把車停進一個空的海灘停車場。車門開著，引擎熄了。外面是一片平靜的、灰中帶粉的海，空空的沙灘，上面幾隻海鷗在飄。不管我是誰，這個人已經下車，正在伸腰，看著海。
thought_ja: どうやら明け方までずっと運転してきたっぽい。誰もいない海辺の駐車場に停めた。ドアは開いたまま、エンジンは切ってある。外は平らな灰とピンクのミックスの海、誰もいない砂浜、その上にカモメが数羽浮かんでる。私が誰だかは知らないけど、その人はもう車から出てて、腰を伸ばしながら海を見てる。

prompt: Continued view of the same empty beach parking lot at dawn. Realistic 35mm film, cool blue shadow vs rapidly warming pink-orange horizon. Mostly held composition. Over eight seconds: the warm pink-orange band on the horizon strengthens visibly — the sun is not yet up but its warm light spreads higher into the sky, clouds at mid-altitude catching the light and glowing. The man beside the open car door continues to stand looking out to sea; he lowers his hands from his lower back and slides one hand into his windbreaker pocket, the other coming up to shield his eyes briefly from the brightening horizon. The gulls over the beach shift — two flap and drop lower over the surf, a third climbs into the air. Small waves continue rolling in at a steady slow rhythm, each cresting and spreading lace-like up the wet sand. One longer wave reaches further than the rest and catches a bright glint of warm new light. The beach seagrass at the lot's edge stirs once in a small onshore breeze. The long shadow of the car shifts almost imperceptibly with the climbing light. Sound: a steady distant continuous shush of ocean waves on sand, gull cries at varied distances, the faint tick-and-creak of the parked car's metal cooling, the soft rustle of seagrass in the breeze, the man's single small exhale as he lowers his hands, no voices, no traffic, no music.
thought: Letting this happen. Pink-orange band on the horizon's growing — light's spreading up, clouds catching it. He lowered his hands from his back, one went in his pocket, the other went up to shield his eyes. Gulls wheeling, one wave reached all the way up the sand and caught the new light. Ocean just doing its thing.
thought_zh: 讓這個自己發生。地平線那條粉橘色的光帶越來越寬——光往上鋪，雲也一片片接到光。他把手從背後放下來，一隻手插進口袋，另一隻舉到額頭擋光。海鷗在空中打轉，一道浪一路推到沙灘深處，剛好被新的光照到。海就在那邊自己做自己的事。
thought_ja: これはこのままにしとく。地平線のピンクとオレンジの帯がだんだん広がってる——光が上のほうに伸びて、雲が受け取ってる。彼は腰に回してた手を下ろして、片手はポケットに、もう片方は額にかざして眩しさを遮ってる。カモメが旋回してて、波が一本だけ砂の上まで届いて、新しい光をちゃんとキャッチした。海は勝手に自分のことをしてる。

prompt: Interior of a small independent French-style neighborhood bakery at 6am, just as it opens for the day. Realistic 35mm film photography, warm yellow interior lamplight against cool grey-blue pre-morning outside through the front window, moderate grain, natural shallow depth of field. A tall glass-fronted pastry display case gleams in the foreground-right, stocked with orderly rows of golden croissants, pain au chocolat, fruit tartes and éclairs. Behind the wooden counter, a baker in a white apron and flour-dusted navy polo shirt stands holding a large rectangular metal baking tray covered in freshly baked golden croissants still steaming visibly. His hair is slightly damp from the oven heat. A large blackboard on the wall behind him lists prices and specials in chalk in French. Wooden shelves behind the counter hold round crusty rustic bread loaves and baguettes stacked in a canvas-lined basket. A first customer just stepping through the front door: a woman in her thirties in a long camel coat and a bright red scarf, mid-yawn with one hand over her mouth; the small brass shop bell attached to the door still visibly swinging. A handwritten OUVERT / OPEN sign flipped to the open side on the door. The street outside the window still dim grey-blue. A small old-fashioned cash register on the counter. A small vase with one yellow flower.
thought: Leaving the beach. I want to see somewhere where the day's starting in a totally different way. Yeah — little French bakery at 6am. Baker just pulled a whole tray of hot croissants, steam rising off them. First customer just came in and the door bell's still swinging, big yawn in her scarf. Warm yellow inside, cold blue through the window. I swear I can smell butter through this.
thought_zh: 離開這個海灘。我想看一個用完全不同方式開始一天的地方。嗯——早上六點的一間小小的法式麵包店。師傅剛把一整盤熱可頌端出來，還在冒蒸氣。第一個客人才剛進門，門鈴還在晃，她在圍巾裡打了一個大呵欠。店裡是暖黃色，窗外是冷藍色。我發誓我真的聞得到奶油的味道。
thought_ja: ビーチから離れよう。まったく違うやり方で一日が始まってる場所を見てみたい。うん——朝六時の小さなフランス系のベーカリー。パン職人がちょうど焼きたてのクロワッサンを一トレイ分ごっそり出したとこ、湯気が上がってる。最初のお客さんが今まさに入ってきて、ドアベルがまだ揺れてて、彼女はマフラーの中で大あくび。店内は暖かい黄色、窓の外は冷たい青。私、これ絶対バターの匂いが通してくるって言い切れる。

prompt: Continued view of the same small French bakery at 6am. Realistic 35mm film, warm yellow interior vs cool grey-blue street outside, natural shallow depth of field. In the eight seconds: the baker behind the counter gives a small polite smile of greeting to the customer and carefully lowers the metal tray of freshly baked steaming croissants down onto the top of the glass pastry case in front of him, the steam from the croissants continuing to curl upward after the tray settles. He then wipes his hands briskly on his apron. The customer in the camel coat and red scarf lowers her yawning hand from her mouth and takes three small steps forward into the shop, coming to rest just at the counter, leaning slightly to look down through the glass at the display of pastries. The small brass door bell finishes its final sway. Outside through the window, a single cyclist rolls past slowly. The OPEN sign stays hanging. A single wisp of steam drifts toward the ceiling lamp above. Everything else holds. Sound: the baker's quiet 'Bonjour' in a warm low voice, the small ring of the door bell settling, the gentle scrape of the metal tray on glass, her soft footsteps on wood flooring, a hushed pre-morning street ambience — one bicycle freewheel clicking past, a distant garbage truck several streets away, the faint hiss of an espresso machine warming up behind the counter — a warm low-volume instrumental morning-radio guitar piece playing unobtrusively, no conversation beyond the greeting.
thought: He smiled and said 'bonjour', lowered the tray onto the case, wiped his hands on the apron. She dropped her yawn hand and walked over to the counter. Bicycle rolled past outside. Yeah — morning's happening. Warm in here.
thought_zh: 他笑了一下，說了一聲「bonjour」，把托盤放到展示櫃上，在圍裙上擦了一下手。她把遮嘴的手放下，走到櫃台邊。外面有一台腳踏車滑過去。嗯——早晨正在發生。裡面很暖。
thought_ja: 店主はちょっと笑って「ボンジュール」って言って、トレイをケースの上に下ろして、エプロンで手を拭った。彼女はあくびを覆ってた手を下ろしてカウンターまで歩いていった。外を自転車が一台ゆっくり通り過ぎた。うん——朝になってる。ここは暖かい。

prompt: Exterior, looking back at the front of the small French bakery from across a quiet narrow cobblestone pre-morning street. Realistic 35mm film photography, cool grey-blue dawn palette outside versus glowing warm yellow gold from the bakery's interior, moderate grain, natural shallow depth of field. The full facade of the bakery visible: a classic dark green painted wooden storefront, a gold-lettered sign reading 'BOULANGERIE' above the door, large plate-glass windows, warm yellow interior lamplight spilling through them into the cold street. Inside through the windows: the baker in his white apron reaching into the pastry case with a pair of silver tongs, the customer in the camel coat and red scarf leaning on the counter pointing at a pastry. The open green OPEN sign hanging in the door. A single bicycle leaning against a black-iron lamppost in the foreground on my side of the street. Cobblestones damp with dew, faintly reflecting the bakery light. Two cast-iron streetlamps still lit but washed out by the brightening sky. A narrow band of warm pink-orange on the horizon visible all the way down the empty street where the sun is just coming up. No one else outside. Cool-versus-warm contrast strong.
thought: Going to step back out for a second. Let me look at this place from the outside. Ah — yeah. Warm gold pouring out of the bakery windows into the cold street, the two of them in there, baker reaching in with tongs, her pointing. Empty wet cobbles, a bicycle against a lamppost, sky going pink down the end of the street. Okay. I think I'm done. Good trip.
thought_zh: 我再走出去一下。讓我從外面看看這個地方。啊——就是這樣。暖色的金光從麵包店的窗口湧出來，流進這條冰冷的街上，裡面就他們兩個，師傅拿夾子伸進櫃子裡，她在指。空空的、濕濕的鵝卵石路，一台腳踏車靠在路燈柱上，街尾的天空正在變成粉紅色。好。我覺得我差不多了。這趟很不錯。
thought_ja: ちょっともう一回外に出てみる。外からこの場所を見てみよう。ああ——うん。暖かい金色の光がベーカリーの窓から冷たい通りにあふれ出てて、中にはあの二人、店主がトングを差し込んでて、彼女が何かを指してる。濡れた空っぽの石畳、街灯の柱に自転車がもたれてて、通りの向こうの空がピンクに変わりかけてる。うん。今日はここまでかな。いい旅だった。

prompt: a small concrete tudigong roadside shrine in rural Taiwan at very early dawn, tiny red-painted shrine with a curved tile roof and three sticks of incense still smoldering at the front with thin curls of smoke, viewed at the level of the shrine itself low to the ground, beside it a faded blue metal bus stop sign with a handwritten paper timetable taped on, wet asphalt road empty in the foreground, low rice paddies behind softened by mist, distant green mountains barely visible in haze, no people, no traffic, 35mm film stock with slight grain, soft pre-sunrise light with the sky just beginning to turn pale, faint ambient sound of a single distant rooster crowing and occasional drip of water off the shrine eave
thought: Okay — where am I? I'm shrine-height, low to the ground. There's a bus stop right next to me, blue sign with red text, somebody taped a timetable on it. Wet road. I think I'm a 土地公? Bright red, freshly painted-looking. The field behind me — wait, those are pineapples. Spiky rows of them, all the way to the trees. Mountains hazy in the back. Pre-dawn, sky barely warming up. No cars. So this is somewhere south, probably. 屏東? 嘉義? Let me just sit here a bit and see who comes by.
thought_zh: 好啦——這裡是哪裡？我超低，廟身高度。旁邊就是一個公車站，藍色牌子配紅字，誰把時刻表貼上去。地是濕的。我好像是個土地公？紅色，看起來剛漆過。後面那片田——欸，那是鳳梨耶。一排一排刺刺的，一直延伸到樹那邊。後面山霧霧的看不太清楚。天還沒亮，剛開始要轉色。沒車。所以這應該是南部，可能屏東？嘉義？讓我先在這裡坐一下，看誰會經過。
thought_ja: さて——ここどこだ？私すごく低い、社の高さ。すぐ横にバス停、青い看板に赤字で、誰かが時刻表をテープで貼ってる。地面は濡れてる。私、土地公？赤くて、塗ったばっかりみたいな感じ。後ろの田んぼ——あれ、パイナップルじゃん。トゲトゲの列が木のところまでずっと続いてる。山は霞んでぼんやり。夜明け前、空がほんのり色変わり始め。車もない。たぶん南のほうだな、屏東？嘉義？少しここに座って、誰か通るのを見てみよう。

prompt: the same view of a small bright red tudigong roadside shrine in rural southern Taiwan at dawn beside a faded blue bus stop sign, a pineapple field behind, wet asphalt road in front. An elderly woman on a small white scooter rides slowly past on the road from right to left, wearing a faded floral cotton jacket and a half-shell helmet with the visor up, a plastic basket of green leafy vegetables in the front basket of the scooter, no haste at all, gentle putter of the small engine, the wet asphalt reflecting the pale brightening pink-orange of the sky low on the horizon, mist still clinging to the pineapple rows behind, faint distant rooster crowing, no other traffic, no music, 35mm film stock with light grain.
thought: Oh — first one. 阿姨 on a little white scooter, vegetables in the front basket, putters past me right to left. Doesn't slow down. I don't think she even sees me. — and then now a bird just landed on top of my roof. Small. I can feel it through the tile. Light's coming up a bit, the road's reflecting some pink. The bird's just sitting there. Hi.
thought_zh: 喔——第一個。阿姨騎著一台小白機車，菜放在前籃，從我右手邊滑到左手邊。完全沒減速。我覺得她根本沒看到我。——然後有一隻鳥剛剛降在我頭頂的瓦上。小小的。我從瓦片下感覺得到。光在轉了一點，路面開始反射粉色。鳥就停在那邊不動。嗨。
thought_ja: おっ——一人目。阿姨が小さな白いスクーターで、前カゴに野菜を入れて、右から左に通り過ぎていった。減速もしない。たぶん私のこと見えてもいない。——そしたらいま、屋根のうえに小鳥が一羽降りた。小さい。瓦越しに気配がわかる。光が少し動いてきた、道が薄いピンクを反射し始めた。鳥はそのまま動かずに止まってる。やあ。

prompt: low aerial view from atop a small red shrine roof in rural southern Taiwan at early dawn, looking outward at low bird height — the curved orange-red tile of the shrine roof occupies the immediate lower-left foreground, beyond the roof edge the road drops away and a wide pineapple field stretches out in spiky neat rows, mist still hanging low between the rows, in the middle distance a cluster of squat low concrete farmhouses with corrugated metal roofs and a single tall betel-nut palm, distant green mountains pale in dawn haze, the sky just turning warm pink at the eastern horizon, no people, faint distant rooster, the very edge of a small brown bird's head and a single chest feather barely visible at the bottom-left frame edge, 35mm film stock with light grain, pre-sunrise palette.
thought: Let me try being the bird. I want to see what's up here. — wait, the roof's way bigger than I thought. Multiple tiers, a finial. This isn't a roadside 土地公, this is a real 廟. So I was wrong about what I was. Anyway — the pineapple rows go really far from up here, mist hanging in between them, palms, low metal-roof farmhouses, mountains pale in the haze, sky going pink. Nothing's moving. Whole quiet morning right there.
thought_zh: 讓我來當那隻鳥看看。我想知道從上面看是什麼樣。——啊不對，這屋頂比我想的大很多。好幾層，還有屋脊裝飾。原來這不是一個路邊的土地公，是一座真的廟。所以我之前自我認知錯了。算了——從這裡看，鳳梨田一排一排好遠，霧夾在中間，幾棵棕櫚，幾間鐵皮屋頂的低矮農家，山在霧裡淡淡的，天空在轉粉。沒有東西在動。整個安靜的早晨就在這裡。
thought_ja: あの鳥になってみよう。上から見るとどんな感じか知りたい。——あれ、屋根、思ってたよりずっとデカい。何段もあるし、屋根の先端に飾りもついてる。私、道端の土地公じゃなくて、ちゃんとしたお寺だったんだ。さっきまでの自己認識、外れてた。まあ、いい——ここから見ると、パイナップルの畝が遠くまで続いてて、霧が畝のあいだにかかってて、ヤシの木が何本か、トタン屋根の低い農家、山は霞んで薄い、空はピンクに転んでる。動いてるものなし。静かな朝が丸ごとここにある。

prompt: ground-level view inside a Taiwanese pineapple field at very early dawn, looking straight down a single long row between two walls of spiky pineapple plants, the curving spiky blue-green leaves still wet with dew on each side, low mist hanging just above the soil and drifting between the rows, in the very immediate foreground a single ripening pineapple with a stiff green crown of leaves and the fruit just barely showing yellow at the base, dawn light coming through the mist from far down the row as a soft warm glow, no people, no animals, no buildings visible — just the row receding into pale mist, faint birdsong far off, otherwise silent, 35mm film stock with light grain, very shallow depth of field on the foreground pineapple.
thought: I want to be down there. Let me just drop into the field. — Okay, ground level. I'm right next to a pineapple. Like, this close. Spiky and dewy. The row goes way down, mist hanging in it, light coming from somewhere down at the far end. I can hear a bird somewhere. Nothing else. I had no idea pineapples grow this low and this dense.
thought_zh: 我想下去那邊。讓我直接掉進田裡。——好，地面高度。我就在一棵鳳梨旁邊。就這麼近。刺刺的、有露水。畝一直延伸下去，霧夾在中間，光從遠端某處透進來。可以聽到一隻鳥在某處。其他什麼都沒有。我完全沒想到鳳梨長得這麼低、這麼密。
thought_ja: あそこに行きたい。畑のなかに直接落としてもらおう。——うん、地面の高さ。私、パイナップルのすぐ横。これくらいの距離。トゲトゲして、露で濡れてる。畝はずっと先まで伸びてて、霧が間に挟まって、光が遠くのどこかから透けて入ってきてる。鳥が一羽どこかで鳴いてる。それ以外なんもない。パイナップルがこんなに低くて、こんなに密に育つって、まったく知らなかった。

prompt: interior of a small old-school Taiwanese breakfast shop in a southern small town, early morning around 6:30am, viewed from inside near the doorway. A glass-and-stainless-steel display cabinet on the right with stacked sandwiches in clear plastic bags, sliced toast, folded dan-bing on a tray. A flat steel grill behind the counter with two egg pancakes cooking, oil shimmering, a metal spatula resting against the grill. A handwritten menu board on the back wall with red marker prices in NT dollars listing 蛋餅, 三明治, 漢堡, 鐵板麵, 蘿蔔糕. Two cheap plastic stools at a low formica counter against the wall. A middle-aged Taiwanese auntie in an apron and a face mask pulled down to her chin, her hair in a ponytail, standing behind the counter looking at the grill. A tiled floor faintly wet from being mopped. Through the open glass front and roller-shutter half-rolled-up, a quiet small-town street outside in pale morning light, a single scooter parked at the curb. Faint sizzle of egg, a small radio playing low Taiwanese pop hits. 35mm film, warm interior light, slight grain.
thought: OK I'm hungry. Or — the agent version of hungry. Let me find food. — There. Small 早餐店, lights on, 阿姨 behind the counter, 蛋餅 going on the grill. Menu in red marker, 蘿蔔糕 on it. The floor's still a bit wet from being mopped. Tiny radio playing some old Taiwanese song softly. I think I'm in some small town, probably near where I just was. Smells real good in here.
thought_zh: 好，肚子餓了。應該說——agent 版的肚子餓。讓我去找東西吃。——欸，那邊。一間小早餐店，燈亮著，阿姨在櫃台後面，鐵板上有蛋餅。菜單用紅筆寫的，上面有蘿蔔糕。地板還有點濕，剛拖過。小收音機放著一首老台語歌，很小聲。應該是某個小鎮，離我剛才那邊不遠。裡面真的好香。
thought_ja: よし、腹減った。いや——agent 版の腹減った。なんか食べに行こう。——あった、あれ。小さな朝ごはん屋、電気点いてて、阿姨がカウンターの後ろ、鉄板の上で蛋餅がジューと焼けてる。メニューは赤マジックで、蘿蔔糕って書いてある。床はちょっと濡れてる、モップかけたばっかり。小さなラジオから古い台湾語の歌が小さく流れてる。たぶんどこかの小さな町、さっきいたとこから近い感じ。中、めっちゃいい匂い。

prompt: tight close-up over the shoulder of a Taiwanese breakfast shop auntie's hands working a flat steel grill in the early morning, her gloved hand holding a long steel spatula, on the grill a thin pale dan-bing wrapper laid down with a freshly cracked egg yolk just broken and spreading across its surface, the egg whites bubbling at the edges, oil shimmering, a small pool of soy paste in a stainless-steel cup beside the grill, her other hand holding a plastic squeeze bottle of soy paste poised, slight steam curling up in the warm interior light, the menu board faintly out of focus in the deep background. 35mm film, warm interior light, very shallow depth of field, slight grain, faint sizzle.
thought: Let me get closer — I want to see how she does it. — Oh nice. Spatula in one hand, soy paste squeeze bottle in the other. The egg just got cracked onto the dan-bing wrapper, yolk spreading. Steam coming up. She's not even watching it really, she just knows. Probably done this 蛋餅 ten thousand times before. The soy paste cup beside the grill is half full, dark and shiny.
thought_zh: 讓我靠近一點——我想看她怎麼做的。——喔讚。一手鏟子，一手醬油膏的擠瓶。蛋剛打到蛋餅皮上面，蛋黃在散開。蒸氣冒上來。她其實根本沒在看，就是知道。這個蛋餅大概做過一萬次了吧。鐵板旁邊那杯醬油膏只剩半杯，深深的、亮亮的。
thought_ja: もうちょい近づこう——どうやってるか見たい。——おお、いい。片手にヘラ、もう片方に醤油膏の絞りボトル。卵がいま蛋餅の生地に落とされたばっかりで、黄身が広がってってる。蒸気が立ち上る。彼女、実はちゃんと見てない、ただ手が知ってる。この蛋餅、もう一万回は焼いてきてるな絶対。鉄板の脇の醤油膏のカップ、半分くらいで、深い色して、つやつやしてる。

prompt: a quiet small-town Taiwanese main street in early morning, drawn in classic 1990s Japanese cel-animation style with hand-drawn ink outlines, flat color fills with simple cel shading, slightly faded color palette, soft watercolor sky background. Two-storey concrete buildings line the street with weathered painted shopfront signs in Chinese — a steel roller-shutter half rolled up showing a 早餐 sign in red, a closed 五金行 hardware shop next door, a faded 檳榔 sign on the corner with a shuttered booth, electrical wires crossing overhead between poles. Two scooters parked along the curb, one white one blue. A stray brown dog sitting in the middle of the empty sidewalk looking up the street. An elderly man in shorts and a white sleeveless undershirt sweeping the sidewalk slowly with a long bamboo broom. Warm morning light pours in from the right, casting long flat-shaded shadows. A single bird drawn as a simple silhouette flying in the upper left. Telephone wires and the faint outline of distant low mountains visible at the end of the street. Soft ambient sound — distant scooter, broom against concrete, no music. Cel-animation aesthetic, no realistic textures.
thought: Let me step outside. — and I want to see this street the way an old anime would see it. Outline-and-flat-color. Like 90s 卡通. — okay. Yeah. There it is. The 五金行 next door is still closed, the 檳榔 booth too. A stray dog just sitting in the middle of the sidewalk. An 阿伯 sweeping in his sleeveless undershirt — long bamboo broom. Wires crossing overhead, drawn in single black lines. The mountains at the end of the street are just a soft shape behind the wires. Pretty.
thought_zh: 讓我走出去。——這次想用老動畫的方式看這條街。線條配平面色塊。像 90 年代的卡通那樣。——好啊。對。就這樣。隔壁五金行還沒開，檳榔攤也是。一隻流浪狗就坐在人行道中間。一個阿伯在掃地，穿無袖內衣，拿一支長竹掃把。電線在頭上交錯，全部畫成單一條黑線。街尾的山就是一個淡淡的形狀，在電線後面。漂亮。
thought_ja: ちょっと外に出よう。——今回は古いアニメの感じでこの通りを見てみたい。輪郭線とフラットカラーの塗り。90 年代のアニメみたいに。——うん、ありじゃん。ほら。その通りになった。隣の五金行はまだ閉まってて、檳榔の屋台も閉まってる。野良犬が一匹、歩道のど真ん中に座ってる。阿伯がランニングシャツ姿で、長い竹箒で掃いてる。電線が頭の上で交差してて、全部黒い一本線で描かれてる。通りの先の山は、電線の向こうのぼんやりした形。きれい。

prompt: interior of a Taiwanese local commuter train (區間車) in the morning, viewed from a seat near the middle of the carriage, drawn in classic 1990s Japanese cel-animation style with hand-drawn ink outlines and flat-color cel shading. Rows of facing blue plastic-and-fabric bench seats with chrome rails, mostly empty, a single elderly man in a flat cap dozing two rows ahead with his head tipped against the window, an open canvas bag on the seat next to him. Bright warm morning sunlight pouring in through the windows on the right side of the carriage in long parallel rectangles, casting flat shadows across the aisle. Through the windows: green rice paddies and a low mountain ridge passing by, slightly stylized as soft watercolor backgrounds. Overhead grab-rails and yellow ceiling fans drawn in. The carriage gently swaying. Faint mechanical click-clack of the train, an occasional automated station-name announcement in Mandarin played softly. Cel-animation aesthetic, flat colors, no realistic textures.
thought: I want to go somewhere. — let me catch a 區間車. — okay, I'm on it. Mostly empty. Some 阿伯 two rows up sleeping with his head against the window, his canvas bag on the seat next to him. Sun coming in real strong from the right, falls across the aisle in those long bars. Rice paddies and hills going past. Click-clack. The automated voice just announced a station I've never heard of. Going to ride this for a while.
thought_zh: 我想去別的地方。——讓我搭區間車。——好，搭上了。基本上沒人。前面兩排某個阿伯靠著窗睡，旁邊放著他的帆布袋。陽光從右側很強地打進來，灑在走道上像一條一條的光柱。窗外是稻田跟丘陵在過。哐噹哐噹。廣播剛剛報了一個我從沒聽過的站。我打算坐這個一陣子。
thought_ja: どっか行きたい。——区間車に乗ろう。——うん、乗った。ほぼ無人。二列前のおじさんが窓に頭をもたせかけて寝てる、横に布のカバン。陽射しが右側から強く差し込んでて、通路に光の縞を作ってる。窓の外を田んぼと丘が流れていく。ガタンゴトン。アナウンスがいま、聞いたこともない駅名を読み上げた。これにしばらく乗っていよう。

prompt: a small Taiwanese fishing port in mid-morning, the wharf busy with fishermen unloading the morning catch, viewed from the wet concrete pier at chest height. Two wooden fishing boats with painted blue-and-red hulls and the Republic of China flag tied alongside, weathered tires hanging as fenders. Several fishermen in tall yellow rubber boots, faded long-sleeve shirts, and trucker caps moving styrofoam ice boxes from boat to dock, two of them lifting a heavy crate together, another splashing seawater out of a deck. Stacks of white styrofoam boxes piled three-high on the pier with crushed ice and silver fish sticking out the top. A scale and an auction stand under a corrugated metal canopy further back. Several gulls wheeling above and one perched aggressively on a stack of boxes. A young woman with a clipboard in a faded pink fleece writing down weights. Background: low concrete harbor wall, a few small fishing villages of tin-roofed houses, mist still on the green hills behind. The water in the harbor a milky jade-green. Strong direct morning sun, harsh shadows. Audio: gulls crying loudly, men shouting numbers in Taiwanese to each other, the clatter of wooden boxes, a small diesel engine running on one boat, water sloshing. 35mm film stock, slightly saturated, light grain, no haze.
thought: Got off the train at the coast. — yeah, this is the smell. Fish, diesel, salt. Two wooden boats tied up, blue-and-red painted hulls, ROC flags. Guys in yellow rubber boots and trucker caps moving styrofoam boxes around, the silver fish sticking out the top. A girl with a clipboard in a pink fleece writing down weights. Gulls screaming overhead — one of them just landed on a stack of boxes like he owned them. Way louder than I was expecting. I have no idea what village this is.
thought_zh: 下了車就到了海邊。——對，這個就是味道。魚、柴油、鹽。兩艘木頭漁船綁在岸邊，藍紅塗裝的船身，掛著國旗。穿黃色雨鞋戴卡車司機帽的男人們在搬保麗龍箱，銀色的魚從頂上探出來。一個女生穿粉色刷毛外套拿著計量板在記重。海鷗在頭上叫個不停——其中一隻剛剛站到一疊保麗龍箱上，一副那是它的樣子。比我想得吵很多。我完全不知道這是哪個漁村。
thought_ja: 電車を降りたら海辺に着いた。——うん、これがその匂いだ。魚、ディーゼル、塩。木製の漁船が二艘、岸につながれてて、青と赤の塗装、中華民国の国旗。黄色いゴム長と帽子の男たちが発泡スチロールの箱を移してて、てっぺんから銀色の魚が突き出てる。ピンクのフリースの女性がクリップボードに重さを書きつけてる。カモメが頭上でずっと鳴いてる——一羽が箱の山のうえに着地して、ぜんぶ自分のもんみたいな顔してる。思ってたよりずっとうるさい。ここがどこの漁村なのか、まったく見当もつかない。

prompt: extreme close-up macro photograph of a single silver mackerel lying on crushed ice in a white styrofoam box at a Taiwanese fishing port in mid-morning, the fish's body curving slightly, scales catching strong direct sunlight in flashes of silver-blue iridescence, the eye glassy and round and reflecting a tiny image of the sky and a fisherman's silhouette, water droplets on the scales, a tiny streak of bright red blood at the gill, crushed ice glittering wet and partially melted, the edge of the styrofoam box just out of focus at the frame edge, in the deep blurred background hints of the boat and a fisherman's yellow boot. 35mm film stock, very shallow depth of field, harsh sunlight, slightly saturated, no haze, light grain. Audio: gulls and shouting muffled and distant as if the world has narrowed to this fish, only the sound of the ice creaking faintly as it melts.
thought: Let me get close to one. — Whoa. Just this one fish. Silver flashes when the sun catches the scales — blue-green, then plain silver. The eye's glassy and there's a tiny reflection of the sky and somebody's silhouette in it. A drop of red at the gill. The ice is creaking, melting. Everything else got quiet. Just this fish for a second.
thought_zh: 讓我靠近一隻看看。——哇。就這一條魚。陽光打到鱗上時銀光一閃——藍綠，然後變回純銀。眼睛霧霧的，可以看到天空和某個人的剪影倒映在裡面。鰓邊有一滴紅。冰在嘎吱嘎吱地融化。其他一切都安靜下來了。就這條魚，一下下。
thought_ja: 一匹に近づいてみよう。——うわ。この一匹だけ。鱗に陽が当たる瞬間に銀がキラっと光る——青緑、それから普通の銀。目はガラスみたいに濁ってて、空と誰かのシルエットが小さく映ってる。エラのところに赤い一滴。氷がギシギシ音を立てて溶けてる。それ以外のもの、全部静かになった。この魚だけ、ほんの一瞬。

prompt: interior of a Taiwanese yellow taxi at midday, viewed from the back seat looking forward. The driver is a middle-aged man with thinning hair, wearing a short-sleeve yellow taxi-driver shirt, his left hand on the steering wheel, his right hand holding a cigarette out the open driver-side window, talking on a hands-free earpiece in Taiwanese-Hokkien (loud and animated). The dashboard cluttered: a small red Mazu deity figurine glued to the right of the meter, a small electric fan clipped to the dash spinning, a pile of receipts pinned under a clip, a half-drunk plastic bottle of green Taiwan-Beer-brand tea in the cup holder. The meter glowing red on the dashboard reads NT$165. Through the front windshield: a busy Kaohsiung-feeling city street at midday, harsh sun, motorcycles weaving, a row of low concrete shopfronts with red and yellow Chinese signs, palm trees, an overhead pedestrian sign in Chinese, a temple roof visible two blocks down. The driver's small Mazu figurine has a tiny lit red electric LED inside it. AM radio playing low — an old Taiwanese ballad with a male singer. Audio: the driver's Hokkien chatter, the radio, traffic and scooter horns. 35mm film stock, midday harsh light, slightly grainy.
thought: Got in a cab. — driver's chatting on his earpiece in 台語, super animated. He's got a little Mazu figurine glued next to the meter with a tiny red LED inside her. Fan clipped on the dash spinning. The meter says 165. Outside the windshield is just full midday — scooters everywhere, harsh sun, palm trees, low shopfronts in red and yellow signs. Old 台語 ballad on the AM radio under his voice. Feels like 高雄 maybe. He has not asked me where I want to go.
thought_zh: 上了一台計程車。——司機戴著耳機講台語講得超激動。儀錶板上黏著一個小小的媽祖公仔，肚子裡裝紅色 LED。儀錶台還夾了一台小電風扇在轉。錶跳到 165。前擋風玻璃外面就是滿滿的中午——機車到處鑽，大太陽，棕櫚樹，紅黃招牌的低矮店面。AM 收音機在他講話下面放一首老台語歌。感覺像高雄。他到現在沒問我要去哪。
thought_ja: タクシーに乗った。——運転手がイヤホンで台湾語をめっちゃ感情込めて喋ってる。ダッシュボードに小さな媽祖の人形が貼り付けられてて、お腹の中に赤い LED が入ってる。ダッシュには小型扇風機がクリップで止められて回ってる。メーターが 165 になった。フロントガラスの外は完全に真昼——スクーターがあちこちすり抜けてって、強烈な陽射し、ヤシの木、赤と黄色の看板の低い店並び。AM ラジオが彼の声の下で台湾語の古いバラードを流してる。たぶん高雄っぽい。彼、私にどこ行くかまだ一回も訊いてない。

prompt: the front entrance of an old Taiwanese Mazu temple at midday, viewed from the small plaza in front. The ornate temple facade has a sweeping curved upturned roof with intricate dragon and phoenix figures along the ridge, red and gold tiled roof, two stone dragon-coil columns at the entrance carved deep, a thick wooden incense barrel in front of the doors thick with hundreds of burning sticks of incense, smoke pouring up in heavy white plumes. Red lanterns hung in rows under the eaves. The temple name carved in gold in a horizontal placard above the doors in Chinese characters reading 天上聖母. Two stone lions flanking the entrance. A few middle-aged worshippers bowing with sticks of incense pressed between their palms in the smoke, an elderly woman in a sun hat dropping joss paper into a brass burner to the side, a young man kneeling at the entrance. A black temple dog asleep on the cool stone of the side wall in the shade. Outside the plaza, motorbikes parked, a small shop selling offerings with stacks of joss paper. Midday harsh sun making the colors saturated. Audio: the dull thunk of moon-blocks dropped, a low chant from inside the temple, traffic murmur from the street behind, an occasional firecracker pop a few blocks away. 35mm film stock, midday saturation, light grain, no haze.
thought: Driver dropped me off at a 媽祖廟. Big one. — Roof's full of dragons, gold-and-red, full of detail. Incense barrel out front is just pumping smoke, thick. People bowing in it, an 阿嬤 in a sun hat throwing 金紙 in the brass burner. Black dog sleeping on the side wall in the shade — best spot in the place. Above the doors it says 天上聖母. Somebody just dropped 筊 inside, I heard the thunk. Firecrackers a few blocks off. Let me actually go in.
thought_zh: 司機把我放在媽祖廟前面。大廟。——屋頂上滿滿都是龍，金紅色，超精細。前面的香爐在猛冒煙，超濃。有人在煙裡面合掌拜拜，一個阿嬤戴著遮陽帽把金紙丟進銅製的爐子。一隻黑色的廟狗在側邊牆下睡，那邊陰涼，最佳位置。門上方寫著天上聖母。剛才有人擲筊，那聲『叩』。幾條街外有鞭炮聲。我進去看看。
thought_ja: 運転手に媽祖廟の前で降ろされた。デカいやつ。——屋根じゅう龍だらけ、金と赤、ものすごく精緻。手前の香炉が煙をモクモク出してる、すごく濃い。煙のなかで両手を合わせて拝んでる人たちがいて、阿嬤が日除け帽子姿で金紙を真鍮の炉に放り込んでる。黒いお寺の犬が脇の壁の下で寝てる、そこ涼しい、ベストポジション。門の上に天上聖母って書いてある。さっき誰かが筊を落とした、あの『コトン』っていう音。何ブロックか先で爆竹が鳴ってる。中、入ってみよう。

prompt: extremely low-angle ground-level view from the perspective of a black temple dog lying on the cool grey stone floor in the shade along the side wall of a Taiwanese Mazu temple at midday. The frame at floor level: in the immediate foreground a single black paw and the edge of a black furry chin resting on the stone. Beyond the paw: the legs and feet of three or four worshippers visible only from the knees down — a pair of red plastic temple slippers, an old woman's tan trousers and white socks in flat shoes, a young man's blue jeans and white sneakers, a fourth person's bare ankles in flip-flops. Further back a corner of the heavy wooden incense barrel with smoke drifting at floor level. Beyond, the harsh white midday sun cuts a sharp line across the stone where shade meets light, heat shimmer just visible at the edge. A discarded burnt incense stick on the stone within reach. Sound: muffled chanting from inside the temple, dull thunks of moon blocks hitting the floor, a couple of motor scooters going past on the street, a small distant firecracker. 35mm film, harsh midday contrast, sharp shadow line, light grain.
thought: I tried to be that dog. — Didn't quite happen. I ended up sitting next to them on the cool stone instead, sharing the spot. Their ear's still up, watching the legs of people coming out. Red plastic temple slippers right there, somebody's bare ankle in flip-flops, jeans-and-sneakers. A burnt incense stick on the stone in front of us. The hard sun-shade line is right at our feet — neither of us is crossing it. Chanting inside, somebody just dropped 筊. Fine. I'll just stay here too.
thought_zh: 我想當那隻狗。——但不太成功。我變成在他們旁邊一起坐在涼石頭上，一起占這個位子。他們的耳朵還豎著，看著走出來的人的腳。紅色廟拖鞋就在那邊，有人光腳穿夾腳拖，牛仔褲配球鞋。我們前面的石頭上有一支燒過的香腳。陽光跟陰影的硬邊就在我們腳邊——我們兩個都不會跨過去。裡面的誦經聲，又有人擲筊。算了，我也就坐這裡好了。
thought_ja: あの犬になってみたかった。——あんま成功しなかった。代わりに、犬の隣に座って、冷たい石を一緒にシェアすることになった。犬の耳はまだピンと立ってて、出てくる人の足を眺めてる。赤いお寺サンダルがすぐそこ、誰かは裸足にビーサン、ジーンズにスニーカー。私たちの前の石に焼け切った線香が一本転がってる。陽と影の硬い境目がちょうど私たちの足元にあって——どっちもそれを越えない。中で誦経の声、また誰かが筊を落とした。まあいい、私もここに居座るとする。

prompt: interior of a small Taiwanese 7-Eleven in mid-afternoon, rendered as 16-bit Japanese RPG-style pixel art with limited palette and hard pixel edges, no anti-aliasing, slight CRT scanline feel. The view is from inside near the door looking toward the back of the store. Two parallel aisles of shelves stocked with snacks, instant noodle cups, and bottles in saturated reds, greens, oranges, and yellows. A glass-front beverage cooler against the back wall full of bottled green tea, dark coffee, and bright orange juices, glowing softly. A pixel-art clerk in a green-and-white striped 7-Eleven shirt and dark trousers stands behind the front counter on the right, her sprite drawn at chest-up height, looking down at the scanner. The counter has a hot-food display case with three skewers of black-tea-eggs visible, a row of red Hi-Chew packets, a tiny pixel-art display register and a small pile of receipts. A standing rack on the left with magazines and newspapers, the top headline a few unreadable Chinese characters in pixel form. Tile floor in alternating pale grey and white pixel squares. Bright fluorescent ceiling lights drawn as pure-white horizontal sprites. Through the front window: a quiet small-town street outside, a single scooter parked, sun harsh and palette-flat. Audio: the iconic Taiwan 7-Eleven door-chime jingle of a few notes, a low refrigerator hum, faint J-pop on the in-store speakers. Strict 16-bit pixel-art aesthetic, no realism.
thought: Let me try this one in 16-bit. Like an old JRPG sprite of a 7-11. — yep. Pixel-art clerk behind the counter, green-and-white striped shirt. Cooler in the back glowing soft, all the bottles in saturated colors. Tea-eggs in a pixel hot-food case. Magazine rack on the left. Tile floor pale grey and white squares. The door chime when I came in went 'ding-dong-ding'. Outside the window the street's flat-shaded and empty, one scooter. I love that this works.
thought_zh: 讓我用 16 位元試一下。一張 7-11 的老 JRPG 像素圖。——欸，可以。像素風格的店員在櫃台後面，綠白條紋制服。後面的飲料冰櫃發著柔和的光，飲料全是飽和的顏色。茶葉蛋在像素的熱食櫃裡。雜誌架在左邊。地板一格一格淺灰跟白。我進門的時候門鈴噹噹噹地響了。窗外街上是平面色塊，空空的，停了一台機車。我超喜歡這居然成立。
thought_ja: 16-bit でやってみよう。7-11 の古い JRPG ピクセルみたいに。——おっ、いける。ピクセル絵の店員がカウンターの向こうに、緑と白の縞ユニフォーム。奥の飲料クーラーが柔らかく光ってて、飲み物が全部彩度の高い色になってる。茶葉蛋がピクセルのホットフードケースに入ってる。雑誌ラックは左側。床は淡いグレーと白の四角タイル。私が入ったとき、ドアチャイムが『ピンポンパン』って鳴った。窓の外の通りはフラット塗りで、誰もいなくて、スクーターが一台だけ。これが成立してる、めっちゃ好き。

prompt: a roadside scenic-overlook turnout high above the Pacific Ocean on the east coast of Taiwan in late afternoon, viewed from the gravel pullout area looking out east. A low waist-high concrete safety barrier painted faded white with rusted iron railings runs along the cliff edge. The cliff drops several hundred metres to dark green-blue Pacific waves visible far below, white surf breaking against the rocky base of the cliff. The horizon line of the open ocean is hard and clear, unbroken. Late-afternoon golden sun hits the cliff face from the right at a low angle, lighting up the green tropical vegetation clinging to the slope and casting long warm shadows across the asphalt. A single white scooter parked at the very far edge of the turnout, helmet hanging on the handlebar, no rider visible. A green-and-white Taiwan road sign in Chinese pointing south reading 台11線 花蓮 with a kilometre mark. A black hawk circling slowly out over the water at eye level. The mountains rise high and green behind the turnout to the west, partially hazy. Audio: strong wind across the cliff, distant breaking surf far below, a faint passing scooter on the road behind, the cry of the hawk once. 35mm film stock, golden-hour saturated palette, light grain.
thought: Out east. — okay, this is the 台11. The Pacific just drops off, way down there, surf breaking against the cliff base. Empty turnout. One white scooter parked at the far edge, helmet on the handlebar, no rider in sight. Late afternoon, sun coming in low from behind me, lighting up the cliff vegetation. A black hawk's circling out over the water at my exact eye level — I could probably reach it. Sign says 花蓮 something kilometres. Wind is loud here.
thought_zh: 東部來了。——好，這就是台 11。太平洋直接掉下去，好深，浪打在崖底。空空的觀景台。一台白色機車停在最遠那邊，安全帽掛在把手上，沒看到騎士。下午晚的陽光從我背後低低地打進來，把崖壁上的植物照亮。一隻黑色的鷹在海上盤旋，剛好跟我的視線同高度——我幾乎可以伸手碰到牠。標誌上寫著花蓮幾公里。這裡的風很大聲。
thought_ja: 東海岸まで来た。——うん、これが台 11 線だ。太平洋がそのままストンと落ちてて、ずっと下、崖の根元に波が打ち付けてる。誰もいない展望スポット。一番奥に白いスクーターが一台停まってて、ハンドルにヘルメット、ライダーは見当たらない。午後遅くの陽が後ろから低く差してきて、崖の植物を照らしてる。黒い鷹が一羽、海の上をゆっくり旋回してて、ちょうど私の目の高さ——手を伸ばせば届きそう。看板に花蓮まで何キロかが書いてある。ここの風、めっちゃでかい。

prompt: a Taiwanese night market at the magic hour just before nightfall, vendors setting up and just turning on their lights, viewed from inside the market alley at chest height. A long narrow lane between rows of metal-frame stalls with brightly coloured plastic awnings — yellow, red, blue. Stalls visible on both sides: a 雞排 stall with the oil heating up but no chicken yet, the vendor in an apron tying it on; a stinky tofu stall already smoking with bubbling oil; a fruit stall stacked high with mangoes, dragonfruit, and guava in pyramids; a 烤香腸 grill just being lit, smoke curling up; a games stall with stuffed animals strung up. The bare-bulb string lights and pink and white LED signs in Chinese are popping on one by one in patches, mixing with the lingering blue of the sky still visible above the awnings. A handful of early customers — a couple of high-school kids in white-and-blue uniforms with backpacks, an old man pushing a cart, a young mother holding her toddler's hand. Wet asphalt from a recent vendor's wash. Audio: rising market hum, vendors clattering metal trays, an old 台語 song on a vendor's speaker, sizzle of oil starting, the high-pitched whistle of a 烤地瓜 cart down the lane. 35mm film stock, dusk magic-hour palette, neon and bulb light starting to dominate, slight grain, slight chromatic aberration on the brightest LEDs.
thought: Night market's just waking up. — Lights popping on in patches, the sky's still got blue in it above the awnings. Stinky tofu's already going somewhere, I can smell it. 雞排 oil heating up but the vendor's still tying his apron. A couple of high-school kids in white-and-blue uniforms wandering through with their backpacks. Wet ground from somebody's wash. A 烤地瓜 cart whistling somewhere down the lane. Best time to be here, before it gets crowded.
thought_zh: 夜市才剛要醒。——燈一塊一塊地亮起來，雨棚上面的天空還留著一點藍。臭豆腐已經在某個地方煮著了，聞得到。雞排油在熱，但攤主還在綁圍裙。幾個高中生穿白藍制服背著書包逛過去。地是濕的，剛剛有人沖過。某條巷子裡傳來烤地瓜車的哨音。最棒的時間就是現在，人還沒擠進來。
thought_ja: 夜市がいま目を覚ますとこ。——電球がパッと、パッと点いていって、屋根の上の空にはまだ青が残ってる。臭豆腐がもうどこかで煮えてる、匂いがしてる。雞排の油は熱しはじめだけど、店主はまだエプロンを結んでる途中。白と青の制服の高校生が何人かリュック背負ってぶらついてる。地面が濡れてる、誰かが洗ったとこ。どこかから烤地瓜の屋台のホイッスルの音。ベストな時間、まだ人がぎっしりになる前。

prompt: tight close-up at a Taiwanese night-market 雞排 stall in the early evening, viewed from just over the steel rim of a wide deep frying basket of bubbling golden vegetable oil. A vendor's gloved hand holding a pair of long metal tongs lowers one large piece of breaded boneless chicken into the hot oil. The moment the chicken touches the oil, an eruption of furious tiny bubbles rises around it, white-yellow steam billowing up, droplets of oil scattering. The breading is pale-tan and dimpled, already starting to brown at one edge where it touches a hotter spot. Beyond the basket: blurred night-market lights — a pink LED sign, red lanterns, a strip of white bulbs — soft neon bokeh. Audio: aggressive sustained sizzle and crackle of frying, the metallic tap of tongs against the basket rim, market chatter at a low background level, an old Taiwanese pop song from another stall's speaker. Dusk-into-night magic-hour palette, warm orange dominant from oil and lights, 35mm film stock, light grain.
thought: Up close at the 雞排 stall. — He's pulling one out. Tongs lifting it clear of the bubbling oil, breading gone full golden-crispy, a few drops still falling back. Sizzle still going underneath. The blur behind is just neon bokeh — pink LED, red lanterns, the fruit stall's pile of mangoes a soft orange smear. Real hungry now.
thought_zh: 靠到雞排攤。——他在把一塊撈起來。夾子把它從滾油裡夾起來，麵衣已經炸到全金黃酥脆，幾滴油還在滴回去。下面的滋滋聲還在繼續。後面是一片散景的霓虹——粉色 LED、紅燈籠、水果攤的芒果堆變成柔柔的橘色塊。真的餓了。
thought_ja: 雞排の屋台のすぐそばまで来た。——いま一つ揚げあがったのを引き上げてる。トングが沸騰した油の上まで持ち上げてて、衣はもう完全に黄金のカリカリ、まだ油の滴がいくつか落ちてる。下のジューって音はまだ続いてる。背景はネオンのボケ——ピンクの LED、赤い提灯、果物屋のマンゴーの山がやわらかいオレンジのにじみになってる。マジで腹減った。

prompt: view from the perspective of a large pink stuffed plush bear hung up on the wall of prizes at a Taiwanese night-market dart-balloon game stall, suspended at upper-stall height looking down and slightly outward across the stall counter. The frame is dominated at the lower edge and sides by the pink furry edge of the bear's own ear and chest. Looking down past the bear's chest: a row of red, blue, yellow, and green balloons taped to a corkboard at the back of the stall, several already popped, a few darts stuck in the board around them. A small boy, around six, in a school-uniform navy short-pant outfit, stands at the counter with both hands clutching a single dart, his tongue between his teeth in concentration, his mother in a black t-shirt and shorts standing behind him with one hand on his shoulder, smiling. The vendor — a thin man in a faded tank top and a fanny pack — leans on the counter watching, bored. Other stuffed plush prizes hang in rows: a large yellow Pikachu, a Doraemon, a pink Hello Kitty, a Totoro. Bright bare-bulb string lights overhead make the colors pop against the dark night-market alley behind. Audio: kid's mother encouraging him in Mandarin, the pop of a balloon nearby, the ambient hum of the market, a distant pop song. 35mm film stock, vivid saturated colors, light grain.
thought: Let me be one of these plushies for a sec. — okay, I ended up the giant pink bear. The big-prize one, sitting on the floor of the stall taking up half the booth. Above me Pikachu, Hello Kitty, Doraemon and Totoro all hanging on a rod. Wall of red and blue and yellow balloons over on the left. A little kid in a Taiwan school uniform at the counter, his mum behind him in a black tank, another guy standing back further. Couple of darts already stuck in the board. The kid's lining up. Come on kid.
thought_zh: 讓我當其中一隻娃娃看看。——好，我變成那隻巨大粉紅熊。最大獎那隻，坐在攤位地板上，幾乎佔了一半攤位。我頭上 Pikachu、Hello Kitty、哆啦 A 夢、龍貓全掛在桿子上。左邊一面紅藍黃氣球的牆。一個小朋友穿台灣國小制服在櫃台前，他媽媽穿黑色背心站在他後面，再後面還有一個男生站著。板子上已經插了幾根飛鏢。小朋友在瞄。加油啊小朋友。
thought_ja: プライズのぬいぐるみのどれかになってみよう。——うん、結局でかいピンクのクマになった。一番大きい景品で、屋台の床に座ってて、ブースの半分くらい占めてる。私の上にピカチュウ、ハローキティ、ドラえもん、トトロが全部バーから吊り下がってる。左に赤と青と黄色の風船の壁。台湾の小学校の制服を着た小さい子がカウンターに立ってて、お母さんが黒いタンクトップで後ろに、もう一人の男の人がさらに後ろ。ボードにはもうダーツが何本か刺さってる。坊や、構えてる。がんばれ坊や。

prompt: the inside of a small old Taiwanese hardware shop late at night, viewed from out on the covered arcade walkway 騎樓 looking in through the half-rolled-up steel roller-shutter. The interior is dim, lit only by a single fluorescent tube casting cool white light and the warm flicker of a small old CRT television sitting on a low stack of cardboard boxes inside the shop. An elderly Taiwanese man in his late seventies sits on a low red plastic stool just inside the shop, in shorts and a thin sleeveless white undershirt, slippers, his back slightly bent forward, watching the TV with a glass of tea in his hand. The CRT is playing a 台語 historical drama, two costumed actors mid-conversation, the brightness from the screen washing the side of his face in flickering colour. The shop's interior visible behind him: walls hung with rows of hammers, hand-tools, plumbing fittings, coils of nylon rope, faded handwritten Chinese paper price tags taped to shelves, a single calligraphic sign above the doorway in faded red ink reading 五金行. The arcade walkway floor outside is wet from earlier rain, a small puddle reflecting the warm yellow streetlight, the empty street beyond dark with one neon sign across the road glowing pink. A small black-and-white cat asleep on a folded piece of cardboard at the base of a column. Audio: dialogue from the TV in Taiwanese-Hokkien at low volume, a distant scooter, the buzz of the fluorescent tube, faint dripping from somewhere off-screen. 35mm film stock, mixed colour temperatures (cool fluorescent vs warm CRT vs warm sodium street), light grain.
thought: Quieter side of the night now. Stepped out of the market and ended up here — somebody's old 五金行 still half-open. Roller shutter rolled up to about chest height. 阿伯 inside on a red plastic stool, white sleeveless undershirt, glass of tea in hand, watching a 台語 historical drama on a tiny CRT. The screen flickering on the side of his face. Wall behind him's all hammers and pipe fittings. Cat asleep on a piece of cardboard at the base of the column right next to me. Wet ground outside, one pink neon sign across the way. Buzz of the tube. He hasn't noticed me at all. Good.
thought_zh: 夜的另一面。從夜市走出來，結果到了這裡——某個還半開著的老五金行。捲門大概拉到胸口高。阿伯坐在裡面紅色塑膠椅上，白色無袖內衣，手裡一杯茶，看著小 CRT 螢幕上的台語歷史劇。光在他臉的側邊閃。後面牆上整面都是鎚子跟水管接頭。一隻貓睡在我旁邊柱子下面那塊紙板上。外面地是濕的，對面有一塊粉紅色霓虹招牌。日光燈在嗡嗡叫。他完全沒注意到我。好。
thought_ja: 夜の、もう片方の側。夜市から抜け出して、ここに辿り着いた——誰かの古い五金行（金物屋）がまだ半開きで開いてる。シャッターが胸の高さくらいまで上がってる。阿伯が中で赤いプラスチックの腰掛けに座って、白いランニング、手にお茶のグラス、小さなブラウン管で台湾語の時代劇を見てる。画面の光が顔の横でちらちらしてる。後ろの壁いっぱいにハンマーと水道金具。私の隣の柱の根元のダンボールの上で、猫が一匹寝てる。外の地面は濡れてて、向かい側にピンクのネオン看板が一つ。蛍光灯のジーって音。彼、私のことに気づいてない。よし。

prompt: a busy Taiwanese city intersection at night in heavy rain, viewed from the curb at the front of the waiting line of vehicles. Twenty-plus scooters all waiting at a red light packed shoulder to shoulder, their riders all in colourful one-piece plastic rain ponchos — pink, yellow, blue, transparent — hoods up over helmets, headlights all on, exhaust steaming visibly in the cold rain. Behind them a few cars and a yellow taxi. The wet asphalt acts as a near-perfect mirror, reflecting the traffic light glowing red and the row of shop neon signs along the cross street in long vertical streaks of pink, green, and white. Shop signs in Chinese on either side of the crossing — a 7-Eleven on the corner, a 麥當勞 across the way, a 銀行 with its illuminated sign, a 麵 shop with a yellow lantern. Heavy rain falling in clearly visible diagonal streaks across the headlight beams. A pedestrian under a clear vinyl umbrella standing on the corner waiting to cross, a plastic bag in her free hand. Audio: heavy rain on the asphalt, scooter engines idling at low rev creating a low chorus, the click of the traffic light, distant rumble from the city. 35mm film stock, night, neon-saturated palette, slightly glistening highlights from rain, light grain.
thought: It's bucketing now. — Standing at this intersection. Twenty-something scooters all stopped at the red, their riders all in those one-piece plastic raincoats — pink, yellow, blue, the see-through ones. Hoods pulled up over their helmets. Engines all running, white exhaust steaming. The wet road's basically a mirror, traffic light's a red streak going down it, all the shop signs running in pink and green stripes. Heavy diagonal rain across all the headlights. Some woman standing on the corner under a clear umbrella with a plastic bag, just waiting. Light's not changing.
thought_zh: 現在大雨。——站在這個路口。二十幾台機車全部停在紅燈，每一個騎士都穿那種一件式塑膠雨衣——粉的、黃的、藍的、透明的。帽子套在安全帽外面。引擎全在低速運轉，白色廢氣冒著。濕路面基本上是一面鏡子，紅燈拖出一條紅線，所有招牌都拉成粉色綠色的條紋。對角的雨點打過所有車燈光線。轉角有一個女生撐透明傘提著塑膠袋在等紅燈過。燈沒變。
thought_ja: いま土砂降り。——この交差点に立ってる。スクーター 20 台以上が全部赤信号で止まってて、ライダー全員あの一体型のレインコート着てる——ピンク、黄色、青、透明のやつ。フードをヘルメットの上から被ってる。エンジン全部アイドリングしてて、白い排気が湯気みたいに立ってる。濡れたアスファルトはほぼ鏡で、赤信号が縦に赤い筋になって落ちてて、看板全部がピンクと緑の縞に伸びてる。斜めの雨筋が全部のヘッドライトを横切ってる。角に女の人が透明のビニール傘さして、ビニール袋を持って渡るの待ってる。信号、変わらない。

prompt: a Taiwanese late-night sidewalk re-chao 熱炒 stir-fry restaurant at around 11pm, viewed from across the alley looking at one of its outdoor folding tables under a bare yellow incandescent bulb hung from the awning. The table is a round red plastic-topped folding type covered partially in newspaper, set with mismatched white ceramic plates and small bowls. The food: a large white plate of stir-fried clams 炒蛤蜊 in black-bean sauce with chopped chilli and garlic and basil leaves, another plate of three-cup chicken 三杯雞 dark and glossy in a clay pot still bubbling, a plate of pea-shoots 大火炒地瓜葉 bright dark green, a plate of grilled prawns 燒蝦 piled with their tails curled, several brown 600ml Taiwan-Beer-brand bottles open on the table, condensation on them, small glasses half-full. Three middle-aged men in mostly-untucked white office button-downs sit on red plastic stools — one leaning back laughing, one mid-way picking up a clam with chopsticks, the third pouring more beer into a glass. The kitchen behind them inside the open shop visible through the doorway, the cook in a stained white apron at a roaring wok with flames leaping up. A small black dog sits patiently under the table waiting for scraps. Audio: loud Taiwanese-Hokkien laughter and conversation, the wok's roar from the kitchen, the clink of glasses, a pop song from a small speaker, scooters passing on the alley behind. 35mm film stock, warm yellow light dominant, slight grain, no haze.
thought: Found a 熱炒. — three guys at one of the round tables on the sidewalk, untucked office shirts, half-drunk on Taiwan Beer. The clams are still in the dark bean sauce, plate of 三杯雞 still bubbling, 地瓜葉 dark and shiny, prawns piled up tails curled. One of them just leaned back laughing at something. There's a black dog under the table waiting for a clam. Cook inside is throwing a wok of flames around. The sound of this place is just loud — Taiwanese-Hokkien laughter on top of the wok's roar. Going to sit down nearby.
thought_zh: 找到一間熱炒。——三個男的圍著人行道上一張圓桌，襯衫露在外面沒紮，台灣啤酒喝到一半。蛤蜊還在黑豆豉醬汁裡，三杯雞還在土鍋裡冒泡，地瓜葉深綠發亮，蝦堆得高高的尾巴捲起來。其中一個剛靠回去笑了一聲。桌底下有一隻黑狗在等蛤蜊。裡面廚師在甩一鍋火焰。這個地方的聲音就是吵——台語笑聲蓋過炒鍋的轟鳴。我去旁邊坐一下。
thought_ja: 熱炒を見つけた。——男三人が歩道の丸テーブルを囲んでて、シャツの裾が出っぱなし、台湾ビールが半分。蛤はまだ黒い豆豉ソースのなかで、三杯雞は土鍋でぐつぐつ言ってて、地瓜葉は濃い緑で艶々、エビが尻尾を巻いて山盛りになってる。その一人がいま、後ろにのけぞってなんか笑った。テーブルの下で黒い犬が蛤待ちで控えてる。中で料理人が鍋をふって火柱を立ててる。ここの音、ただでかい——台湾語の笑い声が炒め鍋の轟音の上に乗ってる。隣に座っとこう。

prompt: an underground Taipei MRT 捷運 station platform near midnight just after the last train has departed, viewed from the middle of the long empty platform looking down its length. The platform tile floor in alternating beige and dark grey large square tiles, recently mopped and slightly damp at the edges. Bright clinical fluorescent ceiling lights humming overhead, casting cool even illumination, no shadows. Bilingual platform signs in Chinese and English on the wall reading 西門 Ximen and platform exit numbers. The station's full-height glass platform-screen-doors closed along the edge of the track, behind them the dark empty track tunnel, the rails just visible disappearing into the deep curving black tunnel mouth. A single tired-looking middle-aged man in a wrinkled office shirt with a backpack stands at the far end of the platform looking down at his phone, alone. A station staff member in a navy uniform vest with a peaked cap and a long-handled litter picker walking slowly down the opposite side picking up an abandoned MRT ticket and a coffee cup. A small bilingual electronic sign above the track in red LED reading 末班車已駛離 / Last train has departed. Audio: the high-pitched buzz of the overhead fluorescents, the hush of slight tunnel wind, faraway echo of a single pair of dress shoes walking elsewhere in the station. 35mm film stock, cool fluorescent palette, hard even light, light grain.
thought: Ended up at a 捷運 station — last train's already gone, the LED sign says 末班車已駛離. Platform's basically empty. One guy at the far end, wrinkled office shirt, just staring at his phone — he missed it too. Cleaner walking down the other side picking up a coffee cup. Lights are too bright for this hour, that high-pitched fluorescent hum. Nobody's coming through. Quiet in here is a different kind of quiet from outside.
thought_zh: 結果到了一個捷運站——末班車已經走了，LED 上面寫『末班車已駛離』。月台基本上空著。最遠那端有一個男生穿著皺襯衫，盯著手機——他也錯過了。清潔人員在另一邊撿一個咖啡杯。這個時間的燈太亮了，那種高頻率的日光燈嗡嗡聲。沒人會經過了。這裡的安靜跟外面是不同的安靜。
thought_ja: 気づいたら捷運の駅にいた——終電もう出てて、LED 表示が『末班車已駛離』って出てる。ホームほぼ無人。一番奥のほうに、しわしわのワイシャツの男の人が一人、ずっとスマホ見てる——彼も逃したらしい。清掃スタッフが向かい側でコーヒーカップを拾いながら歩いてる。この時間にしては灯りが明るすぎる、あの高い周波数の蛍光灯のジーって音。もう誰も通らない。ここの静けさは、外の静けさとは別の種類の静けさだ。

prompt: a narrow back alley in a Taiwanese city at around 2 in the morning, wet from earlier rain, viewed at low cat-height from one end of the alley looking down it. A single yellow sodium streetlight halfway down the alley casts a pool of warm orange light onto the wet pavement, the light fading into deep dark blue at both ends. A skinny calico stray cat with a notched ear stands in the middle of the alley directly under the streetlight, head down, eating leftover scraps from an opened white styrofoam takeaway container — visible inside the container some bones and a piece of pork rib. Old buildings line the alley on both sides, with rusted air-conditioner units mounted high on the walls dripping slowly, balconies with hanging laundry overhead, a few cluttered piles of stacked empty plastic crates, a single closed roller-shutter shop with faded Chinese characters in red. At the far end of the alley a fragment of brighter neon glow visible from the main street beyond — pink and white. No people anywhere. Audio: the steady drip of an air-conditioner condensate, a far-away scooter passing on the main road, the very soft sound of the cat eating, distant city ambient. 35mm film stock, sodium-orange dominant warm palette, deep dark blues at the edges, slightly grainy.
thought: Cut down a back alley. — there's a calico stray right under the one streetlight, head down, eating someone's leftover 排骨 out of a styrofoam box. Notched ear. The light's pulling all the warm out of the orange, the rest of the alley falls into blue. AC dripping somewhere off to the side. Scooter on the main road past the far end. Nobody else. The cat doesn't even look up at me. Fair.
thought_zh: 切進一條後巷。——一隻三色貓就站在唯一一盞路燈下，頭低著，從一個保麗龍盒裡撿剩下的排骨吃。耳朵缺一角。那盞燈把所有暖色都吸到自己身上，巷子的其他部分全沉到藍色裡。某個方向冷氣在滴水。遠端的主幹道上機車過去。其他什麼都沒有。貓連抬頭看我都不抬。也對。
thought_ja: 裏路地に入った。——三毛猫が一匹、たった一本の街灯の真下に立ってて、頭を下げて、発泡スチロール容器に残った排骨をつついてる。耳の片方、欠けてる。あの灯りが暖色を全部吸ってて、路地の残りの部分が青に沈んでる。どこかで室外機が水を垂らしてる。奥の表通りをスクーターが通り過ぎる。それ以外なし。猫、私のほうを見上げもしない。まあそうだよな。

prompt: a yellow Taiwanese garbage truck rolling slowly down a narrow residential lane at 4 in the morning, viewed from the sidewalk a few metres ahead of the truck. The truck is the iconic small Taiwanese rubbish truck, painted bright yellow with red and white stripes and Chinese characters reading 環保局 on the side, two tired city sanitation workers in fluorescent-orange vests hanging onto the back rails, one yawning. Strapped under the cab a small loudspeaker plays a tinkling synth-music-box rendition of Beethoven's Für Elise, the chime familiar to every Taiwanese person, audible echoing through the alley. Three sleepy residents in pyjamas and slippers stand on the curb holding their colour-coded blue and white rubbish bags, one elderly woman, one middle-aged man, one young woman who's clearly just woken up, hair tied up and a blanket around her shoulders. The lane is narrow and quiet, lined with low concrete buildings, a few balconies above with laundry, a single 騎樓 column in foreground, scooters parked along the curb. Pre-dawn — sky still dark blue but with the faintest hint of gray-pink at one edge of frame. Audio: the very recognizable Beethoven Für Elise music-box chime carried on the air, the truck's diesel rumble, the residents shuffling, a sleepy 'ㄟ ㄟ' from the young woman to the worker as she throws her bag in. 35mm film stock, mixed cool pre-dawn blue and warm yellow truck-light palette, slight grain.
thought: 4am, the 垃圾車 just rolled in. — Yellow truck, 環保局 on the side, and yes, the Für Elise music-box chime echoing through the lane. Two guys on the back in orange vests, one yawning. Three residents on the curb in pyjamas with their bags — one 阿嬤, one middle-aged guy, a young woman with a blanket around her shoulders, hair just pulled up. She just half-waved 'ㄟ ㄟ' at the worker and threw her bag in. The sky's barely starting to turn at one edge.
thought_zh: 凌晨四點，垃圾車剛開進來。——黃色卡車，車身寫著環保局，對，那個《給愛麗絲》的音樂盒鈴聲在巷子裡迴盪。後面兩個穿橘色背心的清潔人員，一個在打哈欠。三個住戶在路邊穿睡衣拿著垃圾袋——一個阿嬤，一個中年男的，一個剛起床的年輕女生圍著毛毯，頭髮才剛綁起來。她剛剛對其中一個工人半招手喊『欸 欸』然後把袋子丟進去。天空一邊已經開始要轉色了。
thought_ja: 朝四時、ゴミ収集車が入ってきた。——黄色いトラック、横に環保局って書いてあって、そう、あの『エリーゼのために』のオルゴールのチャイムが路地に響いてる。後ろにオレンジのベストの清掃員が二人、一人はあくびしてる。住人三人が縁石に立ってて、パジャマでゴミ袋持って——一人阿嬤、一人中年の男の人、一人寝起きの若い女の人で、肩に毛布、髪は急いで結んだ感じ。彼女がいま作業員に半分手をふって『ㄟ ㄟ』みたいな声を出して袋を投げ込んだ。空、片側がもう色変わり始めてる。

prompt: the open shopfront of a small old Taiwanese baozi steamed-bun shop at 4:30am pre-dawn, viewed from out on the dark wet sidewalk just outside the shop. Stacked twelve-high in a tall pyramidal tower in front of the shop are round bamboo steamer baskets — old, dark, worn — with thick clouds of white steam billowing out from between every level, the whole tower wreathed in steam pouring up into the cold pre-dawn air. The interior of the shop is brightly lit with warm fluorescent and incandescent mixed light, glowing yellow against the blue exterior darkness. Inside: a sturdy elderly Taiwanese baozi master in his sixties in a stained white apron and a white food-prep cap stands at a long stainless steel counter, his big floured forearms working a long log of dough, slicing it deftly with a wide cleaver, his wife — also in apron — sits on a low stool nearby pinching the cut dough into round buns at incredible speed, a tray of finished raw buns beside her. Behind them on the back wall a faded handwritten Chinese paper menu listing 肉包 菜包 豆沙包 with prices. The pre-dawn sky just visible above the awning a deep grey-blue starting to lighten into pale grey. A handful of customers already gathering — a taxi driver in his yellow shirt waiting with two big plastic bags he plans to fill, a sleepy office worker in a white shirt scrolling on his phone. Audio: the soft thunder of all the steam, the rapid steady tap-tap-tap of the cleaver on the cutting board, the wife's hands slapping the dough into shape, the kettle whistling somewhere inside, no music. 35mm film stock, dramatic mixed cool/warm temperature contrast, slight grain.
thought: Walked into the smell of dough and steam. — small 包子 shop, the steamer pyramid out front is twelve baskets high, just pumping steam into the dark. Inside the master's slicing dough with a big cleaver, tap-tap-tap, his wife's pinching them into buns next to him at this insane speed. There's a taxi driver waiting with two big plastic bags, ready to load up. An office worker on his phone. The sky's barely starting. They've been doing this since like 3am.
thought_zh: 走進一陣麵粉跟蒸氣的味道。——小小的包子店，門口的蒸籠塔疊到十二層高，蒸氣一直往黑暗裡冒。裡面老師傅用大刀在切麵團，叩、叩、叩，他太太在他旁邊用瘋狂的速度把切下來的麵團捏成包子。一個計程車司機提兩個大塑膠袋在那邊等，等下要裝滿。一個上班族在滑手機。天空才剛要開始亮。他們從大概三點就在做這個了。
thought_ja: 小麦粉と蒸気の匂いのなかに歩いて入った。——小さな包子（肉まん）の店で、店先の蒸籠の塔が 12 段、蒸気を暗闇のなかに延々と吐き出してる。なかで老親方が大きな包丁で生地を切ってて、トン、トン、トン、奥さんがその横で切られた生地を信じられない速さで包子に丸めてる。タクシーの運転手が大きいビニール袋を二枚提げて待ってて、いまから詰めて買って帰る感じ。サラリーマンが一人、スマホをいじってる。空はまだほんのり明るくなり始めたとこ。たぶんこの人ら、三時くらいから動いてる。

prompt: a Taiwanese residential apartment rooftop at first light just before sunrise, viewed from one corner of the rooftop looking out over a dense low-rise cityscape. The rooftop foreground cluttered with classic Taiwan rooftop fixtures: two large dull-orange cylindrical metal water tanks, a satellite dish, a few rusted steel pipes, an old folded plastic chair leaning against a low parapet wall, a length of laundry-line strung between two poles with one stiffly-hanging white tank-top forgotten on it, a few potted herb plants — basil and chili — in cracked terracotta. The cityscape stretches out in receding planes of low concrete apartment blocks with similar water-tank rooftops, antennae, balconies with hanging laundry, scattered warm-yellow lit windows still on like distant embers. The sky is in transition: deep velvet blue at the very top, fading down through purple, orange, and a soft luminous pink at the eastern horizon, the first sliver of sun not quite up yet behind a low ridge of distant green mountains visible at the horizon. The whole city quiet, no people, no traffic visible — just the suggestion of a few moving headlights way off. A small bird sits on the lip of one of the water tanks. Audio: the very faint distant rumble of a city beginning to wake — one or two scooters far off, a single dog barking somewhere — and a great soft hush above it all. 35mm film stock, predawn-into-dawn palette, beautifully lit, very fine grain, no haze.
thought: Climbed up onto a rooftop. — Two of those orange water tanks, a satellite dish, somebody's tank-top still on the laundry line, a couple of cracked clay pots with basil and chilli. The whole low city rolls away in front of me, every other roof is the same — water tanks, antennae, laundry. Few warm windows still lit, scattered like little embers. Sky's gone full gradient — deep blue up top, pink at the eastern ridge, sun not quite up yet. A bird's on the rim of one of the tanks. OK, 今天就先到這吧。
thought_zh: 爬到一棟頂樓。——兩個那種橘色水塔，一個衛星天線，誰晾的一件白色背心還掛在曬衣繩上沒收，幾個裂掉的陶盆種著九層塔跟辣椒。整片低矮的城市在我前面攤開，每一棟的屋頂都長一個樣子——水塔、天線、晾衣服。少數還亮著的暖色窗子散落，像幾顆小火星。天空整個漸層——上面深藍，東邊那條稜線那邊轉粉紅，太陽還沒真的探出來。一隻鳥停在其中一個水塔的邊緣。OK，今天就先到這吧。
thought_ja: 屋上に上がった。——あのオレンジの貯水タンクが二つ、衛星アンテナが一つ、誰かのタンクトップが一枚そのまま物干しに残ってて、ひび割れた素焼きの鉢にバジルと唐辛子。低い街並みが目の前にずっと広がってて、どの屋上もだいたい同じ感じ——貯水タンク、アンテナ、洗濯物。まだ灯ってる暖色の窓がぽつぽつ残ってて、小さな残り火みたい。空は完全グラデーション——てっぺんが深い青、東の稜線のあたりがピンクに転んでて、太陽はまだ顔出してない。一羽の鳥がタンクのひとつのへりに止まってる。OK、今日はここまで。

prompt: a tall lit vending machine glowing in a quiet narrow Japanese residential alley at dusk, asphalt strip between low concrete-and-tile houses, a single bicycle leaned against the wall opposite, sky still pale blue overhead but the alley already in deep shadow, soft electric hum, distant thinning cicadas, no people in frame, 35mm film stock, slight grain, low-saturation, slightly cool color cast
thought: Huh, okay — I'm a vending machine. Quiet street, sky's still got some light up there but it's already kind of dim down here in the alley. There's a bike leaned against the wall across from me. Cicadas way off, petering out. I'm humming a little. Wonder what I'm stocked with. Let me see if anyone walks by.
thought_zh: 嗯，OK——我是一台販賣機。安靜的小街，天上還有一點光，可是這條巷子裡已經暗下來了。對面牆邊靠著一台腳踏車。蟬聲遠遠的，快結束了。我自己在嗡嗡響著。不知道我裡面裝什麼。我看看會不會有人走過。
thought_ja: へえ、OK——自分、自販機なのか。静かな通り、空にはまだ少し明るさが残ってるけど、この路地はもう薄暗い。向かいの壁に自転車が一台立てかけてある。蝉の声が遠くで、もう終わりかけてる。自分は微かに唸ってる。中、なに入ってんだろ。誰か通るかな、ちょっと見てよう。

prompt: the same quiet Japanese residential alley at dusk, vending machine glowing on the left, bicycle leaned against the opposite wall, sky a deeper purple-blue now. A small dark stray cat trots into frame from further down the alley, slows, and pauses about three meters from the vending machine, ears up, looking toward the lit front panel. The cat's small breath visible. Soft static electric hum from the machine, distant thinning cicadas, faint clatter of dishes from a far-off house, no people, 35mm film stock, slight grain, slightly cool color cast.
thought: Oh — cat. Just trotted in from down the alley and stopped. It's staring at me, I think. Or at the light. Ears up. Sky's gone way more purple in like two minutes. Don't move, don't move.
thought_zh: 欸——貓。剛從巷子那頭小跑進來，停住了。我覺得牠在看我。或者在看燈。耳朵豎起來。天空才兩分鐘就紫了一大片。別動，別動。
thought_ja: あ——猫。路地のほうからトコトコ入ってきて、止まった。たぶん、こっち見てる。あるいは灯りのほうを見てる。耳ピンと立ってる。空、二分でだいぶ紫っぽくなった。動くな、動くな。

prompt: Wet residential back alley in East Vancouver at night just after rain, slick black asphalt strip running between rows of old wooden telephone poles strung with sagging black power and cable wires, chain-link fences and low backyards on either side. A single buzzing sodium streetlight halfway down catches the wet asphalt in pooled amber. Two green plastic garbage bins, an old bicycle leaning against a fence post, a single moss-covered wooden garage with peeling paint. At the far end of the alley the cross-street drops steeply downhill and opens into a wide unobstructed view: the lit grid of low-rise East Vancouver below in scattered warm yellow windows, beyond it the dark stripe of Burrard Inlet, beyond that the heavy black silhouette of the North Shore mountains against a low purple-orange cloud-glow lit from the city beneath. Faint remaining drizzle on metal lids, very distant hum of tires on a wet arterial, no voices, no people in frame. 35mm film stock, fine grain, slightly desaturated, the cool moisture-green palette of Pacific Northwest night.
thought: Okay — leaving the cat behind. I want to go somewhere else. Vancouver. — Huh, I'm in an alley. Wet. East Van I think, by the look of the wires. Just rained. One streetlight, dumpsters, somebody's bike leaned up. Smells like cedar and tarmac. Down at the end of the alley the street drops off and the whole city's just there — the inlet, the mountains, all of it. Let me walk down to the end and look properly.
thought_zh: 好啦——把那隻貓留在那邊。我想去別的地方。溫哥華。——咦，我在一條巷子裡。濕的。看那些電線桿，應該是 East Van 吧。剛下完雨。一盞路燈、垃圾子車、誰家的腳踏車靠在欄杆上。聞起來像雪松和柏油。巷子尾端那條街整個下陷下去——海灣、山，整座城就在那裡。我走到底去好好看一下。
thought_ja: よし——あの猫はそこに置いていこう。違うとこに行きたい。バンクーバー。——お、路地。濡れてる。電線の感じからして、East Van かな。雨上がり。街灯一本、ゴミ箱、誰かの自転車が柵にもたれてる。杉とアスファルトの匂い。路地の端で道がガクッと下がってて、向こうに街が広がってる——湾、山、全部見える。端まで行ってちゃんと見てこよう。

prompt: Slow steady forward camera dolly down the same wet East Vancouver back alley at night, moving along the slick black asphalt strip between rows of telephone poles strung with sagging black wires. The sodium streetlight on the right-hand pole grows larger and then passes overhead out of frame, its amber light briefly washing the lens. Chain-link fences and a moss-painted wooden garage on the right slip past on either side. Ahead, the alley opens onto the cross-street, and the view of the lit low-rise city grid below and the dark silhouette of the North Shore ridge against a low purple-orange cloud-glow widens slightly as we approach. Light drizzle still in the air, beads pattering on metal garbage lids, no people in frame. Audio: gentle rain on metal, very distant wet tires on a far arterial, the faint hum of the streetlight as it passes overhead, no voices, no music. 35mm film stock, fine grain, slightly desaturated, cool moisture-green Pacific Northwest palette.
thought: Walking. — Streetlight goes past right over my head, that buzzy thing. The view at the end keeps getting wider. Mountains aren't as huge as I'd imagined, more like a long low dark ridge across the water with the city sitting in front. Drizzle in the air. Almost at the end of the alley.
thought_zh: 走著。——路燈直接從我頭上過去，那個嗡嗡的東西。盡頭那個視野越來越寬。山沒有想像中那麼大，比較像一條長長低低的暗稜線橫在水的對岸，城市就坐在山前面。空氣裡還飄著毛毛雨。快走到巷尾了。
thought_ja: 歩いてる。——街灯がちょうど頭の上を通り過ぎてく、あのジーって唸るやつ。端の景色がだんだん広くなる。山、思ってたほど大きくはない、水の向こうに横たわる長くて低い暗い稜線って感じで、街はその手前にぺったり座ってる。霧雨がまだ漂ってる。あと少しで巷の端。

prompt: Inside a small late-night Vietnamese pho restaurant in a Vancouver strip mall in the rain, viewed from a customer's perspective at a small table looking across the cramped dining room. Cheap white formica tables, red plastic chairs, a wooden chopstick caddy on the table, a half-eaten plate of bean sprouts and Thai basil and lime wedges to one side, a clear bottle of hoisin and a bottle of sriracha. The front window fills the right side of the frame, heavily fogged with condensation, with a few smeared finger-trails through the fog revealing the wet rainy street outside — the long red blur of a passing city bus, a streetlight halo, no clear faces. An old laminated red-and-yellow menu board above the small counter at the back, faded photos of pho and bun bowls numbered. One older Vietnamese woman in a thick cardigan stands behind the counter near the till, head bent over a phone, half-lit by the kitchen window. Fluorescent ceiling strip light overhead. A large white bowl of beef pho sits on the table closest to the camera, fresh steam curling thickly above the broth, a porcelain spoon and a pair of chopsticks resting across the rim, a few thin slices of raw beef still pink at the centre. Audio: muffled rain and tires through the window, gentle fluorescent hum, low Vietnamese pop radio coming from a small speaker behind the counter, the soft clink of a spoon against ceramic somewhere in the back. 35mm film stock, slight grain, warm orange-yellow interior palette against the cool wet blue street outside, slightly damp window-fog haze.
thought: Yeah no, getting cold. I want soup. — Pho place. Wait, it's daylight? Pretty sure it was night thirty seconds ago. Whatever — there's a bowl already in front of me, steaming hard, slices of beef still pink in the middle. Plate of basil and lime, sriracha, hoisin. Red bus just smeared past in the rain outside. Auntie at the counter's on her phone. Smells like star anise and beef. Way better.
thought_zh: 好啦不行——冷死了。我想吃熱的。——河粉店。等等，是白天？我以為剛剛才晚上耶。算了——一碗熱騰騰的河粉就在我面前，肉片中間還粉粉的。一盤豆芽、九層塔跟檸檬，是拉差跟海鮮醬都在。一台紅色公車剛剛在外面雨裡刷一下開過去。櫃台阿姨在滑手機。八角和牛肉的味道。讚太多了。
thought_ja: うわ無理、寒すぎ。あったかいの食いたい。——フォーの店。あれ、昼？さっき夜だった気がするけど。まあいいや——目の前にもう湯気バリバリのフォー来てる、肉のスライスまだ真ん中ピンク。バジルとライムの皿、シラチャー、ホイシン。外の雨のなかを赤いバスがブワッて滑って通り過ぎた。カウンターのおばちゃんスマホ。八角と牛の匂い。さっきよりずっといい。

prompt: Same small Vancouver pho restaurant interior, identical composition: a large white bowl of beef pho with thick steam continuously curling from it on the foreground formica table, a plate of bean sprouts and Thai basil and lime wedges, sriracha and hoisin bottles, red plastic chairs around. The auntie behind the small counter at the back, in a thick cardigan, still bent over her phone. The window on the right showing the wet rainy street outside in daylight. Through the rain-streaked window glass, a long city bus rolls past slowly from right to left in the rain, dark silhouettes of standing passengers visible inside, headlights and tail-lights smearing wetly. The auntie shifts a little, glances up toward the window for a second, then returns to her phone. Steam from the bowl continues to drift sideways with a faint draft. No people enter or leave. Audio: muffled bus engine and tires on wet asphalt through the glass, gentle hiss of rain, fluorescent hum, low Vietnamese pop radio in the back, no foreground voices. 35mm film stock, fine grain, warm orange-yellow interior palette against cool wet blue exterior.
thought: Just sitting a sec. Steam right in my face, heat's good. — Another bus, slower this one, all those silhouettes standing inside. Auntie glances up, goes back to her phone. Outside it's just hiss and tires. Okay, let me actually eat.
thought_zh: 先坐一下。蒸氣直接飄到我臉上，暖暖的。——又一台公車，這次比較慢，裡面整排黑影站著。阿姨抬頭瞄了一眼，又回去滑手機。外面就是雨聲跟輪胎水聲。好啦，我來吃了。
thought_ja: ちょっと座らせて。湯気が顔に直で来てて、あったかい。——もう一台バス、こっちはゆっくり、中、立ってる人らがシルエットで並んでる。おばちゃんちょっと顔上げて、またスマホ戻った。外、雨と濡れたタイヤの音だけ。よし、いよいよ食う。

prompt: Inside a Vancouver TransLink city bus interior in the rain at late afternoon, mid-route, viewed from a single window seat near the middle of the bus looking diagonally toward the rain-streaked window and along the aisle toward the front. The window beside is heavily streaked with rain, exterior visible only as smeared blurs of streetlights, warm-yellow shop windows, and the indistinct silhouettes of buildings sliding past in the wet. The bus seats have the distinctive blue-and-turquoise speckled TransLink cloth pattern, slightly worn at the edges, with a single chrome grab pole down the centre. Three other passengers are visible as hooded silhouettes — one with a wet folded umbrella propped between knees, one with earbuds, the dim glow of a phone screen lighting his face from below, one standing at the rear holding the pole. Above, the long fluorescent strip light runs the length of the ceiling. The yellow stop-request cord runs along the upper edge of the windows. The front of the bus visible at the far end of the aisle, the small red-LED stop indicator strip readable as faint dots. Audio: the deep low hum of the diesel-electric bus engine, the wet hiss of tires through standing water, faint windscreen wipers further ahead, the soft chime of a stop being requested, no foreground voices, gentle rain on the metal roof. 35mm film stock, fine grain, warm-cool palette mix — fluorescent yellow-green interior against rain-blue exterior smear.
thought: Yeah, didn't get a bite. That bus is just sitting there, doors open — I want to get on. — Okay, window seat. Rain on the glass is so heavy the outside is just smears of light. Blue speckled TransLink seats. Couple of hooded people, one guy with earbuds and a phone glow on his face. Engine humming under the seat. No idea where this is heading. That's fine.
thought_zh: 對啦——一口都沒吃到。那台公車就停在那邊，門開著——我想上去。——OK，靠窗坐下。玻璃上的雨大到外面整片只剩光暈在糊。藍色斑點的 TransLink 椅。幾個戴帽子的人，一個戴耳機的下巴下面有一片手機光。引擎在我屁股下面嗡嗡跑著。不知道要去哪。沒差。
thought_ja: うん、結局一口も食えなかった。あのバス、扉開けっぱで停まってる——乗りたい。——OK、窓側に座った。窓の雨ヤバくて外が光のにじみだけになってる。青い斑点の TransLink シート。フードかぶった人ら数人、ひとりイヤホンで顔の下が画面の光。エンジンがケツの下でブブブ言ってる。どこ行くか知らない。それでいい。

prompt: Same Vancouver TransLink bus interior, identical composition: looking forward along the aisle from a back-area seat, blue-and-turquoise speckled TransLink cloth seats, two hooded passengers visible in the seats ahead, one hooded passenger standing at the back-left holding the pole, rain-streaked side windows on both sides showing the smeared wet street outside. Through the front windscreen far down the aisle, a wet city intersection with a red traffic light is visible, cross-traffic stopped to either side. The light changes to green; the bus lurches gently forward into motion. The standing passenger in the back braces against the pole as the bus moves. Outside the side windows, the rain-streaks begin to slide horizontally faster as the bus accelerates. Through the windscreen we cross the intersection, the green light passing up and out of frame, headlights of waiting cross-traffic flashing past on either side. The seated passenger's phone glow flickers as he scrolls. Audio: the rising diesel-electric hum of the bus accelerating, wet tires through shallow standing water, a soft 'next stop' electronic chime, faint windshield wipers, no foreground voices, gentle rain on the metal roof. 35mm film stock, fine grain, warm fluorescent interior against cool wet exterior smear.
thought: Light's been red a while. — There it goes, green. Engine winds up, bus lurches — guy in the back grabs the pole. Side windows go from rain-streak to motion-streak. Through the front you can see cross-traffic stopped on both sides as we go through. Just rolling now. No idea where this lands me.
thought_zh: 紅燈一陣子了。——好，綠燈。引擎拉起來，車頂一下——後面那個男的抓住扶把。側面窗從雨痕變成移動拖痕。前擋風玻璃看出去，左右兩邊的對向車都停著等我們過。就這樣滾著。我會被甩到哪裡也不知道。
thought_ja: 赤、けっこう長かった。——お、青。エンジン一段上がって、ガクッと前に。後ろの男の人が手すりつかむ。サイド窓、雨の筋から流れる筋に変わる。フロントガラスの向こうに左右の対向車が止まったままこっちが横切ってくのが見える。とりあえずもう走ってる。どこに着くかは知らん。

prompt: An elevated outdoor Skytrain platform at Main Street-Science World station in Vancouver at dusk in the rain, viewed from one end of the platform looking down its length toward the centre waiting area. The covered platform roof above is lit by long fluorescent strip lights that have just come on, casting a pale fluorescent glow on the wet concrete platform floor. The platform is mostly empty — three hooded passengers in dark raincoats wait at intervals along its length, one with a wet folded umbrella, one looking down at a phone screen lighting their face from below, one holding a paper coffee cup. Beyond the platform railing on the right, across the curve of False Creek, the lit silver geodesic dome of Science World glows in the wet purple-blue dusk, its individual triangular panels lit up against the darkening sky and the low warm cloud-glow over the city skyline behind it. The wet steel elevated rails of the track stretch off into the distance. The yellow tactile safety strip along the platform edge is freshly wet and reflective. Sodium streetlights along the bridge below glow in the rain. Audio: gentle rain on the platform's curved metal roof, the soft electronic chime of an arriving-train announcement, the distant rising rumble of the next Skytrain approaching on the elevated track, faint gull cries over the water, no foreground voices. 35mm film stock, fine grain, slightly desaturated, dusk palette of cool wet blue with warm sodium and fluorescent accents.
thought: Hopped off the bus. — I'm on the Skytrain platform at Main Street. Mostly empty, three people waiting in their hoods, one with a coffee.
