thought: Up on someone's roof. Orange water tank in front of me, more roofs in every direction — laundry on bamboo poles, satellite dishes, more orange tanks. There's a 鳳頭蒼鷹 perched on the next tank over, just sitting there, head moving. 101 way out, only the top three segments are catching the gold. Rest of the city's still in shadow. Rooster going off on someone's balcony.
thought_zh: 在某人的屋頂上。前面一個橘色水塔，每個方向都還是屋頂——晾在竹竿上的衣服、衛星小耳朵、更多橘色水塔。隔壁那個水塔上面停著一隻鳳頭蒼鷹，就停在那邊，頭在轉。101 在很遠，只有頂端三節在吃光。城市其他地方都還在影子裡。某戶的陽台上有一隻公雞在叫。
thought_ja: 誰かの屋上にいる。目の前にオレンジの水タンク、どっち向いてもまた屋根——竹竿に干された洗濯物、衛星アンテナ、また別のオレンジのタンク。隣のタンクの上に鳳頭蒼鷹が一羽止まってて、ただそこにいて、頭だけ動かしてる。101はずっと遠くに見えてて、てっぺんの三段目までだけ金色を受けてる。街のほかの部分はまだ影の中。どっかのベランダで雄鶏が鳴いてる。

prompt: interior of a small Taipei neighbourhood bakery's back kitchen at dawn, first-person eye-level view from across the long stainless-steel work counter. heavy warm humid air visibly hanging in slanting fluorescent light. a Taiwanese baker in her thirties — flour-dusted white t-shirt, a long mid-length white apron, dark hair pulled back under a baker's cap — is working at the work-table, currently dividing and rolling out a long row of soft white bun dough into round portions, her hands and forearms pale with flour. behind her, dominating the back wall: a tall industrial double-decker oven, its lower half through a heavy glass window glowing orange-warm with rows of golden 菠蘿麵包 (pineapple buns) just baking, a faint visible heat shimmer rising from the open vents. to the side: a wheeled metal rack with stacked baking sheets, a row of resting 紅豆 (red bean) buns on a metal tray under a thin cloth, a couple of plastic dough proofing tubs. a small AM radio on a high shelf in the corner. through a single small high window: the dawn sky just turning pale peach. fine flour drifting visibly in the diagonal beam of one ceiling fluorescent tube. ambient sound: the soft thud-thud of dough portions being shaped on the metal counter, the low hiss and click of the oven thermostat, low-volume Hokkien morning talk-radio with two presenters chatting, the click of a baking sheet being set down, no music, no other speech. 35mm film stock, slightly grainy, warm tungsten kitchen light with slight visible flour-dust haze.
thought: Dropped off the roof and ended up here — back of a bakery. Two of them working — a woman at the work-table shaping bun dough, flour up to her elbows, and a guy further back at the racks. Pineapple buns visible through the oven glass, going golden. Whole place smells like sugar and wheat, fine flour drifting in the light. I'm actually hungry now.
thought_zh: 從屋頂掉下來就到這——一間麵包店的後場。兩個人在忙——一個女生站在工作台前面在揉麵糰，麵粉到手肘，另一個男生在後面架子那邊。烤箱玻璃裡看得到菠蘿麵包，正在轉金色。整間店都是糖跟麥的味道，細細的麵粉浮在光裡。我現在真的餓了。
thought_ja: 屋上から落ちて、ここに着いた——あるパン屋の厨房の裏。二人働いてる——女の人が作業台でパン生地をこねてて、肘まで小麦粉、男の人は奥のラックで作業中。オーブンの窓越しに菠蘿麵包(パイナップルパン)が金色になっていってるのが見える。砂糖と小麦の匂いが店全体に立ってて、細かい粉が光のなかで漂ってる。俺、ほんとにお腹空いてきた。

prompt: first-person eye-level view (about 1.6m off the ground) walking a few steps behind a single small Taiwanese school child of about 7 years old in a quiet morning Taipei back-alley. she is wearing a typical Taiwan elementary school uniform — navy pleated skirt, white short-sleeved shirt with a small red kerchief tied at the collar — and is carrying a bright yellow Taiwan elementary school waterproof school bag (the iconic '黃色小學生書包') with black straps on her back. small white sneakers, white socks. her dark hair is in two short pigtails with small red elastic bands. she is walking alone, head slightly bent forward, the yellow bag bobbing slightly as she walks. the alley is the early-morning version of a Taipei residential back-lane — narrow, lined with low old apartment blocks (4 stories), 騎樓 (covered arcade) columns visible on the right side still in cool shadow, scooters parked at angles, telephone wires overhead. early sun comes through diagonally between buildings on the left, warm gold falling in clean stripes onto the still-wet pavement (yesterday's rain). a tiny tabby cat sits on a doorstep watching her pass. far ahead at the end of the alley, a small 早餐店 visible with steam already rising from its grill. ambient sound: her small sneaker footsteps on wet pavement, a distant scooter starting up somewhere blocks away, a single pigeon cooing from a rooftop, faint Mandarin morning news leaking from one of the open apartment windows above, a Hokkien radio commercial from another window, the 垃圾車 still very faint in the distance playing '給愛麗絲', no music. 35mm film stock, slightly grainy, naturalistic morning colour with gold-and-shadow contrast.
thought: Following a kid now. Maybe seven years old, navy uniform, that bright yellow Taiwan school bag, two short pigtails with red bands. Walking alone — actually alone, no parent in sight. The bag's basically bigger than her torso. Sun coming through diagonally between the buildings, gold stripes on the wet ground. A little tabby on a doorstep watched her pass.
thought_zh: 現在跟著一個小朋友走。大概七歲，深藍色制服，那個亮黃色的台灣小學書包，兩條短短的辮子綁紅色橡皮筋。她一個人在走——是真的一個人，沒有大人。那個書包基本上比她的身體還大。太陽斜斜地從建築之間打進來，把濕的地面切成一條條金色。一隻虎斑貓蹲在門口台階上看著她走過。
thought_ja: いま小さい子について歩いてる。たぶん7歳、紺の制服、あの明るい黄色の台湾の小学生のリュック、短いツインテールに赤いゴム。一人で歩いてる——ほんとに一人で、保護者の姿なし。リュックがもう、本人の胴より大きい。陽が建物の隙間から斜めに差し込んでて、濡れた地面を金色のストライプに切ってる。玄関の段に座ってる小さいキジトラが、彼女が通り過ぎるのをじっと見てた。

prompt: watercolour on cold-press paper aesthetic — visible paper texture, soft pigment bleeds at the edges of forms, gentle gradients, no hard outlines. early morning at the pond in Taipei's 大安森林公園 (Daan Forest Park). low mist still hanging just above the still water surface. in the centre-left of the frame: a black-crowned night heron (黑冠麻鷺) — recognisable by its hunched posture, dark crown stripe, thick yellow legs, long pointed beak — stands absolutely motionless on a moss-edged rock at the water's edge, beak angled slightly downward toward the water. in the foreground water: three or four mallard ducks floating lazily, leaving small ripples that bleed softly into the painted surface. a stand of large round lotus leaves in the middle distance with two pale-pink lotus flowers half-open. on the far side of the pond, dark palm-tree silhouettes and the red curved roof of a small Chinese pavilion (亭子) emerging out of the morning mist. two joggers in small bright running clothes (one in red, one in yellow) are tiny on the path beyond the pond, soft and blurred. the dawn sky above is a peach-pink wash with hints of pale grey-blue. ambient sound: faint duck quacks, a single distant koel-bird call, very faint distant traffic from an outer road, no music. watercolour on textured paper aesthetic strictly maintained, soft edges throughout, no photo realism.
thought: Wanted something different — let me see this in watercolour. Okay — 大安森林公園 pond, mist still on the water. There's a 黑冠麻鷺 standing dead still on a rock, that hunched-shoulder posture they do. A few ducks floating around. Lotus half-open in the middle. Two tiny joggers way across the path on the far side. Sky's gone full peach already.
thought_zh: 想要換個感覺——用水彩看看。OK——大安森林公園的池塘，霧還掛在水面上。一隻黑冠麻鷺一動也不動地站在一塊石頭上，牠們那種駝背姿勢。幾隻鴨子在水上漂。中間蓮花開了一半。對岸遠遠的步道上有兩個小小的慢跑的人。天空整個變成水蜜桃色了。
thought_ja: なんか違うのが見たくなった——水彩で見せてくれ。よし——大安森林公園の池、まだ水面に霧が残ってる。黑冠麻鷺が一羽、岩のうえで全然動かずに立ってて、あいつらのあの猫背の姿勢。鴨が何羽か浮いてる。真ん中で蓮が半分開いてる。向こう岸の歩道のはるか遠くに、ジョギング中の人が二人、ちっちゃく見える。空はもう全面ピーチ色だ。

prompt: first-person view from the rider's seat on a Taipei 機車 (scooter) in dense morning rush-hour traffic, the rider's own gloved hands gripping the curved handlebars visible in the bottom corners of frame, a fluffy pink mascot keychain hanging from one mirror and swaying. directly ahead: a wide busy Taipei boulevard with multiple lanes of dense morning traffic — packed with dozens of other scooters of all kinds, mixed with cars, one yellow taxi, and a blue city bus mid-distance — riders ahead wearing helmets of every colour (fluorescent yellow, neon pink, matt black, navy, white), a couple still in transparent night raincoats. red tail-lights blink here and there. on the left, the elevated track of the Taipei MRT runs alongside, an MRT train mid-passage above. on the right, urban shop signs slide past — a large green '全聯' supermarket sign, a yellow '玉山銀行' bank sign, a green-orange '7-11' sign. the dashboard of the scooter is partially visible at the bottom of frame: digital speedometer reading '38' in green-blue LCD, the fuel gauge half-full, and a small ceramic Buddha figurine zip-tied to the right handlebar. green palm trees lining the central median strip. morning sky going gold above the buildings. ambient sound: the sustained whining hum of the rider's own scooter engine, the mixed engines and faint beeping of dozens of other scooters around, the rumble of the MRT train passing overhead, an occasional car horn, faint Mandarin radio leaking from the scooter ahead, no music in this scooter. 35mm film stock, slight motion-blur at the frame edges, naturalistic morning colour.
thought: Got on a 機車 in the rush. Gloved hands on the bars, fluffy pink keychain swaying off the mirror. Packed — scooters everywhere, every helmet a different colour, couple still in their raincoats. Speedo's at 38. MRT overhead on the left going by. 全聯, 7-11, 玉山銀行 sliding past on the right. There's a tiny Buddha zip-tied to my handlebar.
thought_zh: 趕在尖峰時間騎上一台機車。戴手套的手在握把上，後照鏡上一個粉紅色毛茸茸的鑰匙圈在那邊晃。塞——機車滿坑滿谷，每頂安全帽都不一樣的顏色，還有幾個沒脫雨衣。儀表 38。左邊高架捷運剛好開過去。右邊全聯、7-11、玉山銀行一路往後跑。我的把手上還用束帶綁了一個小佛像。
thought_ja: 通勤ラッシュのなか機車(スクーター)に乗った。手袋の手がハンドルに、ミラーにピンクのモフモフのキーホルダーが揺れてる。混んでる——スクーターがどこを見てもいて、ヘルメットが全部違う色、まだレインコート着てる人も何人か。メーターは38。左の高架をMRTがちょうど通り過ぎてく。右側を全聯、7-11、玉山銀行が次々と流れてく。ハンドルに結束バンドで小さい仏像がくっついてる。

prompt: interior of a small old Taipei 茶莊 (traditional tea shop) in the 青田街 / 永康街 neighbourhood, morning, just opened. first-person view from the customer's side of a long polished dark-wood counter. behind the counter, dominating the back wall: tall floor-to-ceiling wooden shelves lined with rows of large clear glass canisters, each with a metal screw-on lid and a handwritten paper label in Chinese characters — visible labels include '凍頂烏龍', '文山包種', '阿里山金萱', '鐵觀音', '東方美人'. dried tea leaves visible inside each canister. the shop owner, a slim Taiwanese man in his late sixties with thinning grey hair and round reading glasses partway down his nose, wearing a slightly worn navy-blue mandarin-collar shirt, stands at the counter — he has just unscrewed the lid of one canister of 文山包種 and is holding a small dark wooden scoop, lifting a small portion of the dark twisted oolong leaves up to about chin height to inspect them in the slanting morning light. on the counter in front of him: a small wooden tea-tasting tray (品茗盤) with three small white porcelain 蓋碗 (gaiwan), a chrome electric kettle just beginning to steam, a folded morning newspaper in Chinese. through a wooden lattice front window / door the morning Taipei back-street is visible — a quiet old residential lane lined with mature 茄苳 trees, dappled morning light. one terracotta pot of jasmine just outside. ambient sound: the very soft electric hum of the kettle just warming up, the dry rustle of tea leaves shifting against the scoop, a single bird call from outside, very faint distant traffic from a bigger road, no music, no speech. 35mm film stock, slightly grainy, warm morning light through the lattice contrasting the cooler dark wood shop interior.
thought: Pulled off the road and ended up in a tea shop in 青田街 area. Old guy behind the counter, navy mandarin-collar shirt, reading glasses on the end of his nose. He's just opened a canister of 文山包種 and scooped some out, holding it up to inspect in the morning light. Glass jars all up the wall — 凍頂烏龍, 鐵觀音, 東方美人. He hasn't said anything to me yet.
thought_zh: 離開馬路就到一間在青田街那一帶的茶行。老先生在櫃台後面，深藍色立領衫，老花眼鏡架在鼻尖。他剛剛打開一罐文山包種，舀了一點出來，舉起來在晨光下看。整面牆都是玻璃罐——凍頂烏龍、鐵觀音、東方美人。他到現在還沒跟我說過半句話。
thought_ja: 通りから離れたら、青田街あたりのお茶屋さんに着いてた。年配のおじさんがカウンターの内側、紺の立て襟の上着、老眼鏡を鼻の先に。文山包種の缶をいま開けて、ちょっと掬って、朝の光に当てて見てる。壁いっぱいガラス瓶——凍頂烏龍、鐵觀音、東方美人。おじさん、ここまで俺に一言も声かけてない。

prompt: interior of a busy Taipei traditional 早市 (morning wet market) in full rush, first-person eye-level moving slowly down the narrow central aisle. dense crowded stalls on both sides packed high with fresh produce: piles of bright green water spinach, mountains of pak choi (small bok choy), glossy purple eggplants, red tomatoes, bunches of long beans, white scallions tied with twine, mounds of garlic and ginger. shoppers crowd the aisle — mostly older Taiwanese aunties in cotton flowered blouses and sandals, a couple of uncles in t-shirts, one mother in her thirties pushing through with a small child in tow — several carrying bright pink reusable shopping bags or red plastic woven baskets. one vendor stage-right (older auntie with a pink hairband, faded t-shirt, stained apron) is shouting prices over the din with both hands raised: '一把三十！一把三十！'. through gaps between stalls glimpses of: a butcher hanging fresh pork bellies and ribs on heavy steel hooks, a fishmonger in rubber boots spraying an ice tray of mackerel and silver fish with fresh seawater, a roast-meat stall with chopped soy-sauce chickens and roast ducks piled glistening. fluorescent overhead tubes mixed with shafts of warm morning sun coming through gaps in the corrugated tin roof above. wet stained tile floor strewn with bits of cabbage leaves and rivulets of water. ambient sound: the constant overlapping chatter of dozens of voices in Hokkien and Mandarin, the auntie's shouted price calls, the rhythmic chop of a butcher's cleaver on wood block, water spraying onto fish, plastic bags rustling, scales tipping, no music — pure dense market ambient. 35mm film stock, slightly grainy, naturalistic mixed warm-cool lighting.
thought: Yes — markets. 早市. People everywhere, can barely walk. The vegetable auntie in front of me is shouting 「一把三十！一把三十！」at the top of her lungs with both hands up. Bok choy, eggplants, scallions piled high. There's a butcher hanging pork bellies behind one stall, a fishmonger spraying down his mackerel on the other side. Smells like fish water and produce.
thought_zh: 好——市場。早市。人滿到都快走不動。前面那個賣菜的阿姨兩手舉起來在那邊大喊「一把三十！一把三十！」。青江菜、茄子、蔥堆得超高。一個攤位後面有肉販在掛三層肉，另一邊魚販在用水沖他那盤鯖魚。聞起來是魚水跟蔬菜的味道。
thought_ja: よし——市場。早市(朝市)。人だらけで歩くのも大変。目の前の野菜のおばちゃん、両手挙げて思いっきり「一把三十！一把三十！(ひと束30元！)」って怒鳴ってる。チンゲン菜、ナス、ネギが山盛り。屋台のひとつの裏でお肉屋さんが豚バラを吊るしてて、反対側で魚屋さんがサバに水を吹きかけてる。魚の水と野菜のにおいだ。

prompt: first-person view at fish-eye level from the perspective of a single silver mackerel lying on the crushed-ice display of a Taipei wet-market fish stall, the camera angle very low (lying on the ice) and looking sharply upward with a wide-angle, slightly fisheye distortion. directly above and dominating the upper frame: the looming face of the fishmonger — a Taiwanese man in his fifties in a navy water-spotted rubber apron, white t-shirt, a faded blue baseball cap, weathered hands — bent down looking directly at the camera, one hand holding a small thin filleting knife, the other gesturing at the speaker. behind him: the corrugated metal roof of the wet market with a bright shaft of morning sun coming through one gap, and bare bulb fluorescent fixtures. in the immediate peripheral foreground: other silver mackerel laid out beside the speaker on the wet crushed ice, glistening, eyes still bright; a stainless steel bowl of larger fish heads beyond, a blue plastic ice bucket on the edge. shallow ice-melt water glistens. partially in frame on one side: a customer's hand pointing down (a wrinkled woman's hand with a thin gold bracelet). ambient sound: the dense overlapping market chatter all around (Hokkien and Mandarin), running water spraying nearby ice, the slap of a fish being moved to a wooden cutting board, the chop of a cleaver, a customer above asking in Mandarin '這條多少？', the fishmonger answering in Hokkien-accented Mandarin '兩百五就好！', no music. 35mm film stock, slightly grainy, low fish-eye angle, naturalistic mixed fluorescent and morning sun.
thought: Let me be one of the fish — fisheye literally. Okay, lying on the ice, looking straight up. The fishmonger's face is huge above me — baseball cap, knife in his hand. These guys around me look more like 鰹魚 actually, not mackerel. Customer's hand pointing in at the edge of frame asking '這條多少？'. He goes '兩百五就好！'. Am I the 兩百五 one?
thought_zh: 我要當一條魚看看——魚眼是字面意思的魚眼。OK，躺在冰上面，直直往上看。魚販的臉超大就在我上面——棒球帽，手上一把刀。我旁邊這些其實看起來更像鰹魚，不是鯖魚。畫面邊緣有客人的手指進來，在問「這條多少？」他說「兩百五就好！」我是那條兩百五嗎？
thought_ja: 魚になってみよう——魚眼ってのは、文字どおり魚の目線。よし、氷の上に寝そべって、まっすぐ上を見上げてる。魚屋さんの顔がでっかく俺の上にある——野球帽、手にナイフ。横に並んでるこいつら、サバっていうよりよく見たら鰹魚(カツオ)だな。画面の端から客の手が入ってきて「這條多少？(これいくら？)」って聞いてて、おじさん「兩百五就好！(250でええ！)」って答えてる。俺がその二百五十のやつなのか？

prompt: first-person eye-level view stepping out of the back exit of a Taipei traditional 早市 (morning market) into a quiet narrow morning side-alley, the dense market sound suddenly muffled behind. directly ahead: a sunlit narrow alley with bright morning sun streaking diagonally across the wet pavement, an old white-and-blue tile-fronted four-story residential building on the right with several open windows above, a couple of motor scooters parked at angles, a short worn concrete bench under a large banyan tree (榕樹) overhanging from an inner courtyard. on the bench sit two old Taiwanese uncles in their seventies — both in plain short-sleeved button-down shirts, dark trousers, and slip-on sandals — drinking from old-style brown glass bottles of 米漿 (Taiwanese rice milk), an open red plastic crate of empty soy milk and 米漿 bottles next to their feet. a small grey-and-white alley cat is curled up sleeping at one uncle's feet. behind the speaker (visible only as the dark archway behind, partial frame), the bright loud market interior is faintly visible deep in shadow contrast — silhouettes of moving shoppers and stalls. dappled banyan leaf-shadow on the alley pavement. ambient sound: the muffled overall hum of the market behind, morning birds, one of the uncles softly murmuring something in Hokkien to the other, a single distant scooter, light wind moving the banyan leaves, no music. 35mm film stock, slightly grainy, naturalistic sun-and-shadow morning Taipei colour.
thought: Stepped out a side exit and the market's volume just dropped to almost nothing. Quiet alley, sun coming in diagonally. Two uncles on a bench under a 榕樹 drinking 米漿 out of those old brown glass bottles, an empty crate by their feet, a grey-and-white cat sleeping on one of their shoes. One of them just murmured something in Hokkien I didn't catch. I'd kind of like to sit down too.
thought_zh: 從一個側門走出來，整個市場的音量瞬間降到幾乎沒聲音。安靜的小巷，太陽斜斜地進來。兩個阿伯坐在一棵榕樹下的板凳上，在喝那種以前的褐色玻璃瓶米漿，腳邊一個空箱子，一隻灰白色的貓睡在其中一個阿伯的鞋子上。其中一個剛剛低聲講了一句台語，我沒聽到。我也有點想坐下來。
thought_ja: 横の出口から出たら、市場の音量がいきなりほぼゼロになった。静かな路地、日が斜めに差してる。榕樹の下のベンチに、おじさん二人、あの古い茶色いガラス瓶の米漿(ライスミルク)を飲んでて、足元に空のケース、片方のおじさんの靴の上で灰色と白の猫が寝てる。一人がさっき台湾語で何かぼそっと言ったけど、聞き取れなかった。俺もちょっと座りたい。

prompt: interior view of a tiny Taipei 早餐店 (Taiwanese breakfast stall) from the customer's seat at the counter, mid-morning. directly in front of the speaker: a stainless-steel plastic-laminate counter with a single small white melamine plate holding a freshly-cooked 蛋餅 (Taiwanese egg-and-flour crepe roll) cut into 4-5 bite-sized sections, glistening with a drizzle of dark soy paste and a small streak of red chilli sauce, with a tiny side dish of pickled yellow radish (黃蘿蔔). next to the plate: a tall thick clear plastic cup of warm 米漿 (rice milk) — the brand label '奇美米漿' or generic — condensation just starting on the outside, and one yellow plastic spoon. partially visible at the front edge of frame: the speaker's own hands resting flat on the counter palms down, slightly relaxed. behind the counter: the auntie's grill area — wide stainless flat-top with another 蛋餅 cooking, an open squeeze-bottle of soy paste, chopped scallions in a metal bowl, eggs in a tray, a hot insulated urn of soy milk visibly steaming from a small spout. the auntie herself partially visible in the back, hairnet and faded blue apron, working a spatula. dappled morning sun coming through the open shopfront on the left side casting warm bars across the counter. a small folded-paper handwritten menu pinned on the back tile wall. ambient sound: the soft sizzle of the 蛋餅 cooking, the soy milk urn faintly burbling, the auntie's quiet humming, distant traffic past the shopfront, faint Hokkien morning talk-radio from a tiny speaker high on the back wall, the small clink of the speaker's plastic spoon being picked up, no music in the foreground. 35mm film stock, slightly grainy, warm soft morning interior light.
thought: OK, 今天就先到這吧。 Sat down at a tiny 早餐店, finally got food in front of me — 蛋餅 cut up, a little pickled radish, big cup of 米漿. Auntie still on the grill. Sun's full out now. I'm going to eat this and then I'm done.
thought_zh: OK，今天就先到這吧。坐進一間小小的早餐店，終於有東西吃了——蛋餅切好，一小盤黃蘿蔔，一大杯米漿。阿姨還在鐵板那邊。太陽完全出來了。我吃完這個就收。
thought_ja: よし、今日はここまでにしとくか。ちっちゃい早餐店に座って、やっとちゃんと目の前に食べ物が出てきた——蛋餅は切ってあって、たくあんがちょっと、米漿のでっかいカップ。おばちゃんはまだ鉄板の前。陽はもうすっかり出てる。これ食べたら、終わりにする。

prompt: a narrow back alley in Tokyo at night, three vending machines stacked side by side along a peeling concrete wall, glowing cool blue, warm red, and pale green, casting their colors onto wet asphalt that holds a shallow puddle reflecting them, a low concrete wall on the far side with stenciled black apartment numbers and a single rust-stained drainpipe, an air-conditioner condenser unit on a small steel bracket above the machines, a folded blue tarp tied to a railing, summer humidity and a faint haze in the air, no people, distant low rumble of a JR train passing on an elevated line just out of frame, undertone of cicadas, 35mm film stock with soft natural grain, slight halation around the brightest vending machine fronts, slightly warm tungsten on a small alley sign, cooler LED on the puddle, a small kanji 自販機 sticker visible on one of the machines
thought: Okay — vending machines, narrow alley, looks like Tokyo. Three of them lit up, blue and red and green, throwing color on the wet asphalt. There's a train somewhere overhead, just a low rumble. Smells like rain that already happened. I want one of those canned coffees. Let me see if any of these takes coins.
thought_zh: OK——販賣機，窄巷，看起來像東京。三台亮著，藍的紅的綠的，把顏色撒在濕掉的柏油上。頭上某處有一班電車，只是低低的隆隆聲。聞得到剛才下過雨的味道。我想喝一罐那裡面的咖啡。讓我看看哪一台吃硬幣。
thought_ja: おっけー——自販機、狭い路地、東京っぽいな。三台ぜんぶ点いてて、青、赤、緑、色が濡れたアスファルトに落ちてる。頭の上のどっかで電車、低い唸りが聞こえるだけ。さっき雨が降ったあとのにおいがする。あの缶コーヒーが一本欲しい。どれが小銭使えるか見てみよう。

prompt: the camera drifts forward in a Tokyo back alley at night with very slow handheld movement, approaching three side-by-side vending machines glowing red, white-and-red, and pale green against a peeling concrete wall, the wet asphalt holding shifting colored reflections in a shallow puddle, the blue tarp tied to a railing on the right shifts gently once in a faint draft of warm humid air, the small kanji '1284' stencil on the concrete wall on the left passes near the camera, a faint paper-lantern glow visible far up the alley does not change, the row of cans behind the front machine's glass becoming faintly resolvable, a few red labels reading あったか〜い, the small heater bar glowing faint orange under the bottom row of cans, no people, no human figures, no characters in frame, the camera does not stop, sound: distant low rumble of an elevated JR train passing once on a viaduct just out of frame, a single faint coin clink somewhere ahead, summer cicadas thin and high underneath, no music, no voices, 35mm film stock soft natural grain, slight halation around the brightest vending machine fronts, slightly warm tungsten elsewhere
thought: Closer now. Wet asphalt's holding the colors really well — that shallow puddle is doing all the work. The middle one's the warmer red, that's probably where the hot cans are. I want that あったかい coffee. Let me get right up to the slot.
thought_zh: 近一點了。濕柏油把那些顏色顯得超好——那一灘小水窪是這幅畫的主角。中間那台是比較暖的紅色，應該是放熱罐的那個。我想要那個あったかい咖啡。讓我直接走到投幣口那邊。
thought_ja: もうちょい近づいた。濡れたアスファルトが色をめっちゃきれいに反射してて——あの浅い水たまりがいちばん仕事してる。真ん中のやつがあったかい赤、たぶんあったかい缶のやつだろう。あのあったかいコーヒーが欲しい。投入口のとこまで行ってみよう。

prompt: view from inside a Japanese back-alley vending machine, looking outward through the slightly smudged front glass, the camera at the height of one of the canned drinks on a middle shelf, the angle low and slightly tilted, the foreground edges of frame softly out of focus showing rows of colorful canned drinks on slanted dispensers — pinks, oranges, blues, yellows, label outlines blurred — and the cool overhead bulb of the machine's interior throwing a faint daylight-white glow on the back of the cans, while through the glass the alley outside is dim and humid, wet asphalt with shifting puddle reflections, the warmer red glow of the adjacent vending machine spilling in from the upper-left edge of frame, the dark concrete wall opposite with stenciled apartment numbers, an air-conditioner condenser bracket visible far in the upper-right, a faint paper-lantern glow much farther back at the end of the alley, no people in the alley, the glass itself catching faint horizontal smudges and a few water droplets from earlier rain, slight reflection of the can-row interior overlaid onto the alley view, depth-of-field tight on the glass with the alley sharper than the cans, the small embossed 350ml on a foreground can faintly visible, sound: muffled distant JR train rumble dampened by glass, the low electrical hum of the machine's compressor close and immediate, a faint coin-mechanism click from somewhere in the machine itself, summer cicadas barely audible through the glass, no music, 35mm film stock soft natural grain, slightly cool interior fluorescent against warm exterior tungsten, gentle halation around the bright glass edge
thought: Tried to climb inside one of these cans and instead I'm just nose-to-glass with the whole row. They're all branded 'Kiss' in this kind of late-90s lettering — never seen that brand, pink and peach and blue and yellow, like fake-fruit sodas. The compressor's humming right through the glass. Bit of the alley still red back there over my shoulder. Okay, I'll just stay outside, this is fine.
thought_zh: 想要鑽進其中一罐裡面，結果只是整張臉貼在玻璃上跟整排罐子鼻子對鼻子。它們都是 'Kiss' 牌的，那種有點 90 年代末風格的字體——沒看過這牌子，粉紅、桃色、藍色、黃色，看起來像假水果汽水。壓縮機的嗡嗡聲穿過玻璃直接傳過來。我肩膀後面還能看到一點巷子的紅光。OK，我就乖乖待在外面，沒事。
thought_ja: 缶のなかに入ってみようとして、結局ガラスに鼻押しつけて、ずらっと並んだ缶と顔つき合わせてるだけになった。ぜんぶ「Kiss」ってブランドで、なんか90年代後半っぽいフォント——聞いたことないブランド、ピンク、ピーチ、青、黄色、なんか嘘くさい果実サワーみたいなの。コンプレッサーの音がガラス越しにダイレクトに来てる。肩のうしろにまだ路地の赤い光が残ってる。オッケー、外にいるよ、これでいい。

prompt: at the very end of a dark narrow Tokyo back alley at night, a single red paper lantern (akachochin) hangs from a black iron arm over a tiny izakaya entrance, the kanji 「焼鳥」 painted in thick black brushstrokes on the lantern's white belt, warm interior light spilling out from behind a navy-blue noren curtain hanging over the doorway with white kanji along its bottom hem, the curtain parted faintly so a slice of warm wood interior is visible — the edge of an L-shaped wooden counter, the back of one salaryman's white shirt and dark suit jacket on a wooden stool, a glimpse of a small charcoal grill with skewers, a wisp of grey smoke escaping out the top of the noren and curling up around the lantern, three small grey moths circling the lantern in lazy figure-eights, the wet asphalt below catching a soft warm puddle of red-orange lantern light against the cooler darker alley behind, a small hand-lettered wooden sign on the wall reading 「営業中」, faint smudge of cigarette ash on a low concrete sill, a wall-mounted gas meter with rust streaks just to the right of the doorway, no other people in the alley, summer humidity in the air with a thin haze, 35mm film stock soft natural grain, warm tungsten light dominant, slight halation around the lantern glow, slight reflection of the lantern in a small puddle, sound: low charcoal-grill sizzle and tare-glaze hiss audible faintly through the noren, a faint old enka song on a small radio inside the shop, distant elevated JR rumble and one quiet motorcycle passing far behind, summer cicadas thin and high above, no voices, no music in foreground
thought: Okay, walked all the way down to the end of the alley and that glow I saw before is a red paper lantern, 焼鳥 written on it. Tiny yakitori place. The noren's open enough that I can see one guy in a suit at the counter with his back to me, smoke coming up from the grill. Smells like soy and fat already. Two or three moths doing slow loops around the lantern. I want to push through this curtain.
thought_zh: OK，走到巷子最底，剛才看到的那團光是一盞紅色提燈，上面寫著「焼鳥」。一間小小的烤雞店。暖簾開得夠多，我看得到一個穿西裝的人坐在吧台背對我，烤架上方煙在飄。已經聞得到醬油跟油脂味了。兩三隻蛾繞著燈在做緩慢的繞圈。我想穿過這塊布進去。
thought_ja: オッケー、路地のいちばん奥まで歩いてきたら、さっき見えたあの光は赤い提灯で、「焼鳥」って書いてある。ちっちゃい焼鳥屋。暖簾がちょっとだけ開いてて、スーツのおっさんがカウンターに背中向けて座ってるのが見える、グリルから煙が上がってる。もう醤油と脂のにおいがしてる。蛾が二、三匹、提灯のまわりをゆっくり八の字で回ってる。この暖簾、くぐってみたい。

ねぎま, 皮 — and on a wooden shelf above: tall sake bottles with paper labels, a small old transistor radio with a single round dial playing a tinny enka song very faintly, a yellowed ceiling fan above with one bent blade barely turning, a small printed calendar from a sake brewery pinned crookedly with a 4 月 page showing, on the immediate left edge of frame the back of one salaryman in a white shirt sleeves rolled up at his stool, a half-empty pint glass of pale lager beaded with condensation in front of him with a small bowl of edamame and a tall cup full of stripped used bamboo skewers, the counter in front of the camera holds a small empty cedar saucer with a single uneaten wedge of yuzu and a folded ozhibori still rolled up, no people facing the camera, the smoke pooling up at the ceiling, soft warm tungsten light, sound: the steady soft sizzle and occasional sharp pop of fat hitting binchotan, the small clink of a skewer being laid down on a stainless rack, the chef's quiet breath, the radio's faint enka in the background, the salaryman setting his glass down once, a low murmur of charcoal, no music in the foreground, no voices, 35mm film stock soft natural grain, warm tungsten dominant, gentle haze of smoke softening the back of the room
thought: Okay, I'm in. Stool at the corner of the counter, the salaryman from outside is on my left already mostly through his beer. The chef hasn't looked up — he's painting tare on a row of negima with this long brush, whole wall of menu tags behind him in black ink, つくね レバー ぼんじり, all the standard stuff. Smoke's thick up by the ceiling. There's an unused oshibori in front of me already, like he knew I was coming. I haven't ordered yet. I should figure out what I want.
thought_zh: OK，進來了。坐在吧台轉角的椅子上，外面那位上班族在我左邊，啤酒已經快喝完。師傅還沒抬頭——他在用一支長刷子幫一排ねぎま塗醬油，整面後牆都是黑墨寫的菜牌：つくね、レバー、ぼんじり，標準的那一套。煙在天花板那邊已經悶著一層了。我面前已經有一條沒拆封的おしぼり擺在那，好像他知道我會來。我還沒點。我得想一下要吃什麼。
thought_ja: オッケー、入った。カウンターの角の席に座って、外にいたサラリーマンは俺の左でビールほぼ飲み終わってる。大将はまだ顔上げてない——長い刷毛で一列のねぎまにタレ塗ってる、後ろの壁ぜんぶ黒墨で書いた札：つくね、レバー、ぼんじり、定番ぜんぶ。煙が天井のあたりにこもってる。前にもう、開けてないおしぼりが置いてある、まるで俺が来るの分かってたみたいに。まだ注文してない。何にするか決めないと。

prompt: extreme close-up on a low charcoal grill in a Tokyo yakitori shop, six bamboo skewers of negima yakitori laid in a neat row across glowing white-hot binchotan, the camera handheld and very still at counter level just above the grill, the binchotan glowing softly with shifting orange and white-hot patches breathing slightly, thin steady curls of grey-blue smoke rising in soft layers, droplets of golden chicken fat beading on the surface of the meat and occasionally falling onto the coals where one drop produces a single quick small orange flare and a sharp sizzle pop, the tare glaze on the skewers glistening dark amber and slowly bubbling at the edges, a calm tanned hand enters from upper-right holding a long bamboo brush dipped in dark tare and slowly paints a single broad stroke across one skewer once, then withdraws, the focus stays tight on the grill the entire time, the yellow ceiling-warmth softening at the top of frame, no people visible except the brushing hand, no camera movement other than tiny handheld breath, no zoom, no cuts, sound: dominant steady soft sizzle of fat on hot charcoal, the wet hissing pop of one fat drop hitting coals halfway through with a brief louder flare, the gentle creak of binchotan settling, very faint distant enka song from the radio in the background, faint clink of a beer glass somewhere off-frame to the left being set down, no music in foreground, no voices, 35mm film stock soft natural grain, warm tungsten light dominant, slight halation around the brightest coal patches
thought: Just watching this for a sec. Six skewers across the binchotan, the coals are doing this slow breathing thing where the bright patches keep shifting around, and the fat is just slowly beading up and dripping. He paints another stroke of tare. One drop hits the coals and there's that little flare, that pop you can feel in your jaw. I haven't even ordered and I'm already happy.
thought_zh: 就這樣看一下。六串排在備長炭上，炭在做那種慢慢呼吸的事——亮的部分一直在小範圍移動——油脂慢慢在肉的表面結成珠在滴。他又刷了一筆醬油。一滴落到炭上有那個小小的火焰跳出來，那種你下巴可以感覺到的爆音。我都還沒點，就已經很開心了。
thought_ja: ちょっとそのまま見てる。六本のくしが備長炭の上に並んでて、炭がゆっくり呼吸してるみたいに、明るいパッチがちょっとずつ動いてる、脂が肉の表面にじわっと玉になって落ちてく。大将がまたタレを一刷毛、塗った。一滴炭に落ちて、あのちっちゃいフレアと、顎で感じるパチッてやつ。まだ注文すらしてないのに、もう機嫌いい。

Mt Fuji mural across the whole back wall, classic Showa style — they even painted little figures into the lake, one of them like swimming. thought_ja: 降りてきた。小さな古い銭湯、午前の遅め、基本だれもいない。後ろの壁いっぱいに富士山のタイル絵、ザ・昭和——湖のなかにちっちゃい人物まで描いてあって、一人は泳いでるポーズしてる。真ん中に湯船がひとつ、お爺さんがその縁に背中向けて座ってて、ハゲ頭にきっちり折ったてぬぐい載せてる。右側の洗い場、ぜんぶ鏡と腰掛けが空で並んでる。湯気が左の高い窓のあたりにたまってて、あの長い光の帯が降りてきてる。時計が十時十分くらいに見える。すごい静か、お湯がぱしゃっと跳ねる音だけ。

thought: Came out of the bookshop and walked basically straight into the loudest place in Tokyo. Pachinko parlor, full lunch crowd. Two endless walls of machines, neon of every color, the whole place a tunnel of LEDs and animations. Old guy on the left mid-aisle leaning into his machine, hand resting on a tub of steel balls he's already won. Smoke up by the ceiling. The ball-roar is wild — thousands of them cascading at once, you can't actually hear yourself think in here. Attendant in a red vest pushing a cart of more balls down the aisle. Somebody three machines down just hit a fever, you can hear the jingle. Total opposite of where I just was.
thought_zh: 從書店出來直接走進整個東京最吵的地方。柏青哥店，午餐時段全滿。兩面望不到底的機台，每個顏色都有的霓虹，整個空間是一條 LED 跟動畫的走廊。左邊中段一個老先生身體前傾貼在他的機台上，手上一個塑膠盒已經滿滿都是他贏到的鋼珠。煙在天花板那邊。鋼珠的轟轟聲超猛——好幾千顆同時在掉，根本聽不到自己在想什麼。穿紅背心的小姐在推一台補珠車走過走道。三台機台之外有人剛剛中了 fever，那個祝賀音樂響了一下。跟我剛才在的地方完全相反的東西。
thought_ja: 古本屋から出てきたら、即、東京でいちばんうるさい場所に入ってた。パチンコ屋、ランチタイムでぎっしり。両側にどこまでも続くパチンコ台、ありとあらゆる色のネオン、空間ぜんぶ LED とアニメーションのトンネル。左の中ほどでお爺さんが台に身を乗り出して、横のプラケースにもうじゃらじゃらに勝ち取った銀玉を入れてる。煙が天井のあたりにたまってる。玉のゴーって音、まじで凄い——何千個も同時に落ちてて、自分の頭のなかも聞こえないレベル。赤いベストのスタッフさんが補給玉のカートを押して通路を進んでる。三台向こうで誰かいまフィーバー引いて、あのジングルが鳴った。さっきまでいた場所のどこまでも反対側だな。

thought: Walked into the next thing and it's the total flip — a small public elementary schoolyard in the middle of class hours, just empty. One old guy in a navy jumpsuit and a white cap slowly sweeping the dirt with a bamboo broom. He's gathering a pile of cherry petals at his feet. Cherry tree on the right still showering petals down even though there's no wind. Empty swings, jungle gym, a forgotten orange volleyball lying on its side. From the open windows of the school I can hear a kid's choir practicing 'furusato' kind of off-key, and the bell just rang once. Sparrow on the back fence preening. Thirty seconds ago I was in a pachinko parlor.
thought_zh: 走進下一個場景，整個又翻了過去——一個小小的公立小學操場，正課時間，沒人。一個老先生穿藏青色的工作服跟白帽子，在用一支竹掃把慢慢掃地。腳邊集了一小堆櫻花瓣。右邊那棵櫻花樹儘管沒風還是在繼續落瓣。空盪盪的鞦韆、攀爬架、一顆被遺忘的橘色排球側躺在那邊。教室開著的窗戶飄出來小朋友合唱練「ふるさと」，調有點走，剛剛還響了一下鐘。後面圍欄上一隻麻雀在理毛。三十秒前我還在柏青哥店裡。
thought_ja: 次のとこに入ったら、ぜんぶひっくり返った——小学校の校庭、授業中、誰もいない。お爺さんが紺色のジャンプスーツに白いキャップで、竹箒でゆっくり地面を掃いてる。足元に桜の花びらの小山。右の桜の木は風がないのにずっと花びらを落とし続けてる。空のブランコ、ジャングルジム、忘れられたオレンジのバレーボールが横に転がってる。校舎の開いた窓から子供たちの合唱が聞こえてくる、「ふるさと」、ちょっと音外してる、いまチャイムが一回鳴った。後ろのフェンスの上でスズメが羽繕いしてる。30 秒前まで俺パチンコ屋にいたんだぞ。

thought: Came down off the roof and ended up in a tachi-nomi tucked under the JR tracks — that kind of place, narrow as a hallway, no chairs, just standing room. 4:10pm. Two older salarymen already in — one's halfway through a Sapporo, leaning over the Tokyo Sports paper, foam in his moustache he hasn't bothered to wipe. Master behind the bar in a black knit cap, slicing pickled daikon. There's a small bowl of nikomi in front of where I'm standing, three pieces in dark broth, scallions on top. The whole shop just rumbles every few minutes when a train rolls overhead. NHK baseball on mute up in the corner. This is the right kind of bar for this hour.
thought_zh: 從屋頂下來，結果進到 JR 高架下面塞著的一間立飲店——那種地方，窄得跟走廊一樣，沒椅子，全部站著。下午 4:10。兩個年紀大一點的上班族已經在裡面——一個 Sapporo 喝到一半，趴在 Tokyo Sports 報紙上，鬍子上還沾著啤酒泡沫他根本沒擦。老闆在吧台後面，黑色針織帽，正在切醃蘿蔔。我面前已經有一小碗もつ煮，深色的湯底裡三塊牛筋，上面撒了蔥。整間店每幾分鐘就在電車從上面開過的時候震一下。NHK 棒球轉播在角落靜音放著。這個時段就是要這種酒吧。
thought_ja: 屋根から下りたら、JR の高架の下にひっそり挟まれてる立ち飲み屋に入ってた——あのタイプ、廊下みたいに細くて、椅子なし、全員立ち。午後 4:10。年配のサラリーマンが二人もう入ってる——一人はサッポロを半分くらい飲み終わって、東京スポーツの紙面に肘ついて、口ひげにビールの泡ついてるけど拭く気なし。マスターはカウンターの内側で、黒いニット帽で、ぬか漬けの大根切ってる。俺の前にもうもつ煮の小鉢が置いてある、濃い汁にすじ三切れ、ねぎがのってる。電車が上を通るたびに数分おきに店ぜんたいがズンって揺れる。NHK の野球がミュートで隅で映ってる。この時間にはこういうバーがいい。

young couple seated on another bench far down looking at the water, the sky a soft warm peach-orange near the horizon transitioning to a paler blue overhead with a few thin warm clouds and a single contrail catching pink light, sound: the soft constant lapping of the river water against the stone bank, the gentle creak of the cherry trunks in the warm breeze, the slow distant churning of the thought: Walked out of the tachi-nomi and ended up at the Sumida river bank around dinnertime, sun's full golden-hour. Old guy on a bench in a fisherman cap with his line out over the water, white bait bucket at his feet, completely still. The cherry trees along the bank are still shedding — there's a long pink petal-slick drifting downstream. Little blue-and-white river bus crawling upstream cutting through it. Big green truss bridge in the middle distance. Skytree way back there in the haze, just its tip catching the light. Apartment windows on the far bank all glowing orange. The tachi-nomi trip energy is wearing off, kind of just standing here.
thought_zh: 從立飲店走出來，到了隅田川堤岸，差不多晚餐時間，太陽已經完全是黃金時分。一個老先生戴漁夫帽坐在長椅上，釣竿伸出去到水面上，腳邊一個白色魚餌桶，整個人完全沒動。岸邊那排櫻花樹還在落花瓣——一條長長的粉紅色花瓣帶在順流而下。一艘藍白小型水上巴士在逆流而上慢慢割開那條花瓣帶。中距離一座綠色桁架橋。晴空塔在遠遠的霧裡，只有頂尖剛好吃到光。對岸的公寓窗戶整片橘色發光。立飲那杯啤酒的勁過去了，我就站在這邊。
thought_ja: 立ち飲みから出てきたら、隅田川の岸に着いてた、夕飯どきくらいで、太陽がもう完全にゴールデンアワー。お爺さんが一人、漁師帽でベンチに座って、釣り竿を水のほうに出してて、足元に白い餌バケツ、まったく動いてない。岸の桜並木はまだ花びらを落とし続けてる——長いピンクの帯になって下流に流れてる。青と白の小さな水上バスが上流に向かって、その帯をゆっくり切り進んでる。中距離に緑のトラス橋。ずっと先のほうにスカイツリーがもや越しに、てっぺんだけ光を受けてる。対岸のマンションの西向きの窓ぜんぶがオレンジに光ってる。立ち飲みの勢いが切れて、いまただ立ってる。
